'''Jason Derek Holt''' (born 19 February 1993) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a midfielder for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

Holt has also previously played for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], the latter two while on loan from [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. He represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]], [[Scotland national under-20 football team|under-20]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] level.

==Club career==

===Heart of Midlothian===
Holt grew up in [[Musselburgh]] as a Hearts fan and attended [[Musselburgh Grammar School]] before signing for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20111209/a-word-with_2241384_2542713 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120801070612/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20111209/a-word-with_2241384_2542713 |url-status=dead |archive-date=1 August 2012 |title=A word with... Jason Holt |publisher=heartsfc.co.uk |work=Heart of Midlothian F.C. |date=9 December 2011 |access-date=19 December 2011 }}</ref> He was a member of the Hearts under-19 squad who finished second behind [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in the under-19 league in 2010–11.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20110504/jason-vows-to-build-on-award_2241384_2352478 |title=Jason vows to build on award |publisher=Heart of Midlothian Football Club |work=heartsfc.co.uk |date=4 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110509012927/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20110504/jason-vows-to-build-on-award_2241384_2352478 |archive-date= 9 May 2011 }}</ref> He picked up the Clydesdale Bank Premier League under-19 player of the season award.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cbfootball.co.uk/seasonAwards1011.aspx | title=Under 19 Player of the season 2010–11 | access-date=15 May 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110507123015/http://www.cbfootball.co.uk/seasonawards1011.aspx | archive-date=7 May 2011 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Despite being part of the squad that travelled to Italy for pre season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20100709/squad-for-italy-revealed_2241384_2086990 |title=Hearts Squad Travelling to Italy for Pre season |access-date=15 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100714055308/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20100709/squad-for-italy-revealed_2241384_2086990 |archive-date=14 July 2010 }}</ref> Holt had to wait until the last day of the 2010–11 season to make his First team debut on 15 May 2011 as a substitute against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9484607.stm | title=Dundee United v Hearts  |publisher=BBC Sport| date=15 May 2011}}</ref> His performance for the under 19 squad in the early part of the 2011–12 season earned him a new three-year contract extending his stay with the club until 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20111118/hat-trick-of-new-deals_2241384_2520400 |title=Hat-trick of new deals |publisher=Heart of Midlothian Football Club |date=18 November 2011 |work=heartsfc.co.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111120053436/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20111118/hat-trick-of-new-deals_2241384_2520400 |archive-date=20 November 2011 }}</ref> He scored on his first start for Hearts, away to St Johnstone in March 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/newsitemsdetail.php?param=1974|title=St Johnstone Football Club – News Archive|website=perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk|access-date=2016-01-04}}{{dead link|date=December 2017|bot=Nzd|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>

With Hearts in financial difficulty and wanting to bring through members of their under 19 squad into the first team,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/edinburgh-evening-news/other-sport/hearts_start_fast_tracking_youth_players_to_first_team_1_1977338 | title=Hearts start fast-tracking youth players to first team | work=Evening News |publisher=Johnston Press|location=Edinburgh  | date=21 November 2011 | access-date=21 November 2011}}</ref> Holt was sent on loan to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] to gain first team experience.<ref name="Hearts_Trio">{{cite web|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20111121/trio-off-on-loan_2241384_2523171 |title=Trio off on loan |publisher=Heart of Midlothian Football Club |work=heartsfc.co.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101212143/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20111121/trio-off-on-loan_2241384_2523171 |archive-date= 1 November 2013 }}</ref>

====Loan spells====
On 21 November 2011, after impressing in a bounce game, Holt joined [[Scottish First Division]] side [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on loan until 5 January 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raithroversfc.com/cgi-bin/latestnews.cgi?id=3918 |title=Loan Signings Confirmed |publisher=[[Raith Rovers F.C.]] |date=26 November 2011 |access-date=26 November 2011 }}{{dead link|date=April 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Making his debut on 26 November 2011 scoring the first goal in the ninth minute in their 3–2 win against [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/football/first/results/3408200/ |title=Raith Rovers 3 – 2 Hamilton Academical |publisher=SFL |date=26 November 2011 |access-date=26 November 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525131654/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/football/first/results/3408200/ |archive-date=25 May 2012 }}</ref> In all Holt made five appearances for the side with his last appearance coming as a substitute on 2 January against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16375052 | title=Raith Rovers 0–1 Dundee | publisher=BBC Sport | date=2 January 2012 | access-date=5 January 2012}}</ref> On 5 January he returned to Hearts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raithroversfc.com/cgi-bin/latestnews.cgi?id=3981 |title=Hearts Pair Loan Deals Extended |publisher=Raith Rovers FC |date=5 January 2012 |access-date=5 January 2012 }}{{dead link|date=April 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Holt moved on loan to Sheffield United on 30 January 2015 for the rest of the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jason Holt: Sheffield United sign Hearts midfielder on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31067332|access-date=1 February 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=30 January 2015}}</ref>

===Rangers===
On 22 July 2015, Holt signed a three-year deal with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] after impressing on a trial spell.<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33616730| title=Rangers sign ex-Hearts player on three-year deal| publisher=BBC Sport| date=22 July 2015 }}</ref> The Ibrox side agreed a development compensation fee of £65,000 with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/jason-holt-sign-rangers-within-6111614| title=Jason Holt to sign for Rangers within next 24 hours after shining as a trialist against Burnley |work=Daily Record |location=Glasgow  | first=David|last=McCarthy| date=22 July 2015 }}</ref> Holt scored his first goal for Rangers in a 5–1 win over [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33616730 |title=Jason Holt: Rangers sign ex-Hearts player on three-year deal |publisher=BBC Sport  |date=22 July 2015  }}</ref> He scored a brace against title rivals [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in a 4–2 win for Rangers.<ref>{{Cite news|title =Rangers 4-2 Hibernian | first=Nick |last=Thomson|url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/match-report/2015-16/rangers-4-2-hibernian/|publisher=Rangers Football Club|work=Rangers.co.uk |date= 28 December 2015}}</ref> Holt was named in the Championship team of the year for 2015–16,<ref name="barton">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44523857|title=Jason Holt: Fleetwood sign Rangers midfielder on loan|date=18 June 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=18 June 2018}}</ref> as Rangers won promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref name = "gers promoted"/>

Holt made 33 appearances and scored two goals for Rangers during the 2017–18 season,<ref name = "barton"/> but was made available for transfer by new manager [[Steven Gerrard]] in June 2018.

====Fleetwood Town (Loan)====
On 18 June 2018, Holt was loaned to [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]], managed by his former Rangers teammate [[Joey Barton]].<ref name="barton" /> Following an injury against [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] on 30 March 2019, Holt completed his loan and returned to Rangers. Holt played in 36 games in all competitions and scored two goals for Fleetwood.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/football/fleetwood-town-fc/fleetwood-town-loan-star-jason-holt-returns-to-rangers-as-injury-ends-season-early-1-9698301|title=Fleetwood Town loan star Jason Holt returns to Rangers as injury ends season early|website=Blackpool Gazette|date=8 April 2019 |access-date=2019-05-13}}</ref>

====St Johnstone (Loan)====
On 2 September 2019, Holt signed on loan for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] until the end of the [[2019–20 St Johnstone F.C. season|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Anthony Ralston & Jason Holt join St Johnstone on season-long loans|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49552348|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 September 2019|access-date=2 September 2019}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 11 August 2020, Holt signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Because one Holt wasn't enough...|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/because-one-holt-wasnt-enough/|date=11 August 2020|website=livingstonfc.co.uk}}</ref>

===St Johnstone return===
In August 2024, Holt signed for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] for a second spell.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jason Holt: Relegation with Livingston was horrible but I'm confident it won't be two in a row at St Johnstone|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/5072674/jason-holt-st-johnstone-livingston-relegation/|date=2 September 2024|publisher=The Courier}}</ref>

==International career==
Holt has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] level<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=462&playerID=67704&squadID=9|title=Jason Holt – U19 Squad|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]}}</ref> and [[Scotland national under-20 football team|under-20]] level and was called up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] squad in 2011, making his debut a year later.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/more-scottish-football/holt-steps-up-as-scots-target-vital-points-1.1127524 | title=Holt steps up as Scots target vital points | work=The Herald | location=Glasgow | date=5 October 2011 | access-date=7 November 2011 | archive-date=19 October 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111019065556/http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/more-scottish-football/holt-steps-up-as-scots-target-vital-points-1.1127524 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Craig Alexander Sibbald''' (born 18 May 1995) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. He has previously played for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], and represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] level. Sibbald won the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] with Falkirk during the 2011-12 season and the [[Scottish Championship]] in season 2023-24 with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

==Club career==
===Falkirk===
Sibbald made his first team debut for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] aged 16, in a 2–1 win against [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] in the [[2011–12 Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14244472 |title=Brechin City 1–2 Falkirk |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 July 2011 |accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> This was quickly followed by his first start in the league on 6 August against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14430791 |title=Raith Rovers 1–0 Falkirk |publisher=BBC Sport |date=6 August 2011 |accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref>

Sibbald signed a contract extension with Falkirk on 3 July 2014, which contracted him to the club until 2017.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28147322 |title=Falkirk: Jamie MacDonald one of five new arrivals |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 July 2014 |accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> He signed a new one-year contract with Falkirk on 11 August 2017, after an unsuccessful [[Trial (association football)|trial]] with [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/sibbald-signs-for-falkirk-1-4529756 |title=Sibbald signs for Falkirk |first=David |last=Oliver |newspaper=Falkirk Herald |date=11 August 2017 |accessdate=17 February 2018}}</ref>

===Livingston===
Sibbald signed for newly promoted [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on 30 May 2018 on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44309165 |title=Craig Sibbald joins Livingston on a two-year deal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 May 2018 |accessdate=30 May 2018}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
During July 2022 Sibbald joined [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sibbald joins Dundee United on two-year deal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cz94zv02vm4o |website=BBC Sport |date=11 July 2022 |access-date=12 July 2022}}</ref>

==International career==
Sibbald was [[Cap (sport)|capped]] three times for the [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scottish under-16 team]] from 2010 to 2011.<ref name=ScottishFA>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=67634 |title=Craig Sibbald |publisher=Scottish Football Association |accessdate=17 February 2018}}</ref> On 17 August 2011, Sibbald was called up to the [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scottish under-17 team]] to participate in the 2011 International Youth Toto Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/national-coach-lists-under-17-players-for-austrian-duty |title=National Coach lists under-17 players for Austrian duty |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=18 August 2011 |accessdate=28 July 2019}}</ref> He was capped twice for Scotland at under-17 level in 2012.<ref name=ScottishFA/>

'''Samuel Stanton''' (born 19 April 1994) is a Scottish professional [[association footballer|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

He has also previously played for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], with loan spells at each of [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] & [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], before moving to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Phoenix Rising FC|Phoenix Rising]], [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] and Liverpool FC before moving back to Scotland with [[Raith Rovers FC|Raith Rovers]] as well as representing Scotland at youth international level. 

==Early life==
Stanton attended Broughton Primary and [[Trinity Academy, Edinburgh]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/edinburgh-evening-news/other-sport/hibs_kid_sam_stanton_hungry_after_ibrox_debut_1_2087539 | title=Hibs kid Sam Stanton hungry after Ibrox debut | publisher=Johnston Press | work=Edinburgh Evening News | date=31 January 2012 | accessdate=4 February 2012}}</ref> Stanton shares his surname with a famous former Hibs player, [[Pat Stanton]], however he is not related to him.<ref name="stanton"/>

==Career==
===Hibernian===
Stanton was a member of the [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] [[Hibernian F.C. Under-20s and Academy|under-19 squad]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/page/PlayerProfiles/0,,10290~59538,00.html | title=Sam Stanton Hibernian Profile | publisher=Hibernian FC | work=www.hibernianfc.co.uk | accessdate=2 February 2012 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120212160808/http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/page/PlayerProfiles/0,,10290~59538,00.html | archivedate=12 February 2012 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> He was promoted to the first team on 28 December 2011 when he was an unused substitute for the match against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref name = "stanton">{{cite news | url = http://www.scotsman.com/edinburgh-evening-news/football/hibs/hibs_youngster_sam_stanton_on_the_verge_of_breakthrough_pat_fenlon_1_2070595 | title=Hibs youngster Sam Stanton on the verge of breakthrough | work=Edinburgh Evening News | publisher=Johnston Press | date=21 January 2012 | accessdate=2 February 2012}}</ref> He went on to make his first team debut aged 17 as a substitute against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 28 January 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/16664037.stm | title=Rangers 4 – 0 Hibernian | publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | date=28 January 2012 | access-date=2 February 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/european/hibs_kid_sam_stanton_hungry_after_ibrox_debut_1_2087539|title=Hibs kid Sam Stanton hungry after Ibrox debut|first=David|last=Hardie|work=Edinburgh Evening News|publisher=Johnston Press|date=31 January 2012|accessdate=4 February 2012}}</ref>

He signed a three-year contract with Hibs in September 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/top-football-stories/hibs-rising-star-sam-stanton-signs-three-year-deal-1-2505179| title=Hibs rising star Sam Stanton signs three-year deal |first=David |last=Hardie | work=Edinburgh Evening News | publisher=Johnston Press | date=4 September 2012 | accessdate=4 September 2012}}</ref> Stanton was loaned to [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] in January 2013<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20915157 |title=Cowdenbeath bring in trio on loan |date=4 January 2013 |access-date=4 January 2013 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC}}</ref> and made his debut in a 1–1 draw against [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Morton]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20920351 |title=Cowdenbeath 1–1 Morton |date=5 January 2013 |access-date=6 January 2013 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC}}</ref> His stint at Cowdenbeath ended after just two appearances, however, as he suffered a knee injury that required surgery.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/20130318/euan-on-wonder-goal_2262950_3113944 |title=Euan on Wonder Goal |work=www.hibernianfc.co.uk |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=18 March 2013 |accessdate=20 March 2013}}</ref>

Stanton established himself in the Hibs first team during the second half of the [[2013–14 Hibernian F.C. season|2013–14 season]]. He won the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|SPFL young player of the month award]] for February 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26591966 |title=Sam Stanton: Hibs midfielder is February's young player of month |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=15 March 2014 |access-date=15 March 2014}}</ref> In April 2014, Stanton signed a four-year contract extension with Hibs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27062511 |title=Sam Stanton agrees long-term Hibernian deal |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=17 April 2014 |access-date=17 April 2014}}</ref>

On 8 January 2016, Stanton signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] for the remainder of the [[2015–16 Scottish Championship]] season.

Stanton joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on a season-long loan on deadline day in August 2016.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Findlay|first1=Alan|title=SAM STANTON JOINS ON LOAN FROM HIBS|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=2664|accessdate=31 August 2016}}</ref> He scored his first goals for the club in a 2–2 draw with [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in February 2017<ref>{{cite news|title=Dumbarton 2–2 Ayr United|work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38940682|accessdate=18 February 2017}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
Stanton joined Championship team [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in July 2017, initially on loan.<ref>{{cite news|title=Southampton goalkeeper Harry Lewis joins Dundee United on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40617914|accessdate=15 July 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=15 July 2017}}</ref> The move was made permanent on 19 January 2018, with Stanton signing a two-and-a-half-year contract with United.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/5493/STANTON-SIGNS-PERMANENT-CONTRACT.html |title=Stanton signs permanent contract |publisher=Dundee United |date=19 January 2018 |accessdate=19 January 2018}}</ref>

===Phoenix Rising===
Stanton signed with [[Phoenix Rising FC|Phoenix Rising]] on 23 January 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.phxrisingfc.com/news_article/show/1080244 |title=Phoenix Rising Adds Midfielder Sam Stanton |publisher=Phoenix Rising Communications |date=23 January 2020 |accessdate=23 January 2020 |archive-date=11 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811035211/https://www.phxrisingfc.com/news_article/show/1080244 |url-status=dead }}</ref> After a successful season winning the Western Conference and reaching the [[USL Championship Final]] (which was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]]), Stanton and the club mutually agreed to part ways in December.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=9 December 2020|title=Phoenix Rising FC and Sam Stanton mutually agree to part ways|url=https://www.phxrisingfc.com/news_article/show/1136446|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116170533/https://www.phxrisingfc.com/news_article/show/1136446|archive-date=16 January 2021|access-date=9 December 2020|website=phxrisingfc.com|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Dundalk===
He signed for [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] side [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/scottish-midfielder-sam-stanton-joins-dundalk-from-phoenix-rising-1.4468411|title=Scottish midfielder Sam Stanton joins Dundalk from Phoenix Rising|first=Emmet|last=Malone|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref> Stanton made his debut in the [[2021 President of Ireland's Cup]] on 12 March 2021, as his side beat [[Shamrock Rovers F.C.|Shamrock Rovers]] on penalties to lift the trophy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.ie/articles/26744/presidents-cup-final-report-shamrock-rovers-1---1-dundalk-dundalk-win-4-3-on-penalties/|title=President's Cup Final Report: Shamrock Rovers 1 - 1 Dundalk (Dundalk win 4-3 on penalties)|website=ExtraTime.com}}</ref> He featured in all 6 of the clubs [[UEFA Europa Conference League]] qualifiers<ref name="auto">{{Soccerway|samuel-stanton/223495|accessdate=19 October 2017}}</ref> as they were narrowly knocked out 4–3 on aggregate by [[Vitesse Arnhem]] in the Third Qualifying Round.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/dundalk-1-2-vitesse-arnhem-24750036|title=Dundalk 1-2 Vitesse Arnhem: Brave Dundalk downed in Tallaght as they exit Europe|first=Paul|last=O'Hehir|date=12 August 2021|website=Irish Mirror}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 27 September in a 2–1 win over [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/dundalk-v-bohemians-5559613-Sep2021/|title=Dundalk ease relegation fears with entertaining victory over Bohs|first=Niall|last=Newberry|website=The42|date=27 September 2021 }}</ref> Stanton made a total of 40 appearances for the club in all competitions as they finished in 6th place in the league.<ref name="auto"/>

===Raith Rovers===
On 15 December it was announced that Stanton had returned to Scotland to sign for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a {{frac|2|1|2}}-year contract that would commence on 1 January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/51658/sam-stanton.htm|title=Sam Stanton | Raith Rovers FC|website=www.raithrovers.net|date=20 December 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2021/1215/1266879-sam-stanton-makes-dundalk-exit-to-join-raith-rovers/|title=Sam Stanton makes Dundalk exit to join Raith Rovers|date=15 December 2021|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref>

In January 2025, he joined Scottish League One club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1882368790291181767|title=𝐖𝐞𝐥𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐒𝐚𝐦! All at Arbroath FC are thrilled to announce the loan signing of midfielder Sam Stanton until the end of the season, from Championship side Raith Rovers.|user=ArbroathFC|author-link=Arbroath F.C.|date=23 January 2025|accessdate=24 January 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Stanton was selected for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team]] in August 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/20120731/stanton-earns-scotland-call_2262950_2866914 |title=Stanton Earns Scotland Call  |work=www.hibernianfc.co.uk|publisher=Hibernian FC|date=31 July 2012|accessdate=31 July 2012}}</ref> He appeared as a substitute in a 1–0 defeat against [[Germany national under-19 football team|Germany]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=2986&newsID=10381&newsCategoryID=1|title=Scotland Under-19s lose 1–0 to Germany|work=www.scottishfa.co.uk|publisher=Scottish Football Association|date=14 August 2012|accessdate=14 August 2012}}</ref> He then scored the winning goal in a 2–1 victory against [[Norway national under-19 football team|Norway]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=2986&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=10442|title=Scotland U19s come from behind to defeat Norway|work=www.scottishfa.co.uk|publisher=Scottish Football Association|date=23 August 2012|accessdate=23 August 2012}}</ref> On 5 March 2014, he made his debut for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] side in a 2–2 draw against [[Hungary national under-21 football team|Hungary]] at [[Tannadice Park|Tannadice]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Scotland U21 2–2 Hungary U21|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26460670|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=5 March 2014|access-date=11 March 2014}}</ref>

'''Coll Donaldson''' (born 9 April 1995) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], where he is also [[Captain (association football)|club captain]].

He has previously played for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] and [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Club career==
Donaldson grew up in [[North Berwick]], East Lothian, and attended [[North Berwick High School]], joining [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]]'s youth ranks in 2011 from [[Tynecastle F.C.|Tynecastle]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.tynecastlefc.co.uk/newsstory.php?nid=336 | title=Coll Donaldson makes the bench | publisher=Tynecastle F.C. | date=26 December 2012 | accessdate=29 May 2013 | archive-date=6 February 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206000918/https://www.tynecastlefc.co.uk/newsstory.php?nid=336 | url-status=dead }}</ref> After progressing through the club's youth system and impressing for the reserve team, he signed a new two-year contract for Livingston on 17 January 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/news/news_20130117_1.php| title=New contract for Coll Donaldson | publisher=Livingston F.C. | accessdate=7 April 2013}}</ref> Later that month he went on trial with [[Premier League]] club [[Manchester United]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/livingston-defender-coll-donaldson-will-train-1550712 | title=Manchester United hand trial to Livingston starlet Coll Donaldson | work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |  date=23 January 2013 | accessdate=28 January 2014}}</ref> He made his first-team debut for Livingston as a late substitute against [[Dunfermline Athletic]] on 30 March 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://spfl.co.uk/championship/fixture/3520034/ | title=Pars claim point | publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League]] | work=spfl.co.uk | date=30 March 2013 | accessdate=28 January 2014}}</ref> He then went on to make a further four appearances towards the end of season 2012–13.<ref>{{Soccerbase season|68650|2012|accessdate=26 April 2013}}</ref> In December 2013, Donaldson was allowed to travel to [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] for a trial.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11711/9109411/transfer-news-qpr-in-talks-to-sign-livingston-starlet-coll-donaldson | title=QPR in talks to sign Livingston starlet Coll Donaldson | publisher=[[Sky Sports]] | work=skysports.com | date=10 January 2013 | accessdate=28 January 2014}}</ref> In January 2014, Donaldson completed his move to Queens Park Rangers,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.livingstonfc.co.uk/news/news_20140128_1.php | title=Donaldson QPR Bound | publisher=[[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] | work=livingstonfc.co.uk | date=28 January 2014 | accessdate=28 January 2014}}</ref> for a fee of around £150,000.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/livingston-kid-coll-donaldson-way-3034815 | title=Livingston kid Coll Donaldson on his way to QPR as Harry Redknapp steps in with £150,000 bid | publisher=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] | work=dailyrecord.co.uk | date=18 January 2014 | accessdate=28 January 2014}}</ref> In all he made 29 appearances in all competitions, scoring once.<ref name="Soc">{{soccerbase|68650}}</ref>

On 28 January 2014, aged 19 Donaldson joined Queens Park Rangers from Livingston after impressing QPR manager [[Harry Redknapp]] during a week-long trial.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25917038 | title=QPR: Defender Coll Donaldson joins from Livingston | publisher=BBC Sport | date=27 January 2014 | access-date=22 February 2015}}</ref> Donaldson made his senior and [[Football League Championship|Championship]] debut on 3 May 2014 in a 3–2 away win against [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] at [[Oakwell]], where he was named in the starting line up and played the full 90 minutes.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27167444 | title=Barnsley 2–3 QPR | publisher=BBC Sport | date=3 May 2014 | access-date=22 February 2015}}</ref>

On 13 July 2015, Donaldson joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on a three-year contract following his release from QPR.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33503163 | title=Dundee United sign defender Coll Donaldson | publisher=BBC Sport | date=13 July 2014}}</ref> Donaldson was released on 7 August 2017, after two seasons with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dufc.co/news/coll-donaldson-departs-tannadice/ |title=Coll Donaldson departs Tannadice |publisher=Dundee United FC |date=7 August 2017 |accessdate=7 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807201424/http://dufc.co/news/coll-donaldson-departs-tannadice/ |archive-date=7 August 2017 |url-status=usurped }}</ref>

Later that month, he signed a short-term contract with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Chalk|first1=Paul|title=Caley Thistle held at home by Morton to remain bottom of the Championship|url=http://www.strathspey-herald.co.uk/Sport/Football/Caley-Thistle-held-at-home-by-Morton-to-remain-bottom-of-the-Championship-19082017.htm|accessdate=20 August 2017|work=Strathspey & Badenoch Herald|date=19 August 2017|location=Grantown-on-Spey}}</ref> In December 2017, he extended his Inverness contract for a further two and a half years.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Durent|first1=Jamie|title=Home comforts made Coll Donaldson's decision to extend Caley Thistle stay an easy one|url=http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Sport/Football/Home-comforts-made-Coll-Donaldsons-decision-to-extend-Caley-Thistle-stay-an-easy-one-11122017.htm|accessdate=13 December 2017|work=The Inverness Courier|date=12 December 2017}}</ref>

Donaldson moved to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in January 2020 for an undisclosed transfer fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51122200 |title=Ross County sign Coll Donaldson & Jordan Tillson |website=BBC Sport |date=15 January 2020 |accessdate=15 January 2020}}</ref> He made his debut in a 1–0 defeat to [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in the [[Scottish Cup]].

In January 2022, Donaldson reunited with former boss [[John Hughes (footballer, born 1964)|John Hughes]] after joining [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on loan for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Coll Donaldson arrives on loan {{!}} Dunfermline Athletic Football Club|url=https://www.dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Coll_Donaldson_arrives_on_loan&ID=13538|access-date=2022-01-03|website=www.dafc.co.uk}}</ref>

Donaldson signed a two-year contract with [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in May 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2022/05/26/coll-donaldson-signs/ |title=COLL DONALDSON SIGNS! |publisher=Falkirk Football Club |website=falkirkfc.co.uk |date=26 May 2022 |accessdate=10 July 2022}}</ref> He was appointed club captain in January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/coll-donaldson-on-falkirks-championship-opener-and-putting-derby-record-right-4724606|title=Coll Donaldson on Falkirk's Championship opener and putting derby record right|date=31 July 2024|website=Falkirk Herald}}</ref>

'''Scott Tanser''' (born 23 October 1994) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].

Tanser made his senior debut for [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] in April 2013 and made a total of 57 league and cup appearances for the club before he was allowed to leave for [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] in January 2017. He joined Scottish Premiership club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] five months later. He won the [[Scottish Cup]] and [[Scottish League Cup]] with St Johnstone in the [[2020–21 St Johnstone F.C. season|2020–21]] season. He joined [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in June 2021, winning the Scottish League Cup again in the 2025–26 campaign. He transferred to Falkirk in June 2026.

==Career==

===Rochdale===
Tanser spent time in the youth teams at [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] and [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], before coming through the [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] Academy.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Travers|first1=Chris|title=Port Vale sign Rochdale defender Scott Tanser|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/port-vale-seal-short-term-deal-for-rochdale-defender/story-30091718-detail/story.html|access-date=27 January 2017|work=Stoke Sentinel|date=27 January 2017|language=en}}</ref> He made his professional debut for the "Dale" after coming on as a 70th-minute [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[D'Arcy O'Connor]] in a 1–0 victory over [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] at [[Spotland Stadium]] on 27 April 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rochdale 1–0 Plymouth|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22229020|work=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=27 May 2013}}</ref> This was his only appearance of the [[2012–13 Rochdale A.F.C. season|2012–13]] season and he did not feature in the [[2013–14 Rochdale A.F.C. season|2013–14]] campaign as Rochdale secured [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] out of [[EFL League Two|League Two]]. He broke into the first team at the start of the [[2014–15 Rochdale A.F.C. season|2014–15]] season and signed a two-year [[Association football contracts|contract]] extension in October 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Scott Tanser Pens Contract Extension|url=http://www.rochdaleafc.co.uk/news/article/tanser-contractextension-1987131.aspx|work=[[Rochdale A.F.C.]]|access-date=3 October 2014}}</ref> Speaking the following month, [[Manager (association football)|manager]] [[Keith Hill (footballer)|Keith Hill]] said that Tanser was good enough to win England youth caps but that "politics in football, the bureaucracy and the propaganda" prevented lower league players from receiving a call-up.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Partington|first1=Richard|title=Dale starlets are being overlooked when it comes to international selection says Keith Hill|url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/dale-starlets-being-overlooked-comes-8107876|access-date=27 January 2017|work=[[Manchester Evening News]]|date=13 November 2014}}</ref> Tanser scored his first goal in senior football on 17 January 2015, opening the scoring with a "well-controlled, left-foot [[Volley (association football)|volley]]" as Rochdale recorded a 4–1 home victory over [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]]; he was named on the Football League team of the week.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rochdale 4-1 Crawley Town|url=http://beta.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30757816|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202205417/http://beta.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30757816|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 February 2017|access-date=27 January 2017|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=17 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Percival |first1=Ryan |title=Sky Bet Football League Team of the Week |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2015/january/sky-bet-football-league-team-of-the-week3/ |access-date=9 October 2019 |work=efl.com |date=19 January 2015}}</ref> He ended the season with 30 [[EFL League One|League One]] appearances to his name.

He scored his second career goal on his first appearance of the [[2015–16 Rochdale A.F.C. season|2015–16]] season, as Rochdale beat [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] 2–1 in the [[EFL Trophy|Football League Trophy]] on 6 October.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rochdale 2-1 Chesterfield: Dale into third round thanks to Lewis Alessandra strike|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/rochdale-vs-chesterfld/351633|access-date=27 January 2017|work=[[Sky Sports]]|date=6 October 2015}}</ref> He maintained a first-team place and played ten further games before falling out of the first-team picture completely; his appearance against [[Bury F.C.|Bury]] on 6 December proved to be his last of the season. He played just five league games in the first half of the [[2016–17 Rochdale A.F.C. season|2016–17]] campaign, and his contract was cancelled by mutual consent in January 2017 to allow him to find first-team football elsewhere.<ref>{{cite news|title=Scott Tanser Departs|url=http://www.rochdaleafc.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/scott-tanser-departs-3540202.aspx|access-date=27 January 2017|work=rochdaleafc.co.uk|date=27 January 2017|language=en}}</ref>

===Port Vale===
Tanser signed a contract with League One rivals [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] on 27 January 2017 to run until the end of the [[2016–17 Port Vale F.C. season|2016–17]] season.<ref name="tanj">{{cite news|title=Port Vale: Rochdale full-back Scott Tanser signs deal until end of season|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38771555|access-date=27 January 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=27 January 2017}}</ref> Tanser said that the move "was a bit of a shock actually... one minute I am at Rochdale then the next minute I am signing for Port Vale. It is a bit mad really but that is the way that football is."<ref>{{cite news|title=Scott Tanser, Defender, Port Vale, League One|url=http://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/scott-tanser-defender-port-vale-league-one-3540745.aspx|access-date=30 January 2017|work=port-vale.co.uk|date=27 January 2017|language=en}}</ref> He was released by manager [[Michael Brown (footballer, born 1977)|Michael Brown]] following the club's [[Promotion and relegation|relegation]] in May 2017.<ref>{{cite news|title=Port Vale: Thirteen senior players leave club after relegation to League Two|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39980596|access-date=20 May 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=19 May 2017}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
Tanser signed a one-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in June 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40435976 | title=Scott Tanser: St Johnstone sign left-back on one-year deal | publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport |date=28 June 2017 | access-date=28 June 2017}}</ref> Speaking the following March he stated that "This is the best club I have been at and I have loved it this season... everyone is together here, there are no outcasts in our squad".<ref>{{cite news|title=The secret to St Johnstone? Everyone gets along|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/16127794.The_secret_to_St_Johnstone__Everyone_gets_along/|access-date=13 May 2018|work=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|date=30 March 2018|language=en}}</ref> He made 31 appearances for [[Tommy Wright (footballer, born 1963)|Tommy Wright]]'s "Saints" during the [[2017–18 St Johnstone F.C. season|2017–18]] season as St Johnstone posted an eighth-placed finish. In the summer he told ''[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]]'' that he was bulking up to gain greater strength and physicality, saying he was "on a special diet, total protein and six meals a day. So I'm going to be throwing chicken, beef and all sorts of stuff down my neck soon. It's just as well I'm not a vegetarian!"<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=St Johnstone's Scott Tanser bulking up for next season |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/661485/st-johnstones-scott-tanser-bulking-up-for-next-season/ |access-date=11 December 2018 |work=The Courier |date=29 May 2018}}</ref>

On 29 December 2018, Tanser scored his first goal for St Johnstone in their 2–0 win over [[Tayside derby#Dundee vs St Johnstone|Tayside rivals]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Andy |title=Dundee 0-2 St Johnstone: Perth side move into top six |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46656859 |access-date=21 January 2019 |work=BBC Sport Scotland |date=29 December 2018}}</ref> He signed a new two-year contract extension at the club the following month.<ref>{{cite news |title=Scott Tanser signs new two-year contract extension at St Johnstone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46905875 |access-date=21 January 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=17 January 2019}}</ref> He ended the [[2018–19 St Johnstone F.C. season|2018–19]] season with 45 appearances to his name, as well as three goals as he scored a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] in the penultimate game against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=Scott Tanser shows he is made of the right stuff for St Johnstone |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/890126/scott-tanser-shows-he-is-made-of-the-right-stuff-for-st-johnstone/ |access-date=22 May 2019 |work=The Courier |date=13 May 2019}}</ref> Speaking in September 2019, Wright said of Tanser that "he is quickly becoming a top class full-back and for me he can go on to become one of the top three or four in the country".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=St Johnstone's Scott Tanser can be one of the best full-backs in Scotland |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/980589/st-johnstones-scott-tanser-can-be-one-of-the-best-full-backs-in-scotland/ |access-date=2 July 2020 |work=The Courier |date=19 September 2019}}</ref> Tanser featured in 27 matches of the [[2019–20 St Johnstone F.C. season|2019–20]] season, which was curtailed early due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]].<ref>{{Cite web|title =Celtic champions & Hearts relegated after SPFL ends season|work=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2020|access-date=19 May 2020|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52646282}}</ref>

He won the [[Scottish League Cup]] with St Johnstone in 2021, though was an unused substitute in [[2021 Scottish League Cup final (February)|the final]] as they beat [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] at [[Hampden Park]].<ref name="slcf">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56217717|title=St Johnstone beat Livingston to clinch their first League Cup|publisher=BBC|access-date=28 February 2021|date=28 February 2021}}</ref> St Johnstone went on to complete a cup double by lifting the [[Scottish Cup]] with [[2021 Scottish Cup final|a 1–0 victory]] over [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], with Tanser again an unused substitute.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Media |first1=P. A. |title=St Johnstone complete dream double after beating Hibs to win Scottish Cup |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/may/22/st-johnstone-hibernian-scottish-cup-final-match-report |access-date=23 May 2021 |work=the Guardian |date=2021-05-22 |language=en}}</ref> However, he struggled with injuries towards the end of the [[2020–21 St Johnstone F.C. season|2020–21]] season and was linked with moves away from the club, despite manager [[Callum Davidson]] being keen to keep hold of him.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=St Johnstone defender Scott Tanser looks to be out for the season but should be back for the next one |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/2185192/st-johnstone-scott-tanser-zander-clark/ |access-date=23 May 2021 |work=The Courier |date=2 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=Scott Tanser: Left-back likely to leave St Johnstone |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/2051005/scott-tanser-left-back-likely-to-leave-st-johnstone/ |access-date=23 May 2021 |work=The Courier |date=17 March 2021}}</ref> He was linked with a number of clubs in England's League One.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Peter |title=Ex-Vale left-back Tanser 'chased by Sheffield Wednesday' and League One rivals |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/port-vale-transfer-scott-tanser-5481540 |access-date=2 June 2021 |work=StokeonTrentLive |date=2021-06-02 |language=en}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 7 June 2021, Tanser signed a one-year contract with Scottish Premiership club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], with an option for a further year.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=Former St Johnstone left-back Scott Tanser signs for St Mirren |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/2288293/st-johnstone-scott-tanser-st-mirren/ |access-date=7 June 2021 |work=The Courier |date=7 June 2021}}</ref> He established himself as a popular player at [[St Mirren Park]] for what the ''[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]'' called his "marauding runs down the left flank and his wicked deliveries into the box" and kept his first-team place after [[Jim Goodwin]]'s departure in February.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ramage |first1=Ben |title=Tanser reflects on first season at Saints and insists there's more to come yet |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/scott-tanser-tells-st-mirren-27058482 |access-date=29 May 2022 |work=Daily Record |date=25 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He signed a two-year contract extension with the club in May 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=SCOTT TANSER AGREES CONTRACT EXTENSION UNTIL 2024 |url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4413-scott-tanser-agrees-contract-extension-until-2024 |access-date=2 May 2022 |work=www.stmirren.com |date=2 May 2022}}</ref> Manager [[Stephen Robinson (footballer)|Stephen Robinson]] commented that Tanser was "one of the best left-backs in this league".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ramage |first1=Ben |title=Robinson describes Tanser as 'one of the best' in league after agreeing new deal |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/stephen-robinson-describes-scott-tanser-26855071 |access-date=29 May 2022 |work=Daily Record |date=3 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> In October 2022, Tanser was involved in a car crash that left his wife injured; Robinson said that the accident "puts football into perspective".<ref>{{cite news |title=St Mirren's Tanser out after wife injured in crash |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63429810 |access-date=12 May 2023 |work=BBC Sport |date=28 October 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Ramage |first1=Ben |title=St Mirren defender Scott Tanser involved in car crash and ruled out of Hibs trip |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/st-mirren-defender-scott-tanser-28351950 |access-date=12 May 2023 |work=Daily Record |date=28 October 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He featured 35 times across the [[2022–23 St Mirren F.C. season|2022–23]] campaign.<ref name="2022–23"/>

In October 2023, Tanser extended his contract with Saints until the summer of 2026.<ref>{{cite news |title=St Mirren's Tanser extends contract until 2026 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cd1q2e18n6zo#:~:text=Scott%20Tanser%20has%20signed%20a,his%20native%20England%20in%202017. |access-date=7 October 2023 |work=BBC Sport |date=8 May 2024}}</ref> He said he was very happy after making his 100th club appearance in January.<ref>{{cite news |title=Scott Tanser loving life at Saints after hitting 100th appearance milestone |url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5275-scott-tanser-loving-life-at-saints-after-hitting-100th-appearance-milestone |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=www.stmirren.com |date=18 January 2024}}</ref> By March, he had made more crosses than any other player in the division that season, creating 28 chances and four assists.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tanser the Premiership's crossing king |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/crgr809wj9ro |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=8 March 2024}}</ref> He was named in the Premiership Team of the Week after scoring in a 3–1 with at Dundee on 4 May.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sutherland |first1=Jonathan |title=St Mirren duo make TOTW |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cld0xddyr6yo |access-date=8 May 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=6 May 2024}}</ref> He ended the [[2023–24 St Mirren F.C. season|2023–24]] season with 42 appearances to his name.<ref name="2023–24"/> He featured 32 times in the [[2024–25 St Mirren F.C. season|2024–25]] campaign, being sent off twice in games against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref name="2024–25"/> The St Mirren website described his sending off at Motherwell as "an incredibly harsh decision".<ref>{{cite news |title=St Mirren in controversial narrow defeat to Motherwell |url=https://www.stmirren.com/match-reports/5583-match-report-motherwell-st-mirren-6 |access-date=11 June 2025 |work=St Mirren FC |date=28 September 2024}}</ref>

Tanser achieved his second Scottish League Cup winner's medal, appearing as a substitute in a 3–1 win over [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in the [[2025 Scottish League Cup final]].<ref name="slc25">{{cite news |last1=Canavan |first1=Amy |title=Premier Sports Cup final: St Mirren v Celtic - radio & text |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cj4q1xdlnwgt |access-date=11 January 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> In April 2026, he was reported to be a summer transfer target for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Burns |first1=Scott |title=Scott Tanser targeted for Falkirk transfer as McGlynn eyes St Mirren star |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/scott-tanser-targeted-falkirk-transfer-37022502 |access-date=5 May 2026 |work=Daily Record |date=15 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He featured 32 times in the [[2025–26 St Mirren F.C. season|2025–26]] season, including in both legs of the play-off win over [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref name="2025–26"/>

===Falkirk===
Tanser signed a two-year contract with Scottish Premiership club Falkirk on 1 June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c3928x0lk1ko|title=Falkirk sign experienced Tanser after St Mirren exit|website=BBC Sport|date=1 June 2026|access-date=1 November 2026}}</ref> Manager [[John McGlynn (Scottish footballer)|John McGlynn]] said that "his wealth of experience in the league will help us going forward".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Macleod |first1=Andrew |title=Scott Tanser is a Bairn |url=https://falkirkfc.co.uk/scott-tanser-is-a-bairn/ |access-date=1 November 2026 |work=Falkirk FC |date=1 June 2026}}</ref> He scored his first goal at [[Falkirk Stadium]] in a 2–0 win over Celtic on 1 November.<ref>{{cite news |title=Celtic stunned by Falkirk as inspired Scott Bain frustrates former club |url=https://www.leaderlive.co.uk/sport/national/26688223.celtic-stunned-falkirk-inspired-scott-bain-frustrates-former-club/ |access-date=3 November 2026 |work=The Leader |date=1 November 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Scott Bain''' (born 22 November 1991) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]]. Bain is an [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] youth product, although never played in a competitive first team Aberdeen game. After playing on loan at [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], he played more than 100 games for each of [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] and [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]. He then played 78 games during a trophy-laden seven-year spell at Celtic, winning 14 major honours to become the most decorated goalkeeper in the club’s history.

Bain has played four times for the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

==Club career==
===Aberdeen===
Bain began his footballing career at [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]'s [[Aberdeen F.C. Under-20s and Academy|academy]]. Shortly after his promotion to the first team, he was loaned to [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], where he made his professional debut.<ref>[http://www.afc.co.uk/articles/20100817/scott-bain-moves-to-elgin-_2212158_2125638 Scott Bain moves to Elgin]; Aberdeen FC, 17 August 2010</ref><ref>[http://spfl.co.uk/league-two/fixture/3285981/ Elgin City 0–2 East Stirlingshire]; [[Scottish Professional Football League|SPFL]], 21 August 2010</ref> In May 2011, Bain was released by Aberdeen.

===Alloa Athletic===
In June 2011, Bain signed a one-year contract with [[Scottish Third Division]] side [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]].<ref>[http://eveningexpress.co.uk/Article.aspx/2303707 Hartley signs ex-Aberdeen FC player Bain for Alloa]; Evening Express, 9 June 2011</ref> He established himself as a first-team regular, and helped the club to consecutive promotions in his first two seasons.

===Dundee===
On 29 May 2014, Bain signed a three-year contract with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>[http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/dundee-snap-up-kevin-thomson-3623299  Dundee snap up Kevin Thomson and Scott Bain with both players to be unveiled at Dens Park on Friday]; [[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]], 29 May 2014</ref> He made his debut on 26 August 2014, in a 4–0 win against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DUNDEE VS RAITH ROVERS|url=http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/fixtures-and-results/dundee-vs-raith-rovers-4|publisher=Dundee F.C.|last=Christie|first=James|date=26 August 2014|accessdate=26 August 2014}}</ref> Bain made a first league appearance for Dundee in October 2014, when [[Kyle Letheren]] was injured during a pre-match exercise.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29725040 |title=Dundee: Kyle Letheren injury blow triggers goalkeeper search |first=Jim |last=Spence |work=BBC Sport |date=22 October 2014 |access-date=1 January 2018}}</ref> On 6 April 2015, he signed a new contract with Dundee, extending his deal with the club until 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Goalkeeper Scott Bain signs Dundee contract extension|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32195130|work=BBC Sport|date=6 April 2015|access-date=1 May 2015}}</ref> Bain was dropped from the Dundee first team squad by manager [[Neil McCann]] in November 2017, for unspecified disciplinary reasons.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Shanks|first1=Ciaran|title=McCann says there is 'ongoing disciplinary process' about Scott Bain|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/neil-mccann-dundee-goalie-scott-bain-ongoing-disciplinary-process-scot/|accessdate=14 November 2017|work=Evening Telegraph|date=7 November 2017|location=Dundee}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42100795 |title=Dundee: Scott Bain absence continues amid 'ongoing' issue, says boss Neil McCann |work=BBC Sport |date=23 November 2017 |accessdate=23 November 2017}}</ref>

====Hibernian (loan)====
On 1 January 2018, it was announced that Bain had joined [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on loan until the end of the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/8284 |title=Scott Bain joins Hibernian |publisher=hibernianfc.co.uk |date=1 January 2018 |accessdate=1 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://dundeefc.co.uk/news/bain-leaves-loan |title=Bain leaves on loan |publisher=dundeefc.co.uk |date=1 January 2018 |accessdate=1 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://stv.tv/sport/football/1405423-hibs-sign-goalkeeper-scott-bain-on-loan-from-dundee |title=Hibs sign goalkeeper Scott Bain on loan from Dundee |publisher=stv.tv/sport |date=1 January 2018 |accessdate=1 January 2018 |archive-date=24 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181224170556/https://stv.tv/sport/football/1405423-hibs-sign-goalkeeper-scott-bain-on-loan-from-dundee/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Hibernian cancelled the loan on 31 January, which allowed Bain to join [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] instead.<ref name = "celtic loan"/>

===Celtic===
Bain joined Celtic on 31 January 2018, initially on loan from Dundee.<ref name = "celtic loan"/> Celtic needed another goalkeeper to provide competition for [[Dorus de Vries]], following an injury to [[Craig Gordon]].<ref name = "celtic loan">{{cite web|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/13913|title=Celtic's double deadline day signings from Dundee|work=celticfc.net|date=1 February 2018|accessdate=1 February 2018}}</ref> Bain made his first appearance for Celtic on 11 March, in a 3–2 win against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], after de Vries suffered an injury in training.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43275522 |title=Rangers 2–3 Celtic |work=BBC Sport |date=11 March 2018 |accessdate=11 March 2018 |first=Bryn |last=Palmer}}</ref>

With his contract with Dundee due to expire at the end of the 2017–18 season, Bain signed a four-year contract with Celtic in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/14369 |title=The future's in safe hands: Scott Bain signs four-year deal |publisher=Celtic FC |date=10 May 2018 |accessdate=10 May 2018 |first=Tony |last=Connelly}}</ref> Bain played regularly for Celtic after the January 2019 winter break.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47187256 |title=Scott Bain: Has Celtic goalkeeper become Brendan Rodgers' first-choice between the posts? |first=Stefan |last=Bienkowski |work=BBC Sport |date=10 February 2019 |accessdate=10 February 2019}}</ref>

In October 2019, he signed a one-year contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50247735|title=Celtic goalkeeper Scott Bain signs one-year contract extension|work=BBC Sport |date=31 October 2019}}</ref>

His last game for Celtic was a 3–2 league home win against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 18 May 2024. After failing to make a first team appearance during the 2024–25 season and just earning eight such appearances in total in the previous three seasons,<ref name=sb>{{Cite web|url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=52521|title=Scott Bain | Football Stats | Falkirk | Age 34 | Soccer Base|website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref> Bain was released by Celtic at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c365zkrz9jgo |title=Bain 'will always support' Celtic after seven-year stay ends |website=BBC Sport |date=29 May 2025 |accessdate=29 May 2025}}</ref>

===Falkirk===
On 3 June 2025, Bain signed a one-year deal with [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2025/06/03/scott-bain-is-a-bairn/ | title=SCOTT BAIN IS A BAIRN! | publisher=Falkirk FC | date=3 June 2025 | access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref>
 
On 9 January 2026, Bain signed a two-year contract extension at Falkirk, with the option of an additional year; keeping him at the [[Falkirk Stadium]] until at least June 2028.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/ex-celtic-goalkeeper-scott-bain-signs-new-falkirk-contract-5469997|title=Scott Bain signs new Falkirk contract as Scotland World Cup hopeful commits long-term|date=9 January 2026|website=Falkirk Herald}}</ref>

==International career==
Due to an injury to [[Allan McGregor]], [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] manager [[Gordon Strachan]] called Bain into the national squad for a friendly with [[Qatar national football team|Qatar]] and a [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying]] match with the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] in June 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=Scotland: Allan McGregor's rest gives Scott Bain first call-up|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32780203|access-date=18 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2015}}</ref>

Bain was recalled to the squad in May 2018 for friendly matches against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] and [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]], after McGregor again dropped out through injury.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44159498 |title=Scotland: Scott Bain added to squad as Allan McGregor pulls out |work=BBC Sport |date=18 May 2018 |accessdate=18 May 2018}}</ref> He made his first full international appearance on 2 June 2018, in a 1–0 defeat against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44061121 |title=Mexico 1–0 Scotland |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |work=BBC Sport |date=3 June 2018 |accessdate=3 June 2018}}</ref> His second cap came in a 3–0 defeat against [[Kazakhstan national football team|Kazakhstan]] on 21 March 2019 in [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying Group I|Euro 2020 qualification]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/47543622|title=Reaction as McLeish's Scotland are routed 3-0 in Kazakhstan|date=21 March 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=21 March 2019}}</ref>

Bain was recalled to the international squad in November 2025, six years since his last call-up.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c04gvxrw3x6o |title=Scotland head coach Clarke plays down keeper crisis |website=BBC Sport |first=Chris |last=Bertram |date=3 November 2025 |accessdate=4 November 2025}}</ref> He finally gained his first cap of [[Steve Clarke]]'s time as Scotland boss when he came on as a half-time substitute in a friendly against the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]] at the [[Hill Dickinson Stadium]] on 31 March 2026. Bain made an impressive save from [[Amad Diallo]] as the Scots lost 1-0.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Ivory Coast 1-0 Scotland (31 Mar, 2026) Game Analysis - ESPN (UK) | url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report/_/gameId/401859485 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260402101440/https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report/_/gameId/401859485 | access-date=2026-10-09 | archive-date=2026-04-02}}</ref>

'''Joseph Harris Wright''' (born 26 February 1995) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]. He is a former Wales under-21 international.

He was originally a professional with [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] in England and has played for English clubs [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] (on loan), [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] and [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], as well as with Scottish club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

Born in England, Wright has represented Wales at [[Wales national under-21 football team|Under 21]] level.

==Club career==
===Huddersfield Town===
Wright joined [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] at under-16 level in September 2010, and signed his first professional contract with the club in 2013.<ref name="Wright First Pro Contract">{{Cite web |date=2 April 2013 |title=FOUR 2ND YEAR SCHOLARS OFFERED DEALS |url=http://www.htafc.com/news/article/academy-news-four-offered-pro-deals-749534.aspx?pageView=full#anchored |access-date=11 August 2015 |website=htafc.com |publisher=Huddersfield Town}}</ref> Wright featured on the bench for the Terriers in February 2015, before securing a further one-year contract to keep him at the club until June 2016.<ref name="Wright Contract">{{Cite web |date=22 June 2015 |title=CONTRACT UPDATE |url=http://www.htafc.com/news/article/huddersfield-town-contract-updates-201516-2501475.aspx |access-date=11 August 2015 |website=htafc.com |publisher=Huddersfield Town}}</ref>

====Accrington Stanley (loan)====
In the summer of 2015, Wright signed for [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] on loan until January 2016 and made his professional debut against [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] in August as a substitute for [[Adam Buxton (footballer)|Adam Buxton]].<ref name="Loan to Accrington">{{Cite web |date=27 July 2015 |title=Joe has the Wright stuff |url=http://accringtonstanley.co.uk/2015/07/joe-has-the-wright-stuff/ |access-date=11 August 2015 |website=accringtonstanley.co.uk |publisher=Accrington Stanley}}</ref><ref name="Pro Debut">{{Cite web |date=8 August 2015 |title=Accrington 1 Luton 1 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33744481 |access-date=11 August 2015 |website=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=BBC}}</ref>

On 5 January 2016, Wright's loan deal was extended until the end of the season.

===Doncaster Rovers===
Following the conclusion of the 2015–16 season, Wright joined recently relegated [[Football League Two]] side [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]].

On the final day of the [[2020–21 Doncaster Rovers F.C. season|2020–21 season]], Wright damaged both his knee and ankle after falling awkwardly, the injury expected to rule him out for a period of up to nine months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.doncasterfreepress.co.uk/sport/football/bitter-blow-for-joe-wright-as-severity-of-doncaster-rovers-defenders-injury-is-revealed-3237489|title=Bitter blow for Joe Wright as severity of Doncaster Rovers defender's injury is revealed|publisher=Doncaster Free Press|last=Hoden|first=Liam|date=14 May 2021|accessdate=29 January 2025}}</ref> Following the injury, it was confirmed that the club had been unable to reach an agreement with Wright with regards to a new contract and he would be departing the club, although Rovers would continue to offer him recovery and rehabilitation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/news/2021/may/rovers-submit-retain-and-release-list-to-efl/|title=Rovers submit retain and release list to EFL|website=www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk|date=14 May 2021|accessdate=29 January 2025}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
On 13 July 2022, after a year without a club, Wright joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a one-year deal,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/joe-wright-joins-killie/ | title=Joe Wright joins Killie | date=13 July 2022 }}</ref> having also had a trial with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-set-to-offer-joe-wright-a-contract-after-trialist-completes-90-minutes-against-bonnyrigg-3762633 | title=Hearts set to offer Joe Wright a contract after trialist completes 90 minutes in 5-0 win over Bonnyrigg Rose | date=9 July 2022 }}</ref>

In his debut season, Wright made 44 appearances across all competitions, scoring 5 goals.  Notably, he scored twice in a 2–3 home defeat to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on 4 November 2022 and added goals against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] later in the season.  His performances contributed to Kilmarnock's 10th-place finish in the [[Scottish Premiership]], he extended his stay with the club by signing a two-year contract, keeping him at [[Rugby Park]] until June 2025.

Wright continued to be a key figure in the [[2023–24 Scottish Premiership|2023–24 season]], making 32 appearances and scoring 3 goals.  He found the net in league matches against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 16 September 2023, [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on 30 December 2023, and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 13 April 2024. His contributions helped Kilmarnock secure a 4th-place finish, earning qualification for the [[UEFA Europa League]].

In the [[2024–25 Scottish Premiership|2024–25 season]], Wright has made 36 appearances across all competitions, scoring 2 goals. A highlight of the season was his decisive goal in the [[UEFA Conference League|UEFA Europa Conference League]] on 15 August 2024, where he scored the only goal in a 1–0 away victory against [[Tromsø IL]], securing a 3–2 aggregate win and advancing Kilmarnock to the play-off round against [[F.C. Copenhagen|FC Copenhagen]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tromso 0-1 Kilmarnock (2-3 agg): Joe Wright header sends Killie to Europa Conference League play-offs against FC Copenhagen |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/tromso-vs-kilmarnock/report/520919 |access-date=2025-04-30 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref>

===Bradford City===
On 6 June 2025, Wright agreed to join newly promoted League One side [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityafc.com/news/2025/june/06/bantams-snap-up-wright/|title=BANTAMS SNAP UP WRIGHT|website=www.bradfordcityafc.com|date=6 June 2025|accessdate=6 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ckg789lrg22o|title=Joe Wright: Bradford City sign Kilmarnock defender on two-year deal|date=6 June 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

He made his first appearance for the Bantams in the opening game of the 2025/26 [[EFL League One]] season in a 2–1 victory against [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Bradford City 2-1 Wycombe Wanderers | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cj4wdk51l4kt }}</ref><ref name="sb2526" />

Wright scored his first goal for the club on 30 August 2025 as the opener in a 3–2 win against fellow newly promoted side [[AFC Wimbledon]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradford City 3-2 AFC Wimbledon: League One |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx29lvv9jxnt |access-date=2025-12-27 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 31 August 2026, Wright returned to the [[Scottish Premiership]] with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |last=@officialbantams |date=31 August 2026 |title=WRIGHT DEPARTS BANTAMS |url=https://www.bradfordcityafc.com/news/2026/august/31/wright-departs-bantams/ |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=www.bradfordcityafc.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-31 |title=Joe Wright becomes latest summer signing |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/joe-wright-becomes-latest-summer-signing/ |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Wright made his Dundee debut on 6 September as a substitute away to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Heart of Midlothian vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership updates & report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwn8mrrnrr45t |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He suffered an injured hamstring the following week in a bounce game against [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], keeping him out for several weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2026-09-14 |title=Dundee injury woes worsen with TWO more sidelined |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5579299/dundee-injury-woes-worsen-two-sidelined/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Wright has represented the [[Wales national under-21 football team]].<ref name="Wales u21 debut">{{Cite web |date=31 March 2015 |title=Wales U21 3 Bulgaria U21 1 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31952436 |access-date=11 August 2015 |website=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=BBC}}</ref>
