'''Matthew Colin Foulds''' (born 1  February 1998) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

==Career==
Foulds was one of five academy players who signed their first professional contracts at [[Bury F.C.|Bury]] on 18 February 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=Five Youngsters Sign Pro Deals|url=http://www.buryfc.co.uk/news/article/five-youngsters-sign-professional-deals-2245138.aspx|accessdate=2 September 2015|publisher=Bury F.C.|date=18 February 2015|archive-date=16 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170516210625/http://www.buryfc.co.uk/news/article/five-youngsters-sign-professional-deals-2245138.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was first included in a matchday squad on 22 August of that year, as the Shakers drew 3–3 away to [[Crewe Alexandra]] in [[Football League One|League One]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Crewe 3-3 Bury|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33944430|access-date=2 September 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 August 2015}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut in a 1–4 loss to [[Premier League]] team [[Leicester City]] in a [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] second-round game at [[Gigg Lane]], replacing [[Chris Hussey]] at the start of the second half.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bury 1-4 Leicester|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33969858|access-date=2 September 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 August 2015}}</ref> On 1 September, Foulds made his first start, playing the entirety of a 2–1 win at [[Accrington Stanley]] in the first round of the [[Football League Trophy]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Accrington 1-2 Bury|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34047910|access-date=2 September 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 September 2015}}</ref>

[[Premier League]] club [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] agreed a deal to sign Foulds on 19 November 2015 for an undisclosed fee, with the player set to move to [[Goodison Park]] at the beginning of the 2016 January transfer window.<ref>{{cite news|title=Blues Agree Foulds Deal|url=http://www.evertonfc.com/news/2015/11/19/blues-agree-foulds-deal|accessdate=19 November 2015|publisher=Everton F.C.|date=19 November 2015}}</ref>

After four years with the club, Foulds was released by Everton at the end of his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.evertonfc.com/news/1697344/everton-announces-players-to-leave-club|title=EVERTON ANNOUNCES PLAYERS TO LEAVE CLUB|publisher=[[Everton F.C.]]|date=25 June 2020|accessdate=9 October 2020}}</ref>

In September 2020, Foulds spent time on trial with [[Serie C]] club [[Como 1907|Como]] and on 14 October, he signed a two-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://comofootball.com/matty-foulds-al-como/|title=MATTY FOULDS AL COMO|publisher=[[Como 1907|Como]]|date=14 October 2020|accessdate=14 October 2020|language=Italian|archive-date=9 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209175207/https://comofootball.com/matty-foulds-al-como/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 5 January 2021, Foulds agreed to terminate his contract by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://comofootball.com/risolto-il-contratto-con-matty-foulds/|title=RISOLTO IL CONTRATTO CON MATTY FOULDS|publisher=[[Como 1907]]|date=5 January 2020|accessdate=5 January 2020|language=Italian|archive-date=9 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209180711/https://comofootball.com/risolto-il-contratto-con-matty-foulds/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Later that month he signed a short-term contract with hometown club [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], a club he had originally played youth football for.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/19016644.defender-foulds-leaves-italy-sign-bradford-city/|title=Foulds comes home to become Bradford City's fifth signing of the window|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/2021/january/foulds-becomes-fifth-january-addition/|title=FOULDS BECOMES FIFTH JANUARY ADDITION|website=www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk|access-date=16 January 2021|archive-date=21 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121235646/https://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/2021/january/foulds-becomes-fifth-january-addition/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 12 May 2021 he was one of four players offered a new contract by Bradford City.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/2021/may/nine-bantams-to-depart/|title=NINE BANTAMS TO DEPART|website=www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/19296490.bradford-city-release-nine-players-contracts-expire/|title=City wave goodbye to nine - including long-serving defensive duo|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus}}</ref> On 15 June 2021, he agreed a one-year contract extension with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/bradford-everton-como-italian-b1866101.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220512/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/bradford-everton-como-italian-b1866101.html |archive-date=12 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Matthew Foulds signs Bradford deal|work=[[The Independent]]|date=15 June 2021|accessdate=15 June 2021}}</ref> He was one of seven players offered a new contract by Bradford City at the end of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/sportlatest/20138405.bradford-city-bid-farewell-six-seven-offered-new-deals/|title=Bantams says goodbye to six as seven including skipper offered new deals|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus}}</ref> Foulds signed a new two-year deal with the club on 18 May 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityafc.com/news/2022/may/two-more-years-for-foulds/|title=TWO MORE YEARS FOR FOULDS|website=www.bradfordcityafc.com|date=18 May 2022}}</ref>

In January 2023 he moved on loan to [[Harrogate Town F.C.|Harrogate Town]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64311891|title=Bradford loan left-back Foulds to Harrogate|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> In June 2023, he signed permanently for Harrogate for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Harrogate sign defenders Foulds and McDonald |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65861391 |access-date=2023-06-09}}</ref>

On 8 May 2025, the club announced the player would be released in June when his contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-08 |title=Harrogate Town release five players at the end of 2024-25 League Two season |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cx2q9qw3xqqo |access-date=2025-05-10 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In July 2025, Foulds signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/matty-foulds-signs-for-saints/|title=Matty Foulds signs for Saints!|publisher=[[St Johnstone F.C.]]|date=3 July 2025|accessdate=11 August 2025}}</ref>

web|url=http://www.celticfc.net/team/1203 |title=Welcome to Paradise |publisher=CelticFC |date= |accessdate=26 September 2015}} On 21 May 2015, Nesbitt scored a hat-trick in the [[2014–15 Scottish web|title=Partick Thistle 2–0 St Johnstone|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35430343|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Wilson|first=Richard|date=23 February 2016}} He signed on loan with [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in August 2016.{{cite web|last=Mitchell |first=Jonathan |url=http://gmfc.net/2016/08/09/aidan-nesbitt-signs-on-loan-from-celtic//|title=Aidan Nesbitt signs on loan from news|url=http://gmfc.net/2017/01/04/nesbitt-loan-extended-until-end-of-the-season/ |title=Nesbitt loan extended until end of the season |publisher=Greenock Morton F.C. |first=Jonathan |last=Mitchell '''Božo Mikulić''' ({{IPA|hr|bǒːʒo mîkulitɕ}};<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hjp.znanje.hr/index.php?show=search_by_id&id=d1djXQ%3D%3D|title=Bȏg|quote=Bóžo|website=Hrvatski jezični portal|access-date=2018-03-19|language=sh}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://hjp.znanje.hr/index.php?show=search_by_id&id=eF1gUBk%3D&keyword=II|title=Nìkola|quote=Mȉkulić|website=Hrvatski jezični portal|access-date=2018-03-19|language=sh}}</ref> born 29 January 1997) is a Croatian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C|St Johnstone]].

==Career==
Apart from his initial two years at [[NK Omladinac Vranjic]], Mikulić spent his entire youth career in [[RNK Split]], becoming a youth international in 2014.<ref>[http://hns-cff.hr/players/119407/bozo-mikulic/ Božo Mikulić] at Croatian Football Federation official site</ref> As the captain of [[RNK Split|Split]]'s U19 team, who also handled his team's set-pieces, he was loaned out to the [[Druga HNL|second-tier]] team [[NK Imotski]] where he scored on his senior debut, a 1–1 away draw with [[NK Dugopolje]].<ref>[http://www.dalmacijanews.hr/clanak/n0vj-mikulic-debitirao-pogotkom-odlican-je-osjecaj-ali-bio-bih-jos-sretniji-da-smo-odnijeli-sva-tri-boda Mikulić debitirao pogotkom: Odličan je osjećaj, ali bio bih još sretniji da smo odnijeli sva tri boda] at Dalmacijanews</ref> In the summer of 2016, he returned to [[RNK Split]] and made his [[Prva HNL]] debut.

On 31 August 2017, Mikulić signed for Italian club [[U.C. Sampdoria]] on a permanent deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sampdoria.it/en/croatian-youngster-mikulic-signs-samp/|title=Croatian youngster Mikulic signs for Samp|publisher=U.C. Sampdoria|date=31 August 2017|access-date=2 September 2017}}</ref>

On 15 June 2018, Mikulić moved to [[Croatia|Croatian]] club [[HNK Hajduk Split|Hajduk Split]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hajduk.hr/vijest/bozo-mikulic-potpisao-za-hajduk-/10333|title=BOŽO MIKULIĆ POTPISAO ZA HAJDUK!|language=Croatian|website=hajduk.hr|date=15 June 2018|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref> He made his league debut for the club on 5 August 2018 in a 1–1 home draw with [[NK Lokomotiva|Lokomotiva Zagreb]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2018/08/05/croatia/1-hnl/hnk-hajduk-split/nk-lokomotiva-zagreb/2798642/|title=Hajduk Split vs. Lokomotiva Zagreb – 5 August 2018 – Soccerway|website=int.soccerway.com|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref> On 7 August 2019, he joined [[Slaven Belupo]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hajduk.hr/vijest/bozo-mikulic-na-posudbi-u-slaven-belupu/11881|title=Božo Mikulić na posudbi u Slaven Belupu|language=Croatian|website=hajduk.hr|date=7 August 2019|access-date=7 August 2019}}</ref>

On 24 August 2021, he returned to Italy and signed a two-year contract with [[Serie C]] club [[A.C.R. Messina|ACR Messina]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[A.C.R. Messina|ACR Messina]]|url=https://www.facebook.com/MessinaOfficialPage/posts/1184617308692157|title=Božo Mikulić è un giocatore del Messina|date=24 August 2021|accessdate=23 November 2021|language=it}}</ref>

On 17 February 2022, Mikulić moved to [[FK Auda|Auda]], newly promoted to [[Latvian Higher League]].<ref>{{cite press release|publisher=[[FK Auda|Auda]]|url=https://www.facebook.com/fkauda/posts/357376479724108|title=Esam priecīgi paziņot, ka no Itālijas C sērijas kluba ACR Messina futbola klubam AUDA pievienojas Božo Mikuličs|date=17 February 2022|access-date=18 February 2022|language=lv}}</ref>

On 15 October 2024, Mikulić agreed to join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a contract until the end of the season, subject to a work permit being granted.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/deal-agreed-for-bozo-mikulic|title=Deal agreed for Bozo Mikulic|website=www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk|date=15 October 2024|accessdate=18 October 2024}}</ref>

'''Jack McMillan''' (born 18 December 1997) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]. He has previously played for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] and [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]].

==Career==

===Motherwell===
McMillan is a product of the [[Motherwell F.C. Reserve and Youth squads|Motherwell Academy]]. He made his debut for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 15 October 2016, in a 2–0 defeat against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37594146|title=Celtic 2–0 Motherwell|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=15 October 2016|accessdate=26 January 2016}}</ref>

On 2 December 2016, McMillan signed a new two-and-a-half-year deal with Motherwell.<ref>{{cite web|title=McMillan signs contract extension|url=http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2016/12/02/mcmillan-signs-contract-extension/|publisher=Motherwell F.C.|accessdate=26 January 2017|date=2 December 2016}}</ref>

On 31 August 2017, McMillan moved on loan to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] until January 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=McMillan departs on loan|url=http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2017/08/31/mcmillan-departs-on-loan/|publisher=Motherwell F.C.|date=31 August 2017|accessdate=31 August 2017}}</ref>

===Livingston===
He then made the move permanent on 19 January 2018, signing until summer 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jack McMillan a-loan no more|url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/jack-mcmillan-loan-no/|publisher=Livingston F.C.|date=19 January 2018|accessdate=19 January 2018}}</ref> McMillan moved on loan to [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in January 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=SIGNING NEWS:JACK MCMILLAN IS A JAG|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-jack-mcmillan-is-a-jag/|publisher=Partick Thistle F.C.|date=21 January 2019|accessdate=13 July 2019}}</ref> He made 16 appearances for the Jags in all competitions in which he featured predominantly as part of a back three.

===Partick Thistle return===
Three years after his initial loan at the club, on 1 June 2022, McMillan signed a two-year deal with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Signing News: McMillan agrees two-year deal |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-mcmillan-agrees-two-year-deal/ |access-date=2022-06-01 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref> McMillan was offered a new contract with Partick Thistle but opted to reject it, resulting in his departure from the club at the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jack McMillan leaves Partick Thistle |url= https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/jack-mcmillan-leaves-partick-thistle/ |website=Partick Thistle FC| accessdate=21 June 2024| language=en}}</ref>

===Exeter City===
On 20 June 2024, McMillan made his first foray into English football by signing a two-year deal with [[EFL League One]] side [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City.]]The transfer reunited McMillan with manager [[Gary Caldwell]] who had originally signed him to Partick Thistle during his initial loan spell.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jack McMillan signs for City |url= https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/jack-mcmillan-signs-city |website=Exeter City FC |accessdate=21 June 2024|language=en}}</ref>

'''Ryan Strain''' (born 2 April 1997) is an Australian professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Fullback (association football)|right back]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]. Born in England, he plays for the [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia national team]].

==Club career==

===Adelaide United===
On 22 September 2017, Strain signed a 1-year scholarship contract with [[Adelaide United FC|Adelaide United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adelaideunited.com.au/news/reds-sign-trio-scholarships|title=Reds sign trio on scholarships|publisher=[[Adelaide United FC|Adelaide United]]|date=22 September 2017}}</ref> 3 months later, he signed a two-year contract extension as a senior player, making him the 30th player to progress from the club's youth team to their senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adelaideunited.com.au/news/strain-signs-two-year-extension-united|title=Strain signs two-year extension with United|publisher=[[Adelaide United FC|Adelaide United]]|date=22 December 2017}}</ref>

===Maccabi Haifa===
In June 2021, Strain joined Israeli club [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.|Maccabi Haifa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.one.co.il/Article/387076.html|title=ההגנה מתגבשת: ראיין סטריין סיכם במכבי חיפה|trans-title=The defence is coming together: Ryan Strain concluded with Maccabi Haifa|language=he|website=[[One (website)|One]]|date=23 June 2021}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
In June 2022, Strain joined Scottish club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a two-year deal, following the expiry of his contract at Israeli side Maccabi Haifa.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4470-st-mirren-sign-ryan-strain-on-two-year-deal|title=St Mirren sign Ryan Strain on two-year deal|publisher=[[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]|website=stmirren.com|date=21 June 2022}}</ref> Ryan left [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in June 2024 at the end of his contract, deciding his future lay elsewhere. His grandfather [[Gerry Baker]] played for the Paisley club between 1958 and 1960.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bt.com/sport/news/2022/june/ryan-strain-follows-in-footsteps-of-grandfather-gerry-baker-by-joining-st-mirren |title=Ryan Strain follows in footsteps of grandfather Gerry Baker by joining St Mirren. Ryan left St. Mirren in May 2024, deciding not to renew his contract. |website=BT Sport |date=21 June 2022 |accessdate=3 July 2022}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Strain was called up to an [[Australia national under-20 soccer team|Australian under-20]] squad in August 2015.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.modburysc.com.au/strain-selected-for-young-socceroos-camp/|website=[[Modbury Jets SC]]|date=14 August 2015|title=Strain selected for Young Socceroos camp}}</ref>

In November 2020, Strain was called up to the [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team|Australian under-23]] team for friendlies against [[A-League]] sides.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.adelaideunited.com.au/news/ryan-strain-called-olyroos-training-camp|title=Ryan Strain called into Olyroos training camp|date=9 November 2020|accessdate=10 November 2020|website=[[Adelaide United FC]]}}</ref> He made his debut on 17 November 2020 in a practice match against the new expansion [[A-League]] club [[Macarthur FC]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Greco|first=John|date=17 November 2020|title=Australia U-23's secure comeback win over Macarthur FC|url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/live-australia-u-23-mens-v-macarthur-fc-match-report-goals-video-highlights-stream-updates|access-date=17 November 2020|website=[[Australia men's national soccer team|Socceroos]]}}</ref>

===Senior===
Strain was called up to the [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australian senior national team]] in August 2021, for [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – AFC third round|2022 World Cup qualifiers]] against [[China national football team|China]] and [[Vietnam national football team|Vietnam]].<ref>[https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/september-squad-announcement 27 players destined for Doha as Socceroos get set for final phase of AFC Asian Qualifying], Socceroos official website, 28 August 2021</ref> Strain did not feature in either game, with media reports suggesting that he had injured his hamstring.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7416303/no-time-to-relax-for-arnies-socceroos/|title=No time to relax for Arnie's Socceroos|first=Ed|last=Jackson|date=4 September 2021|accessdate=19 October 2021|quote=Fullback Ryan Strain is also understood to be battling a hamstring niggle.}}</ref>

Strain was again called up to the Australian squad in September 2022 for two friendly matches against [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]] in the lead-up to the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/keanu-baccus-ryan-strain-urged-27986792|title=Keanu Baccus and Ryan Strain urged to grab World Cup opportunity after St Mirren duo bag Australia call-up|date=14 September 2022|access-date=15 September 2022|publisher=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|first=Ben|last=Ramage}}</ref> He made his debut for Australia in the second game, a 2–0 win, as a second-half substitute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/australia-boss-delivers-key-message-28100211|title=Australia boss delivers key message to St Mirren World Cup hopefuls Keanu Baccus and Ryan Strain|date=28 September 2022|access-date=28 September 2022|first=Ben|last=Ramage|website=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]}}</ref>

After missing out on selection in Australia's squad for the 2022 FIFA World Cup, Strain was next called up for Australia for friendly matches against [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]] in March 2023, following the withdrawal of [[Aaron Mooy]] due to injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/ryan-strain-earns-australia-chance-29506201|title=Ryan Strain earns Australia chance as St Mirren defender joins Keanu Baccus on international duty|first=Ben|last=Ramage|date=20 March 2023|access-date=26 March 2023|website=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]}}</ref> He made his second appearance for Australia as a substitute in a loss to [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] on 15 June 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cyxgpdegwglo.amp|title=Saints pair feature as Socceroos defeated by Messi-inspired Argentina|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 June 2023|access-date=15 June 2023}}</ref> Strain made his first international start in a 1–0 loss to [[England national football team|England]] at [[Wembley Stadium]] on 13 October 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/strain-makes-memorable-debut-against-old-pals|title=Strain makes memorable starting debut against old pals|first=Tim|last=Gibson|website=[[Socceroos]]|access-date=26 October 2023|date=14 October 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Strain is the son of English athlete [[Lorraine Baker]] and the grandson of American-born footballer [[Gerry Baker]], who also played for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/reds-winger-ryan-strain-lifted-the-ffa-cup-60-years-after-his-grandfather-won-the-scottish-cup/news-story/ff8d9b1946609de21827ec2f8c8ac5d3 |title=Reds winger Ryan Strain lifted the FFA Cup 60 years after his grandfather won the Scottish Cup |publisher=Fox Sports|location=Australia|date=2 November 2018 |access-date=22 March 2023}}</ref> He is also younger brother of [[Aston Villa F.C.]] trainee [[Tom Strain]], who plays for [[Salisbury United FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/exclusive-tom-strains-journey-from-adelaide-to-aston-villa-and-back-again-30955891 |title=Exclusive: Tom Strain's journey from Adelaide to Aston Villa and back again |publisher=One Football|location=Australia|date=2 November 2018 |access-date=22 March 2023}}</ref>

'''Jamie Gullan''' (born 2 July 1999) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. Gullan has previously played for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], where he spent loan spells with [[Gala Fairydean Rovers F.C.|Gala Fairydean Rovers]], [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] and [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], before joining Raith permanently in 2022. He spent 2024 with [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] club [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]].

==Career==
===Hibernian===
Gullan was in the [[Heart of Midlothian F.C. Under-20s and Academy|Heart of Midlothian]] youth system, but was released and he then signed with Hibernian.<ref name = "debut"/> During the 2017–18 season he played for the Hibs development team, and he was also loaned to [[Gala Fairydean Rovers F.C.|Gala Fairydean Rovers]] and [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/8366 |title=DEVELOPMENT LOANS FOR DEVELOPMENT SQUAD DUO |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=26 January 2018 |accessdate=7 October 2018}}</ref> He scored one of the goals as Hibs won the [[2017–18 Scottish Youth Cup]] final against Aberdeen.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/16188356.scottish-youth-cup-final-aberdeen-1-hibernian-3/ |first=Martin |last=McMillan |title=Scottish Youth Cup Final: Aberdeen 1 Hibernian 3 |date=27 April 2018 |accessdate=7 October 2018 |newspaper=The Herald }}</ref>

He made his first team debut for Hibernian in July 2018, in a [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League]] qualifier against Faroese club [[NSI Runavik]].<ref name = "debut">{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/jamie-gullan-brought-back-down-to-earth-after-hibs-debut-in-faroes-1-4773435 |title=Jamie Gullan brought back down to earth after Hibs debut in Faroes |first=David |last=Hardie |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=25 July 2018 |accessdate=7 October 2018}}</ref> In February 2019, Gullan was loaned to [[Scottish League One]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/9760 |title=JAMIE GULLAN SEALS RAITH ROVERS LOAN |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=28 February 2019 |accessdate=28 February 2019}}</ref> Gullan scored his first goal for Raith on 7 May 2019, in a playoff match against [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48165387 |title=Raith Rovers 2–1 Forfar Athletic |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=7 May 2019 |accessdate=8 May 2019 |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin}}</ref> He returned to Raith on loan in August 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49451651 |title=Melker Hallberg: Hibernian sign Swedish midfielder from Udinese |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=23 August 2019 |accessdate=23 August 2019}}</ref> Gullan scored nine goals for Raith during this second spell, which helped to put them top of the [[2019–20 Scottish League One]] table in early January.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50995343 |title=Scottish League One: Leaders Raith Rovers stay two points clear |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=4 January 2020 |accessdate=5 January 2020}}</ref> The clubs agreed to extend the loan by one week during January 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10490 |title=LOAN UPDATE: JAMIE GULLAN |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=6 January 2020 |accessdate=6 January 2020}}</ref>

Gullan returned to Hibs for the second part of the 2019–20 season, acting as cover for [[Christian Doidge]] and [[Marc McNulty]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-jamie-gullan-speaks-dislodging-strike-duo-and-changes-hes-had-make-raith-return-1888751 |title=Hibs' Jamie Gullan speaks on dislodging strike duo and changes he's had to make since Raith return |first=David |last=Hardie |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=25 February 2020 |accessdate=29 February 2020}}</ref> Gullan scored his first goal for Hibs on 28 February 2020, netting the fifth in a 5–2 Scottish Cup quarter-final win against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51585973 |title=Hibernian 5–2 Inverness Caledonian Thistle |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=28 February 2020 |accessdate=29 February 2020}}</ref>

On 1 February 2021, Gullan joined [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/46440/jamie-gullan-signs.htm|title=Jamie Gullan signs|publisher=Raith Rovers FC|date=1 February 2021|access-date=1 February 2021|archive-date=1 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201203239/https://www.raithrovers.net/46440/jamie-gullan-signs.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored two of the goals in a 5–1 [[Fife derby]] win against [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline]] on 30 March.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56205600 |title=Raith Rovers 5–1 Dunfermline |first=Andy |last=Campbell |website=BBC Sport |date=30 March 2021 |accessdate=31 March 2021}}</ref>

On 22 August 2021, Gullan made his first competitive appearance back at [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] following his loan spell with [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], he came off the bench in the game which saw [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] draw 2–2 with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] away from home.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58215736|title=Dundee 2–2 Hibernian|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Nick|last=McPheat|date=22 August 2021|access-date=22 August 2021}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===
On 6 January 2022, Gullan signed for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] permanently on a two-and-a-half-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/51948/jamie-gullan-signs-2.htm|title=Jamie Gullan|publisher=Raith Rovers FC|date=6 January 2022|access-date=6 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/transfer-jamie-gullan-joins-raith-rovers|title=Jamie Gullan Joins Raith Rovers|publisher=Hibernian FC|date=6 January 2022|access-date=6 January 2022}}</ref> He left for Irish side [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] in January 2024 for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jamie Gullan departs {{!}} Raith Rovers FC |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/67012/jamie-gullan-departs.htm |access-date=2024-01-26 |website=www.raithrovers.net|date=26 January 2024 }}</ref>

=== St Johnstone ===
On 30 May 2025, Gullan joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jamie Gullan signs for Saints! |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/ |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=St Johnstone Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

'''Ross MacIver''' (born 28 February 1999) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]. He previously played for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], and has spent time on loan at [[Wick Academy F.C.|Wick Academy]], [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]], [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] and [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]].

==Career==
===Ross County===
MacIver came through the Ross County Academy and was part of the Ross County Under-20s team that won the [[2016–17 SPFL Development League]] for the first time in the club's history. He made his first team debut in the [[2018–19 Scottish Challenge Cup]] third round against [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] coming on for the last 13 minutes of the match and taking home the man of the match reward for his outstanding efforts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/league/challenge-cup/results/1023436|title=Ross County Vs. Montrose|publisher=SPFL|accessdate=13 October 2018|date=13 October 2018}}</ref>

====Loans====
In January 2017, MacIver was loaned out to [[Highland Football League]] Club [[Wick Academy F.C.|Wick Academy]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wick-academy.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=2071&Itemid=9|title=Ross MacIver Signs Loan Deal|publisher=Wick Academy FC|accessdate=28 January 2017|date=28 January 2017}}</ref> On 26 January 2018, along with teammate [[Russell Dingwall]], he was loaned to [[Scottish League One]] team [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] until the end of the season. MacIver went on to score one goal in ten games for the club which caught the attention of premier league sides such as Aberdeen and Kilmarnock who were in desperate need of a predator type attacker.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/russell-dingwall-and-ross-MacIver-complete-loan-move-to-forfar/|title=Russell Dingwall and Ross MacIver complete loan move to Forfar|publisher=Ross County FC|accessdate=26 January 2018|date=26 January 2018|archive-date=30 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130013600/http://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/russell-dingwall-and-ross-maciver-complete-loan-move-to-forfar/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In February 2019, MacIver joined [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross MacIver loaned to Elgin City FC|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/ross-MacIver-loaned-to-elgin-city-fc/|publisher=Ross County F.C.|date=6 February 2019|accessdate=26 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=MacIver aims to grasp senior opportunity with Elgin|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/1685683/MacIver-aims-to-grasp-senior-opportunity-with-elgin/|publisher=The Press and Journal|last=Skinner|first=Andy|date=26 February 2019|accessdate=26 December 2019}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
Ahead of the [[2019–20 Motherwell F.C. season|2019–20 season]], having been released by Ross County, MacIver signed for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref name=profile>{{cite web|title=Ross MacIver player profile|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/player/ross-MacIver/|publisher=Motherwell F.C.|accessdate=26 December 2019}}</ref> He made his debut as a substitute on 26 December 2019, away to his former club Ross County, scoring Motherwell's equalising goal in a 2–1 win. This ended up being the only goal of his senior Motherwell career. In other performances he ran around efficiently which was highly commended by the Steelmen faithful .<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross County 1–2 Motherwell|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50847213|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Mullen|first=Scott|date=26 December 2019|accessdate=26 December 2019}}</ref>

MacIver joined [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on a season-long loan in September 2020,<ref>{{cite web|title=MORTON MOVE FOR MacIver|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/morton-move-for-MacIver|website=spfl.co.uk|date=22 September 2020|accessdate=14 October 2020}}</ref> but was recalled by Motherwell in January 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dodds |first1=Christopher |title=Morton loanee MacIver recalled by parent club Motherwell |url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/18998580.morton-loanee-maciver-recalled-parent-club-motherwell/ |access-date=17 January 2021 |work=Greenock Telegraph |date=8 January 2021}}</ref> He was then loaned to [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in March 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.motherwelltimes.co.uk/sport/football/international/yusuf-hussain-and-ross-maciver-depart-motherwell-until-summer-3165942 |title=Yusuf Hussain and Ross MacIver depart Motherwell until summer |newspaper=Motherwell Times |date=15 March 2021 |accessdate=15 March 2021 |first=Craig |last=Goldthorp}}</ref> MacIver scored his first goal for Thistle in a 2–0 win away to Dumbarton, which sent Thistle top of League One.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56220264|title=Dumbarton v Partick Thistle|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
MacIver joined Partick Thistle on a permanent basis after winning the League One title with the club, signing a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/new-signing-ross-maciver-joins-the-club/|title=Signing News: Ross MacIver joins the Club|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref> On 28 February 2022, MacIver joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] on loan for the remainder of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/ross-maciver-joins-alloa-athletic-on-loan-for-the-remainder-of-the-season/ |title=Ross MacIver joins Alloa Athletic on loan for the remainder of the season |publisher=Partick Thistle FC |date=28 February 2022 |accessdate=1 March 2022}}</ref>

===Alloa Athletic===
After a successful loan spell MacIver joined [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] on a permanent deal after being released by [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.alloaadvertiser.com/sport/20163653.ross-maciver-joins-alloa-brian-rice-continues-summer-business/|title=Ross MacIver joins Alloa as Brian Rice continues summer business |publisher=Alloa Adviser|date=25 May 2022|accessdate=25 May 2022}}</ref>

===Falkirk===
MacIver joined Falkirk on a two year deal in May 2023.<ref>https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2023/05/25/ross-maciver-joins-the-bairns/#:~:text=The%2024%2Dyear%2Dold%20striker,Wasps%20and%20scoring%20seven%20goals.</ref> After winning the League One title with Falkirk, MacIver signed a two year contract extension with the club.<ref>https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/08/13/ross-maciver-extends-deal/</ref>

'''Ethan Billy Hamilton''' (born 18 October 1998) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

==Club career==
Hamilton began his career with [[Edinburgh]]-based club [[Hutchison Vale F.C.|Hutchison Vale]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Ethan Hamilton makes the United bench |url=https://www.hutchisonvale.com/club-news/ethan-hamilton-makes-united-bench/ |website=hutchisonvale.com |publisher=Hutchison Vale Community Sports Club |date=18 February 2018 |access-date=13 January 2019 }}</ref> the same club that [[Darren Fletcher]] (who also later played for Manchester United) began his career at.<ref name="MUFC">[https://www.manutd.com/en/players-and-staff/detail/ethan-hamilton Profile] ManUtd.com</ref>

Hamilton played several matches for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]'s under-18s team during the 2014–15 season, before signing for the club as an academy scholar in July 2015, when he was 16 years old.<ref name="MUFC"/> Hamilton was a regular for the Manchester United Under-18s in the first half of the 2015–16 season, but did not play at all in the second half of the season.<ref name="MUFC"/> He returned to the team for the 2016–17 season, when, despite not finding the back of the net until December, he finished as the team's third-highest goalscorer, with 8 goals in 23 appearances; he also played eight times for the club's reserve team that season, before making the regular step up for the 2017–18 season.<ref name="MUFC"/> He made 22 appearances for the reserves that season, his performances earning him a call-up to the first team in February 2018, after [[Paul Pogba]] was ruled out of the club's [[2017–18 FA Cup|FA Cup fifth round]] tie against [[Huddersfield Town F.C.|Huddersfield Town]];<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Froggatt |title=Pogba replaced by Hamilton for Huddersfield tie |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/paul-pogba-replaced-by-ethan-hamilton-for-match-at-huddersfield |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=17 February 2018 |access-date=13 January 2019 }}</ref> Hamilton was assigned the number 48 shirt and named as a substitute, but did not play in the game.<ref>{{cite news |first=Gary |last=Rose |title=Huddersfield Town 0–2 Manchester United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43012781 |website=BBC Sport |date=17 February 2018 |access-date=13 January 2019 }}</ref> At the end of the season, Hamilton was nominated alongside [[Demetri Mitchell]] and [[Kieran O'Hara]] for the Denzil Haroun Reserve Team Player of the Year award, given to Manchester United's best reserve team player of the season; the award was ultimately won by Mitchell.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Mitchell scoops Reserves award |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/demi-mitchell-wins-denzil-haroun-reserves-player-of-the-year-award-for-2017-18 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=1 May 2018 |access-date=13 January 2019 }}</ref>

Ahead of the 2018–19 season, Hamilton signed his first professional contract with Manchester United,<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Hamilton signs new deal with United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/ethan-hamilton-signs-new-contract-with-man-united |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=11 July 2018 |access-date=13 January 2019 }}</ref> before being named as part of the squad for the club's pre-season tour of the United States.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=The United prospects with a chance to shine on tour |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/opinion-adam-marshall-profiles-the-young-man-united-players-on-tour-2018 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=17 July 2018 |access-date=13 January 2019 }}</ref> He made one appearance on the tour, coming on as an 89th-minute substitute for [[Juan Mata]] in a game against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] on 26 July. The match finished 1–1 after 90 minutes and went straight to [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]]; with the score at 6–6 after nine kicks each, Hamilton saw his penalty saved by [[Pepe Reina]], only for [[José Mauri]] to also miss. United went on to win the shoot-out 9–8 after 13 kicks each.<ref>{{cite web |title=Milan 1(8)-1(9) Manchester United |url=https://www.internationalchampionscup.com/en/protected/matches/05c9f0d35adacec6c32cb42b#tab_match-pitch=formation&tab_match=play-by-play |website=internationalchampionscup.com |publisher=International Champions Cup |access-date=13 January 2019 }}</ref> Hamilton made 14 appearances for the Manchester United reserves in the first half of the 2018–19 season, before moving on loan to [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] in January 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rochdale sign Ethan Ebanks-Landell and Ethan Hamilton on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46838461 |website=BBC Sport |date=11 January 2019 |access-date=11 January 2019 }}</ref>

For the 2019–20 season, Hamilton joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]] on loan.<ref>{{cite news |title=Man Utd midfielder Ethan Hamilton joins Southend on loan |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/ethan-hamilton-joins-southend-united-on-loan-for-2019-20-season |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=16 August 2019 |access-date=16 August 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Ethan Hamilton: Man Utd midfielder joins Southend United on loan for the season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49374677 |website=BBC Sport |date=16 August 2019 |access-date=16 August 2019 }}</ref> He scored his first goal for Southend when he scored in an [[EFL Trophy]] tie against [[AFC Wimbledon]] on 13 November 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50412766 |title=Leasing.com Trophy: Top-tier academy sides flourish as group stages finish|date=14 November 2019 |website=BBC |access-date=14 November 2019}}</ref> His spell with Southend came to an end when he was recalled by Manchester United on 3 January 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/ethan-hamilton-returns-to-man-united-from-southend-loan-spell |title=Hamilton returns from loan spell at Southend |date=3 January 2020 |website=Manutd.com |access-date=3 January 2020}}</ref>

Three days later, Hamilton joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] on another loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ethan Hamilton Signs For The Whites |url=https://www.bwfc.co.uk/news/2020/january/ethan-hamilton-signs-for-the-whites/ |website=bwfc.co.uk |publisher=Bolton Wanderers |date=6 January 2020 |access-date=6 January 2020 }}</ref>

He was released by Manchester United at the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=United issue update on Academy squads |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-under-23s-and-under-18s-retained-and-released-list-for-2020 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=25 June 2020 |access-date=4 July 2020 }}</ref> He signed for [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] in August 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53769247|title=Ethan Hamilton: Peterborough United sign former Manchester United midfielder|work=BBC Sport |date=13 August 2020}}</ref> He scored his first and only goal for Peterborough in an [[EFL Trophy]] tie against [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on 12 January 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.portsmouthfc.co.uk/news/2021/january/match-report-for-peterborough-united-vs-portsmouth-on-12-jan-21/ |title=Peterborough 5 Pompey 1 |date=12 January 2021|publisher=portsmouthfc.co.uk |access-date=17 January 2021 }}</ref>

On 31 August 2021, Hamilton joined [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.accringtonstanley.co.uk/news/2021/august/signing-hamilton-agrees-a-two-year-deal/ |title=SIGNING: Hamilton agrees a two-year deal |date=31 August 2021|publisher=accringtonstanley.co.uk |access-date=31 August 2021 }}</ref> He made his Accrington debut on 4 September, appearing as a substitute alongside [[Jovan Malcolm]], also making his debut.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/19559521.accrington-stanley-boss-john-coleman-not-getting-carried-away-shrewsbury-win/|title=Stanley boss John Coleman not getting carried away after Shrewsbury win|website=Lancashire Telegraph |date=4 September 2021 }}</ref>

On 1 August 2023, Hamilton joined [[Lincoln City F.C.|Lincoln City]] for an undisclosed fee, signing a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=Imps seal exciting midfielder Hamilton|url=https://www.weareimps.com/news/2023/august/imps-seal-exciting-midfielder-hamilton/|access-date=1 August 2023 |publisher=Lincoln City FC|date=1 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Lincoln City sign Accrington Stanley midfielder on three-year deal|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66371316|access-date=1 August 2023 |publisher=BBC|date=1 August 2023}}</ref> On 5 August 2023, he made his Lincoln City debut starting against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.weareimps.com/news/2023/august/bolton-wanderers-imps/|title=Bolton Wanderers 3 Imps 0|website=www.weareimps.com|date=5 August 2023|accessdate=5 August 2023}}</ref> His first Lincoln goal was the winner in a 1–0 victory against [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] on 19 August 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.weareimps.com/news/2023/august/shrewsbury-town-imps/|title=Shrewsbury Town 0 Imps 1|website=www.weareimps.com|date=19 August 2023|accessdate=19 August 2023}}</ref> On 29 February, manager [[Michael Skubala]] confirmed that Hamilton would be out for the season following a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68438182|title=Lincoln City midfielder ruled out for rest of season|website=BBC|date=19 February 2024|accessdate=3 March 2024}}</ref> He returned to the side on 5 October 2024 following his long term injury, coming off the bench against [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.weareimps.com/news/imps-2-leyton-orient-1|title=Imps 2–1 Leyton Orient|website=Lincoln City FC|date=5 October 2024|accessdate=6 October 2024}}</ref>

On 26 August 2025, Hamilton joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a three-year deal from Lincoln City for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hamilton arrives at the Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/hamilton-arrives/ |access-date=26 August 2025 |publisher=Dundee FC |date=26 August 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Hamilton first played for Scotland at under-15 level, appearing in friendly matches against Germany, Italy and Russia in March 2013.<ref name="SFA"/> He also made a single appearance for the [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scotland U16 side]] in August that year, playing the first 40 minutes of a match against [[Cyprus national under-16 football team|Cyprus]].<ref name="SFA"/> In 2017, he was selected to play for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19 side]] in their [[2017 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification|UEFA European Under-19 Championship elite round]] qualifying matches against [[Austria national under-19 football team|Austria]], the [[Czech Republic national under-19 football team|Czech Republic]] and [[Hungary national under-19 football team|Hungary]].<ref name="SFA">{{SFA|184291}}</ref>

'''Ethan Ross''' (born 15 August 2001) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]. He has previously played for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and had previous loan spells at [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] and [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].

==Career==
===Aberdeen===

Ross joined [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] when he was 10 years old,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.afc.co.uk/2019/01/04/ethan-ross-red-matchday-feature/|title=Ethan Ross Red Matchday Feature|publisher=Aberdeen FC|date=4 January 2019|accessdate=28 March 2019}}</ref><ref>[http://www.afc.co.uk/u20_player/ethan-ross/ Ethan Ross] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190902183957/https://www.afc.co.uk/u20_player/ethan-ross/ |date=2 September 2019 }} Aberdeen FC</ref> and was the captain of their Under-18 side. He made his first team debut for Aberdeen on 29 January 2019, coming off the bench at [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] in a [[Scottish Cup]] replay.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stenhousemuir 1-4 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46955341|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|date=29 January 2019|access-date=28 March 2019}}</ref> On 9 March 2019, he made his league debut, again coming off the bench in an away match against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Celtic 0-0 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47424791|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|date=9 March 2019|access-date=28 March 2019}}</ref> He signed a new two-year contract in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ethan Ross Signs on for another two years|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2019/05/17/ethan-ross-signs-on-for-another-two-years/|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|date=17 May 2019|accessdate=17 May 2019}}</ref>

Ross joined [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on loan in January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=First_signing_of_2020&ID=11654|title=First signing of 2020|last=|first=|date=3 January 2020|website=Dunfermline Athletic FC|access-date=3 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/1931500/aberdeens-ethan-ross-heads-to-dunfermline-on-loan/ |title=Aberdeen's Ethan Ross heads to Dunfermline on loan |last=Cryle |first=Ryan |date=3 January 2020 |newspaper=Press & Journal |accessdate=3 January 2020 |publisher=DC Thomson}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===

In October 2020, Ross signed for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/44980/ethan-ross-signs.html|title=Ethan Ross signs|last=|first=|date=2 October 2020|website=Raith Rovers FC|access-date=2 October 2020}}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> He was recalled by Aberdeen in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/2854015/birmingham-city-launch-2-million-bid-for-aberdeen-striker-sam-cosgrove/|title=Birmingham City 'launch £2 million bid for Aberdeen striker Sam Cosgrove'|last=Cryle|first=Ryan|date=29 January 2021|website=Press & Journal|access-date=1 February 2021}}</ref> Ross was offered a new contract by Aberdeen, but he decided to leave the club at the end of the 2020/21 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/3256294/ethan-ross-decides-not-to-return-to-aberdeen/ |title=Ethan Ross decides not to return to Aberdeen|first=Paul|last=Third|date=22 June 2021|accessdate=1 July 2021|newspaper=Press & Journal}}</ref>

On 14 October 2021, Ross signed for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a permanent deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/50575/new-signing.html|title=Ethan Ross|website=Raith Rovers FC|date=14 October 2021|accessdate=19 November 2021}}</ref> Having failed to sign a contract at [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] and agreeing a compensation fee with former club Aberdeen, he became an "immediate impact" at Raith scoring three goals in his first six matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/2743440/ethan-ross-john-mcglynn-aberdeen-raith-rovers/|title=Ethan Ross delivers 'pleasant surprise' as John McGlynn hails ex-Aberdeen starlet's blistering start to life at Raith Rovers|website=The Courier|date=18 November 2021|accessdate=19 November 2021}}</ref>

===Falkirk===

In 2023, he joined [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on a season-long loan deal, won [[Scottish League One]] and then signed on a permanent deal in June 2024.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/06/04/ethan-ross-signs/ | title=ETHAN ROSS SIGNS! - Falkirk Football Club | date=4 June 2024 }}</ref>

'''Morgan Marc Boyes''' (born 22 April 2001) is a Welsh professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. Mainly a [[centre-back]], he can also play as a [[left-back]]. He is a former Wales under-21 international.

==Early life==
Boyes was born in the Welsh city of [[St Asaph]] and moved to [[Chester]] in England at the age of five.<ref name=BBCpro>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54467576|title=Morgan Boyes: Liverpool and Wales youngster aims to follow Neco Williams' lead|first=Gareth|last=Vincent|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=9 October 2020|access-date=1 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.leaderlive.co.uk/news/17682166.liverpool-fc-academy-climbs-mount-snowdon-stephen-darby-foundation/|title=Liverpool FC Academy climbs Mount Snowdon for Stephen Darby Foundation|first=Keiran|last=Samra|newspaper=[[The Leader (Welsh newspaper)|The Leader]]|date=4 June 2019|access-date=1 June 2021}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Liverpool===
Boyes made his professional debut for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on 17 December 2019, starting in the away match against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in the [[2019–20 EFL Cup#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] of the [[EFL Cup]], which finished as a 5–0 loss. He scored an own goal in the match, after blocking a ball from [[Ahmed Elmohamady]], to find it looped over the goalkeeper's head into the corner of the net.<ref name="SW">{{Soccerway}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/dec/17/aston-villa-liverpool-carabao-cup-match-report |title=Aston Villa's Jonathan Kodjia shows no mercy to knock out Liverpool's kids |author=Paul Doyle |newspaper=The Guardian|date=17 December 2019|accessdate=19 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50723225 |title=Aston Villa 5 – Liverpool 0 |author=Simon Stone |publisher=BBC |date=17 December 2019|accessdate=19 December 2019}}</ref> Boyes made another appearance for Liverpool in the 2019–20 season, as he appeared in stoppage time against [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] in the fourth round replay of the [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]].<ref name=BBCpro />

On 12 August 2020, Boyes joined [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 August 2020 |title=Morgan Boyes: Fleetwood Town sign young Liverpool defender on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53756235 |access-date=12 August 2020 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-gb}}</ref> On 23 September, he made his debut for the Cod Army. Starting at left centre-back in a [[2020–21 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] Third round tie against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]. He played the full match in a 2–5 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2020/09/liverpool-loanee-given-tough-start-as-senior-debut-ends-in-defeat-to-everton/ |title=Liverpool loanee given tough start as senior debut ends in defeat to Everton |first=Jack |last=Lusby |work=This is Anfield.com |date=24 September 2020 |accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref> He made kept his place in the squad for the next game. A 0–1 defeat against [[AFC Wimbledon]] in the [[2020–21 EFL League One|League One]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54215155 |title=Fleetwood Town 0-1 AFC Wimbledon |work=BBC Sport |date=26 September 2020 |accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref> However, he would only make two more appearances before being recalled by Liverpool on 2 January 2021.<ref name="Fleetwood">{{cite web |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=123802&season_id=153 |title=Games played by Morgan Boyes in the 2020/21 season |website=Soccerbase.com |accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Morgan Boyes returns from loan spell at Fleetwood Town |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/academy/421838-morgan-boyes-returns-from-loan-spell-at-fleetwood-town? |access-date=2 January 2021 |publisher=Liverpool FC |date=2 January 2021}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 4 January 2022, Boyes joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on an 18-month contract, with an option of a further year.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Black|first=Dave|date=2022-01-04|title=Morgan Boyes joins the Lions from Liverpool.|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/morgan-boyes-joins-the-lions-from-liverpool/|access-date=2022-01-04|website=Livingston FC|language=en-GB}}</ref>

====Inverness====
On 1 September 2023 Boyes joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Inverness CT|Inverness]] on a loan deal till the end of the 2023/24 season.

===Greenock Morton===
Following his departure from Livi, Boyes signed for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=6 July 2024|title=Defender is third former Inverness Caley Thistle player to join same Championship club this summer|url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/defender-is-third-former-caley-thistle-player-to-join-same-c-355039/|website=inverness-courier.co.uk}}</ref>

=== St Johnstone ===
On 29 May 2025, Boyes signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Morgan Boyes signs for Saints! |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/ |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=St Johnstone Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Boyes has Wales caps at both under-19 and under-21 levels. In March 2021, he was called up to the [[Wales national under-21 football team]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.faw.cymru/en/news/u21-squad-announced-face-republic-ireland/ |title=U21 squad announced to face Republic of Ireland |publisher=Football Association of Wales |date=16 March 2021 |accessdate=16 March 2021 }}</ref><ref>[https://twitter.com/Cymru/status/1371792612982624257 Wales U21 squad]</ref> playing all 90 minutes in Wales's 2–1 defeat by [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Ireland]] at Colliers Park, [[Wrexham]] on 26 March 2021.<ref name="FAW-26Mar2021">{{cite web |title=FRUSTRATION FOR CYMRU U21 IN IRISH DEFEAT |url=https://www.faw.cymru/en/news/frustration-cymru-u21-irish-defeat/?back=/en/news/&pos=28 |website=FAW |access-date=20 April 2021}}</ref> Manager [[Paul Bodin]] then selected a largely unchanged squad, including Boyes, for the side's [[2023 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification|Euro 2023 qualifying game]] against [[Moldova national under-21 football team|Moldova]] on 4 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=CYMRU U21 SQUAD ANNOUNCED TO FACE MOLDOVA |url=https://www.faw.cymru/en/news/cymru-u21-squad-announced-face-moldova/?back=/en/news/&pos=11 |website=FAW |access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Boyes is a centre-back but has also been deployed as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left back]] so far during his career.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/team/academy/player/morgan-boyes |title=Player profile: Morgan Boyes |publisher=Liverpool FC |accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref> He has described himself as a "calm defender who likes to play and build up from the back.".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fleetwoodtownfc.com/news/2020/august/boyes-i-want-to-get-going-straight-away/ |title=Boyes: I want to get going straight away |publisher=Fleetwood Town FC |date=12 August 2020 |accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref> [[Joey Barton]], who managed Boyes during his loan spell at Fleetwood, described him as "a young player with plenty of potential".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fleetwoodtownfc.com/news/2020/august/liverpool-youngster-boyes-joins-town/ |title=Liverpool youngster Boyes joins Town |publisher=Fleetwood Town FC |date=12 August 2020 |accessdate=22 September 2021}}</ref>

'''Daniel Finlayson''' (born 19 January 2001) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who last played for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

==Career==
===Rangers===
Finlayson came through the youth system at [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. In February 2020 he moved on loan to [[USL Championship]] club [[Orange County SC|Orange County]] alongside [[Cammy Palmer]] and Matthew Shiels, as part of a partnership between Rangers and Orange County.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.angelsonparade.com/2020/2/3/21115809/transfer-news-rangers-fc-loan-cammy-palmer-matthew-shiels-danny-finlayson-to-orange-county-sc|title=Rangers FC loan Cammy Palmer, Matthew Shiels, Danny Finlayson to Orange County SC|website=angelsonparade.com|date=3 February 2020|accessdate=16 July 2020|archive-date=27 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210927134935/https://www.angelsonparade.com/2020/2/3/21115809/transfer-news-rangers-fc-loan-cammy-palmer-matthew-shiels-danny-finlayson-to-orange-county-sc|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his league debut for the club on 16 July 2020 against [[Phoenix Rising FC|Phoenix Rising]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2020/07/17/united-states/mls-reserve-league/los-angeles-blues-sc/arizona-united/3284048/|title=Orange County SC vs. Phoenix Rising – 16 July 2020 – Soccerway|website=int.soccerway.com|accessdate=16 July 2020}}</ref>

=== St Mirren ===
On 5 October 2020, Finlayson returned to Scotland to join [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a season-long loan deal with an option to buy for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/3784-daniel-finlayson-joins-on-season-long-loan|title=Daniel Finlayson joins on season-long loan|website=www.stmirren.com|date=5 October 2020}}</ref> St Mirren announced on 21 May 2021 that they had exercised this option and had signed Finlayson to a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=2020/21 SQUAD UPDATE |url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/3990-2020-21-squad-update |publisher=St Mirren FC |date=21 May 2021 |access-date=23 May 2021}}</ref> He was loaned to [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] in October 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/news/19618297.kelty-hearts-daniel-finlayson-signs-loan-st-mirren/ |title=Kelty Hearts: Daniel Finlayson signs on loan from St Mirren |first=Ross |last=Hart |newspaper=Dunfermline Press |date=1 October 2021 |accessdate=4 February 2022}}</ref>

=== Linfield ===
In June 2022, Finlayson moved on loan to [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]] until the end of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4455-daniel-finlayson-joins-linfield-on-loan|title=DANIEL FINLAYSON JOINS LINFIELD ON LOAN|website=stmirren.com|accessdate=9 June 2022}}</ref> It was agreed in April 2023 that the move would be made on a permanent basis.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4916-daniel-finlayson-joins-linfield-on-permanent-deal |title=Daniel Finlayson joins Linfield on permanent deal |website=stmirren.com |date=25 April 2023 |accessdate=7 July 2023}}</ref>

=== Livingston ===

Finlayson departed Linfield at the end of his contract, and on 13 May 2024, it was announced that Finlayson had signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], linking up with former Linfield team-mate [[Matthew Clarke (footballer, born 1994)|Matthew Clarke]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Daniel Finlayson becomes signing number five |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/daniel-finlayson-becomes-signing-number-five/ |website=Livingston FC |access-date=17 February 2026}}</ref> During his first season with the Lions, the club successfully won promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]] through the [[2024-25 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|play-offs]]. Finlayson played in 38 of 40 possible games in the league, with 22 starts and 16 substitute appearances, featuring in all four play-off fixtures. Livingston also won the [[2024-25 Scottish Challenge Cup|Challenge Cup]], with Finlayson appearing from the bench during a 5-0 win in the final against [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]. During the 2025-26 season Finlayson became a more regular starter and played 90 minutes in 33 of Livingston's matches.<ref>{{cite web |title=Games played by Daniel Finlayson in 2025/2026 |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=107111&season_id=158 |website=Soccerbase |access-date=17 February 2026}}</ref>

After Livingston were relegated from the Premiership in the 2025-26 season, Finlayson left the club following the expiration of his contract and joined St Johnstone.<ref>{{cite web |title=Squad Update – Retained & Released List|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-retained-released-list/|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=19 May 2026}}</ref>

=== St Johnstone ===
Finlayson signed a two-year contract with St Johnstone on 20 May 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 May 2026 |title=Daniel Finlayson signs for Saints! |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/daniel-finlayson-signs-for-saints/ |access-date=17 August 2026 |website=St Johnstone FC}}</ref>

'''Lewis Neilson''' (born 15 May 2003) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], primarily as a [[centre back]] or [[defensive midfielder]].

Neilson has previously played for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], as well as on loan for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

==Club career==
===Dundee United===
Neilson joined [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] at the age of 10 and signed his first professional contract with the club in the summer of 2019, before extending the contract until 2022 the following March.<ref name="new-contract">{{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6454/LEWIS-NEILSON-SIGNS-A-NEW-CONTRACT.html|title=LEWIS NEILSON SIGNS A NEW CONTRACT|publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.]]|date=10 March 2020|accessdate=26 August 2020}}</ref> After graduating from the club's academy,<ref name="new-contract"/> he made his professional debut in a 1–1 draw against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on the opening day of the [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership]] season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53535018|title=Dundee Utd 1-1 St Johnstone: Liam Craig earns a point for 10-man visitors|work=BBC Sport|date=August 1, 2020}}</ref> Neilson was loaned to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in March 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2040094/dundee-united-youngsters-kai-fotheringham-and-lewis-neilson-join-falkirk-on-loan-until-the-end-of-the-season/ |title=Dundee United youngsters Kai Fotheringham and Lewis Neilson join Falkirk on loan until the end of the season |first=Calum |last=Woodger |date=12 March 2021 |accessdate=15 March 2021}}</ref>

Following his return from loan, Neilson sustained an ankle injury, for which he required surgery. He did not appear in the United first team again until December 2021 when he started against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2867754/lewis-neilson-targets-big-year-2022-dundee-united/|title = Lewis Neilson targets 'big year' in 2022 after making first Dundee United start in five months| date=30 December 2021 }}</ref> Neilson departed United in June 2022 after turning down a new contract offer.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7333/LEWIS-NEILSON-TO-LEAVE-DUNDEE-UNITED.html | title=Lewis Neilson to Leave Dundee United }}</ref>

===Hearts===
After leaving Dundee United, Neilson signed a three-year contract with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61745096 |title=Hearts sign Australia defender Kye Rowles & Lewis Neilson from Dundee Utd |website=BBC Sport |date=9 June 2022 |accessdate=9 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/lewis-neilson-completes-hearts-transfer-27189830 | title=Lewis Neilson seals Hearts transfer as Dundee United defender pens 3-year deal | date=9 June 2022 }}</ref> In his first season with Hearts, he made 16 first-team appearances. But he did not feature in the final months and spent time involved with the club's [[Heart of Midlothian F.C. Reserves and Academy|B team]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=Lewis Neilson's future is made clear as the Hearts defender looks to further his career {{!}} Edinburgh News | date=29 May 2023 | url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/lewis-neilsons-future-is-made-clear-as-the-hearts-defender-looks-to-further-his-career-4161675 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529153057/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/lewis-neilsons-future-is-made-clear-as-the-hearts-defender-looks-to-further-his-career-4161675 | access-date=2025-05-17 | archive-date=2023-05-29}}</ref>

==== Partick Thistle (loan) ====
On 3 August 2023, Neilson joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lewis Neilson signs on loan for the season |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/lewis-neilson-signs-on-loan-for-the-season/ |access-date=2023-08-04 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

Neilson scored the first goal of his professional career on 2 January 2024, scoring the winner for Thistle with a header from a corner, in a 3–2 home win over Queens Park.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67821091 | title=Partick Thistle 3-2 Queen's Park: Visitors remain three points adrift | work=BBC Sport | date=2 January 2024 }}</ref>

Neilson played the first half of the season as a centre back for Thistle, before moving into a defensive midfielder role for the second half of the campaign.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Premiership club make their move for versatile Hearts defender Lewis Neilson | date=25 July 2024 | url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/premiership-club-make-their-move-for-versatile-hearts-defender-lewis-neilson-4716171 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725184609/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/premiership-club-make-their-move-for-versatile-hearts-defender-lewis-neilson-4716171 | access-date=2025-05-17 | archive-date=2024-07-25}}</ref>

==== St Johnstone (loan) ====
On 30 July 2024, Neilson joined {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on loan for the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lewis Neilson signs for Saints |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/lewis-neilson-signs-for-saints |access-date=2024-07-31 |website=St Johnstone Football Club |language=en}}</ref> Neilson was recalled early from his loan at St Johnstone, by his parent club Hearts on 1 January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Lewis Neilson returns to Hearts | url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/lewis-neilson-returns-to-hearts | access-date=2025-05-17 | website=www.heartsfc.co.uk}}</ref>

==International career==
Neilson has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=283917&lid=17|title=Lewis Neilson Scotland Scottish FA|website=scottishfa.co.uk|accessdate=26 August 2020}}</ref>

In September 2022, Neilson was called up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] for friendlies against [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland under-21]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scot-gemmill-names-squad-for-northern-ireland-double-header/ | title=Scot Gemmill names squad for Northern Ireland double header }}</ref>
