'''Callum Graham Jones''' (born 5 April 2001) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]. He is a former Wales under-18 international.

==Early career==
Jones is a youth product of [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]], [[The New Saints F.C.|The New Saints]], [[F.C. Oswestry Town|Oswestry Town]], and [[Bury F.C.|Bury]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oncloudseven.com/1089-callum-jones/|title=1089 Callum Jones – On Cloud Seven|accessdate=16 September 2020}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Hull City===
On 17 October 2019, Jones signed a professional contract with [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] for one year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hulldailymail.co.uk/sport/football/hull-city-u23s-callum-jones-3437845|title=Why Hull City have tied down promising teenager Callum Jones|first=Jonty|last=Colman|date=17 October 2019|website=HullLive|accessdate=16 September 2020}}</ref> Jones made his professional debut with Hull in a 2–1 [[EFL Trophy]] defeat to [[Leicester City F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Leicester City U21s]] on 8 September 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hullcitytigers.com/news/2020/september/hull-city-1-2-leicester-city-u21s-efl-trophy-match-report/|title=Hull City 1–2 Leicester City U21s: Match Report|publisher=Hull City A.F.C. |accessdate=11 November 2020}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club, also in the EFL Trophy, in a 2–0 win over [[Harrogate Town A.F.C.|Harrogate Town]] on 10 November 2020, where he was also captain.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hulldailymail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/harrogate-town-hull-city-ratings-4688644|title=Callum Jones and Martin Samuelsen shine in deserving Hull City win at Harrogate Town – ratings|work=Hull Daily Mail |accessdate=11 November 2020}}</ref> On 6 January 2021, Jones signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with Hull City.<ref>{{cite news
 | url = https://www.hullcitytigers.com/news/2021/january/callum-jones-signs-new-contract/
 | title = Callum Jones Signs New Contract
 | date = 6 January 2021
 | publisher = Hull City A.F.C.
 | accessdate = 6 January 2021
 | archive-date = 8 January 2021
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210108050902/https://www.hullcitytigers.com/news/2021/january/callum-jones-signs-new-contract/
 | url-status = dead
 }}</ref> On 27 January 2023, Jones signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with Hull City.<ref>{{cite news | url = https://www.wearehullcity.co.uk/news/2023/january/callum-jones-pens-new-contract/ | title = Callum Jones pens new contract | date = 27 January 2023 | publisher = Hull City A.F.C. | accessdate = 27 January 2023}}</ref>

====Morecambe (loan)====
On 16 June 2021, Jones signed a season long loan deal with [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Loan Deal: Callum Jones |url=https://www.morecambefc.com/news/2021/june/loan-deal--callum-jones/ |accessdate=16 June 2021 |publisher=[[Morecambe F.C.]] |date=16 June 2021}}</ref> On 18 January 2022, Jones was recalled by Hull City.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.morecambefc.com/news/2022/january/callum-jones-recalled-by-hull-city/|title=Callum Jones recalled by Hull City|website=www.morecambefc.com|date=18 January 2022|accessdate=18 January 2022}}</ref>

====Grimsby Town (loan)====
On 5 March 2022, Jones signed a month-long loan deal with [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]]. 
He made his debut the same day in a 1–0 victory at [[Blundell Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gtfc.co.uk/mariners-secure-jones-loan/|title=Mariners Secure Jones Loan|publisher=Grimsby Town F.C.|date=5 March 2022|accessdate=5 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.grimsbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/grimsby-town-transfer-dilemma-progress-6832296|title=Paul Hurst handed transfer dilemma as Grimsby Town progress underlined|date=20 March 2022|work=Grimsby Telegraph|accessdate=21 March 2022}}</ref>

On 20 March 2022, following an injury which would rule him out for the rest of the season, Jones returned to Hull City.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.grimsbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/grimsby-town-transfer-verdict-injury-6834098|title=Paul Hurst delivers Grimsby Town transfer verdict after Callum Jones injury blow|date=21 March 2022|work=Grimsby Telegraph|accessdate=21 March 2022}}</ref>

====Forest Green Rovers (loan)====
On 30 June 2023, Jones signed for recently relegated [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fgr.co.uk/news/jones-joins-fgr-on-loan|title=Jones joins FGR on loan|website=www.fgr.co.uk|date=30 June 2023|accessdate=30 June 2023}}</ref>

====Morecambe (loan)====
On 12 July 2024, Jones joined [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite news |url = https://www.wearehullcity.co.uk/news/2024/july/12/jones-joins-morecambe-on-loan/ |title = Jones joins Morecambe on loan |date = 12 July 2024 |publisher = Hull City A.F.C. |accessdate = 12 July 2024}}</ref> On 17 May 2025, Hull City confirmed that Jones would depart the club after the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 May 2025 |title=Retained List: 2024/25 |url=https://www.wearehullcity.co.uk/news/2025/may/17/retained-list-2024-25/ |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=www.wearehullcity.co.uk}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 15 July 2025, Jones joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-15 |title=Jones is a Dark Blue |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/jones-signs/ |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Jones made his debut on 22 July 2025, in an away League Cup victory against [[Bonnyrigg Rose F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bonnyrigg Rose vs Dundee: Premier Sports Cup score updates & report, BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cr79k93844zt |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 20 September, Jones scored his first goal for the ''Dee'', coming on as a substitute and scoring a stoppage time penalty to give Dundee their first league win of the season at home to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee 3-2 Livingston: 97th-minute penalty earns Pressley's side first league win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cq5j48e2x58t |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Born in England, Jones is of Welsh descent through a grandmother. He is a youth international for Wales, having first represented the [[Wales national under-18 football team|Wales U18]]s in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tnsfc.co.uk/2018/05/26/callum-jones-caps-a-great-season-with-wales/|title=Callum Jones Caps a great season with Wales|website=tnsfc.co.uk|date=26 May 2018 |accessdate=16 September 2020}}</ref>

'''Harrison Sharp''' (born 4 April 2001) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{soccerbase|114944|accessdate=19 October 2020}}</ref>

== Club career ==
Sharp made his debut for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] coming off the bench in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] against [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], after keeper [[Calum Ferrie]] was sent off during the game.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Robertson|first=Neil|date=8 September 2019|title=Dundee 1 Elgin City 2: Ten-man Dark Blues suffer huge cup upset against League 2 part-timers|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/974331/dundee-1-elgin-city-2-dark-blues-suffer-huge-cup-upset-against-league-2-part-timers/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=19 October 2020|website=thecourier.co.uk}}</ref>

In October 2020, Sharp joined [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=9 October 2020|title=Harry joins Edinburgh City on loan|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/harry-joins-edinburgh-city-on-loan/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=19 October 2020|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref>

On 7 January 2021, Sharp signed a two-year extension with Dundee, keeping him at the club until 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=7 January 2021|title=Harry signs new deal|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/harry-signs-new-deal/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=7 January 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref> In December 2021, he was listed as an outfield substitute for a Dundee game away to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] due to a combined injury and [[COVID-19]] crisis within the squad, though spent the entire game on the bench.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mair|first=Steven|date=2021-12-26|title=Dundee bench consists of assistant manager, two goalkeepers and a teenager|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/farcical-dundee-bench-consists-assistant-25788506|access-date=2021-12-26|website=Daily Record|language=en}}</ref> He made his first start for Dundee in a draw away to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee dig in for Motherwell draw |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60534423 |access-date=2022-03-05}}</ref> He made six further starts that season, including in a 3–1 victory at home to Hibernian.

Sharp began the [[2022–23 Dundee F.C. season|2022–23 season]] as first choice goalkeeper, starting all four [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage matches. He also started the season as Dundee's starting keeper, before being dropped to the bench in September.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Harper scores brace as Inverness beat Dundee |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62859925 |access-date=2023-04-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee win adds to struggling Hamilton's woes |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63018085 |access-date=2023-04-26}}</ref> He won the [[Scottish Championship]] with Dundee at the end of the season.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>

On 2 June 2023, Dundee announced that Sharp had signed a new two-year contract, keeping him there until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-02 |title=Sharp extends stay |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/sharp-extends-stay/ |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> On 3 August, he joined Scottish Championship club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a loan until January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scott |first=Douglas |date=2023-08-03 |title=Harry Sharp joins Dunfermline {{!}} Dunfermline Athletic Football Club - |url=https://dafc.co.uk/harry-sharp-joins-dunfermline/ |access-date=2023-08-03 |website=Dunfermline Athletic Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his debut two days later in a league win over [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dunfermline edge fellow new boys Airdrieonians |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66194516 |access-date=2023-08-05}}</ref> Sharp was recalled by Dundee on 18 January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-18 |title=Sharp and Wilkie back from loans |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/sharp-wilkie-back/ |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> He came on as a substitute two days later to replace [[Adam Legzdins]] in the [[Scottish Cup]] game away to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kilmarnock v Dundee |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67938501 |access-date=2024-01-20 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his first start of the season for Dundee the next week, and played well including saving a penalty in an away league victory over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], which saw him named to the [[SPFL]] Team of the Week.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Livingston v Dundee |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68039655 |access-date=2024-01-27 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Team of the Week {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/team-of-the-week-49737 |access-date=2024-01-31 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref>

On 14 February 2025, Sharp again signed a new two-year deal with Dundee, running until the summer of 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-14 |title=New deal for Sharp |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/new-deal-for-sharp/ |access-date=2025-02-14 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> On 23 October 2025, Sharp joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] on an emergency week-long loan following an injury to their first-choice keeper [[Cammy Gill]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DEE KEEPER SHARP JOINS ON EMERGENCY LOAN {{!}} Montrose Football Club |url=https://montrosefc.co.uk/2025/10/23/dee-keeper-sharp-joins-on-emergency-loan/ |access-date=2026-01-05 |website=montrosefc.co.uk}}</ref> Sharp made his debut for the ''Gable Endies'' two days later in a home league defeat to [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Montrose vs Cove Rangers: Scottish League One stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cly4e5l1gedt |access-date=2026-01-05 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 5 January 2026, Sharp returned to Montrose on loan following another injury to Gill and remained their main keeper until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-05 |title=Harry Sharp joins Montrose on loan |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/harry-sharp-joins-montrose-on-loan/ |access-date=2026-01-05 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> After an injury finished [[Jon McCracken]]'s season amid a minor goalkeeping crisis, Dundee received special dispensation from the [[Scottish FA|SFA]] in May to call Sharp back from his loan after Montrose's season ended for the ''Dee''<nowiki/>'s last 3 post-split fixtures.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-09 |title=Steven Pressley reveals 'cold, dark December' inspiration for Dundee's survival victory as he hails super sub impact in Livi win |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5488253/steven-pressley-inspiration-dundee-livingston-super-sub/ |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== International career ==
Sharp was selected for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad in May 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61507036 |title=Rangers' Alex Lowry one of five new call-ups by Scotland Under-21s |website=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2022 |access-date=19 May 2022}}</ref>

'''Brad Spencer''' (born 16 May 1996) is a Scottish professional footballer who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]. He is vice-captain of the club.

==Background==
Brad Spencer is the son of former [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] [[Forward (association football)|striker]] [[John Spencer (Scottish footballer)|John Spencer]].<ref name=killie17>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40981144|title=Kilmarnock sign Eamonn Brophy and Brad Spencer|date=18 August 2017|website=BBC Sport }}</ref> As a result of his father's career path, Brad was born in [[London]] and spent some of his childhood living in southern England and the United States.

==Career==
After spending his youth career with [[Houston Dynamo]], Spencer signed for Scottish top division side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in the summer of 2017<ref name=killie17/> but was released a year later without making a first team appearance. He moved down to [[Scottish League One]] club [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] where he made no great impact, but after switching to fellow third tier part-timers [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] in January 2019<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47017172 Arbroath and Raith Rovers suffer defeats at top of Scottish League One], BBC Sport, 26 January 2019</ref> he became an important member of the team which finished second and took part in the [[2018–19 Scottish Championship|Championship play-offs]], although they were eliminated by [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] (who also failed in their efforts to move up a level).<ref name=loons/>

Spencer then returned to full-time football when he signed for Raith a short time later,<ref name=loons>[https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/brad-spencer-leaves-loons-raith-rovers-965186 Brad Spencer leaves the Loons for Raith Rovers], Fife Today, 12 June 2019</ref> and having quickly agreed an extension to his initial one-year contract<ref>[https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/brad-spencer-thriving-raith-rovers-and-delighted-extend-contract-931377?amp Brad Spencer 'thriving' at Raith Rovers and delighted to extend contract], Fife Today, 17 October 2019</ref><ref>[https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish-league-1/1007206/raith-rovers-midfielder-brad-spencer-happy-to-heed-fatherly-advice-as-he-prepares-for-east-fife-clash/amp/ Raith Rovers midfielder Brad Spencer happy to heed fatherly advice as he prepares for East Fife clash], The Courier, 26 October 2019</ref> he went on to play a role in their [[2019–20 Scottish League One]] title win and promotion. After missing most of the pre-season with a knee injury,<ref>[https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/another-injury-blow-raith-rovers-2988642 Another injury blow for Raith Rovers], Fife Today, 1 October 2020</ref> his debut in the [[Scottish Championship]] (which was delayed and shortened by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]], in addition to the previous campaign being ended early) came in October 2020 when he came off the bench in the first half and provided an [[Assist (association football)|assist]] in a 5–2 win over [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>[https://www.raithrovers.net/45254/queen-of-the-south-5-2-raith-rovers.htm Table-topping Raith hit five], Raith Rovers FC, 24 October 2020</ref>

He joined [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in the summer of 2023, where he scored a penalty on the final day to complete an undefeated league winning campaign.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67910593 Falkirk: Brad Spencer, son of ex-Scotland striker John, driving Bairns' resurgence], Kenny Crawford, BBC Sport, 9 January 2024</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Crawford |first=Kenny |date=4 May 2024 |title=Falkirk's unbeaten season 'top' of McGlynn's career |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c80zyxw94qro |work=BBC Sport |pages=1}}</ref>

'''Kai Colin Fotheringham''' (born 18 April 2003) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. He made his senior debut for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in 2020 and has also spent time on loan with [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] and [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]].

==Club career==
Fotheringham joined [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] at youth level. In August 2020 he extended his contract with the club until 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fotheringham signs contract extension |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6570/FOTHERINGHAM-SIGNS-CONTRACT-EXTENSION.html |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=Dundee United Football Club |date=18 August 2020}}</ref> He made his senior debut in a 6-2 win against [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] in a [[Scottish League Cup]] match on 7 October 2020.<ref>{{Cite tweet |author=Dundee United F.C. |author-link=Dundee United F.C. |user=dundeeunitedfc |number= 1313956551728783361 |date=7 October 2020 |title=Hear from Stevie Frail and Kai Fotheringham after tonight's 6-2 win at Brechin City in the Betfred Cup |access-date=20 February 2021 }}</ref> His league debut was in a 5-1 [[Scottish Premiership]] defeat against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 27 January 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title='Siege mentality' helps St Mirren rout United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55728196 |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Fotheringham was loaned to [[Scottish League One|League One]] club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in March 2021<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2040094/dundee-united-youngsters-kai-fotheringham-and-lewis-neilson-join-falkirk-on-loan-until-the-end-of-the-season/ |title=Dundee United youngsters Kai Fotheringham and Lewis Neilson join Falkirk on loan until the end of the season |first=Calum |last=Woodger |date=12 March 2021 |accessdate=15 March 2021}}</ref> and made his debut for them against [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] on 20 March.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Banks |first1=Ben |title=Falkirk players 'a credit to themselves' in Montrose win says Lee Miller |url=https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/interview/falkirk-players-a-credit-to-themselves-in-montrose-win-says-lee-miller/ |access-date=24 March 2021 |work=Not The Old Firm |date=22 March 2021}}</ref> Three days later he scored a late winning goal in Falkirk's [[Scottish Cup]] tie against [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] after coming on as a substitute.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dunfermline join Hearts in cup exit |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56505295 |access-date=24 March 2021 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In July 2021, Fotheringham joined [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McCabe |first1=Paul |title=Raith Rovers take Dundee United youngster on loan |url=https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/raith-rovers-take-dundee-united-youngster-on-loan-3324836 |access-date=29 July 2021 |work=Fife Today |date=27 July 2021}}</ref> On 2 February 2022, Fotheringham joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] on loan for the remainder of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://coverangersfc.com/2022/02/02/kai-fotheringham-joins-on-loan/ |title=Kai Fotheringham joins on loan |publisher=Cove Rangers FC |date=2 February 2022 |accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref> He was then loaned to [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] in August 2022 but would be recalled six months later, continuing his development with the Dundee United first-team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7461/KAI-FOTHERINGHAM-JOINS-STIRLING-ALBION-ON-LOAN.html |title=KAI FOTHERINGHAM JOINS STIRLING ALBION ON LOAN |publisher=Dundee United FC |website=dundeeunitedfc.co.uk |date=26 August 2022 |accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=KAI FOTHERINGHAM RECALLED FROM STIRLING ALBION |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7699/KAI-FOTHERINGHAM-RECALLED-FROM-STIRLING-ALBION.html |access-date=2023-02-01 |website=Dundee United Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

On 25 August 2025, Fotheringham joined [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kai Fotheringham signs for Saints! {{!}} ST JOHNSTONE FC |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/kai-fotheringham-signs-for-saints/ |access-date=2025-09-01 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Fotheringham represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] level, playing against [[Australia men's national under-17 soccer team|Australia]] in 2019,<ref>{{cite web |title=Kai Fotheringham |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=299123&lid=17 |access-date=20 February 2021 |publisher=Scottish Football Association}}</ref> and made his debut at [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] level in November 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kai Fotheringham |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=299123&lid=5 |access-date=18 November 2023 |publisher=Scottish Football Association}}</ref>

'''Enes Alić''' (born 3 September 1999) is a Bosnian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|enes-alic_2}}</ref>

==Career==
On 30 January 2023, Alić joined [[Kisvárda FC|Kisvárda]] in Hungary.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Kisvárda FC|url=https://kisvardafc.hu/hir/fiatal-balhatvedet-szerzodtettunk/6109|title=Fiatal balhátvédet szerződtettünk|trans-title=We signed a young left-back|date=30 January 2023|access-date=14 March 2023|language=hu}}</ref> He was signed by Croatian club [[NK Varaždin (2012)|Varaždin]] on 31 August 2024.<ref>[https://www.nacional.hr/zadnji-dan-prijelaznog-roka-u-ligama-petice-gdje-ce-osimhen-baturina-blizu-fiorentine-hajduk-vraca-biuka/ ZADNJI DAN PRIJELAZNOG ROKA Ivan Perišić ide u Como, Baturina ostaje u Dinamu, Roko Šimić potpisao za Cardiff] at Nacional.hr</ref>

On 9 June 2025, Alić signed a two-year contract with [[Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian Premier League]] side [[FK Željezničar Sarajevo|Željezničar]].<ref>{{cite web|website=fkzeljeznicar.ba|url=https://fkzeljeznicar.ba/foto-enes-alic-novi-fudbaler-zeljeznicara/83579/|title=Enes Alić novi fudbaler Željezničara|date=9 June 2025|access-date=10 June 2025|language=bs}}</ref> He made his debut against [[FC Koper|Koper]] in a [[2025–26 UEFA Conference League qualifying#First qualifying round|2025–26 UEFA Conference League first qualifying round]] first leg on 10 July 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/nogomet/zeljeznicar-u-96-minuti-izbjegao-poraz-od-kopra-i-zadrzao-sanse-za-drugo-pretkolo/250710176|title=Željezničar u 96. minuti izbjegao poraz od Kopra i zadržao šanse za drugo pretkolo|date=10 July 2025|access-date=10 July 2025|language=bs|author=D.P.|publisher=Klix.ba}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 1–0 league victory away against [[HŠK Posušje|Posušje]] on 3 August 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportsport.ba/fudbal/wwin-liga-bih-2-kolo-posusje-zeljeznicar-izvjestaj/504257|title=Alić sjajno pogodio za prvu "tricu" Željezničara|date=3 August 2025|access-date=3 August 2025|language=bs|author=A.B.|publisher=sportsport.ba}}</ref> He signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in August 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/enes-alic-joins-the-saints/|title=Enes Alic joins the Saints!|date=24 August 2026|access-date=31 August 2026|website=perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk}}</ref>

'''Cheick Tiemoko Diabate''' (born 21 January 2002) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

==Career==
===Exeter City===
Diabate started his career at [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]] before a move to [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] in 2018. He first appeared in a matchday squad during Exeter's 2–0 away [[EFL Trophy]] group-stage victory over [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]] in October 2019,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Newport County vs. Exeter City |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/10/08/england/football-league-trophy/newport-county-afc/exeter-city-fc/3106522/ |publisher=Soccerway |date=8 October 2019 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> and then later that season enjoyed a brief loan spell with [[Buckland Athletic F.C.|Buckland Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Buckland Athletic on Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/OfficalBAFC/status/1221841068783808514 |publisher=[[Buckland Athletic F.C.]] |website=Twitter |date=27 January 2020 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> In a disrupted 2020–21 campaign, Diabate had loan spells at [[Bideford A.F.C.|Bideford]]<ref>{{Cite news |title=✍️ Loan deals: Cheick Diabate and Lewis Wilson join Bideford until January |url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2020/august/-loan-deals-cheick-diabate-and-lewis-wilson-join-bideford-until-january/ |publisher=[[Exeter City F.C.]] |date=4 August 2020 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> and [[Tiverton Town F.C.|Tiverton Town]]<ref>{{Cite news |title=✍️ Cheick Diabate joins Tiverton Town on loan |url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2020/october/diabate-loan/ |publisher=[[Exeter City F.C.]] |date=7 October 2020 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> before making his Exeter debut in November 2020, featuring for the final twenty-eight minutes of their EFL Trophy tie with [[West Bromwich Albion F.C. Reserves and Academy|West Bromwich Albion U23s]], which resulted in a 4–0 win for The Grecians.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Exeter City vs. West Bromwich Albion U21 |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2020/11/17/england/football-league-trophy/exeter-city-fc/west-bromwich-albion-under-21/3343246/ |publisher=Soccerway |date=17 November 2020 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref>

On 14 July 2021, Diabate joined [[Southern Football League|Southern League]] Premier Division South side, [[Truro City F.C.|Truro City]]<ref>{{Cite news |title=✍️ Cheick Diabate joins Truro on loan |url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2021/july/cheick-truro-loan/ |publisher=[[Exeter City F.C.]] |date=14 July 2021 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> and went onto make his debut during a 1–1 draw with [[Walton Casuals F.C.|Walton Casuals]] a month later.<ref name="Aylesbury">{{Cite news |title=Cheick Diabate Profile |url=http://www.aylesburyunitedfc.co.uk/players/cheick-diabate |publisher=[[Aylesbury United F.C.]] |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> He then scored his first career goal in a 4–1 away victory over [[Poole Town F.C.|Poole Town]] in October<ref name="Aylesbury"/> before eventually returning to Exeter two months later following an injury crisis at the [[Devon]]-based side.<ref>{{Cite news |title=💬 Cheick Diabate on his return to City |url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2021/december/cheick-loan-iv/ |publisher=[[Exeter City F.C.]] |date=21 December 2021 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> He made his league debut for the club just a week later in a 2–1 defeat to [[Sutton United F.C.|Sutton United]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Sutton United vs. Exeter City |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/01/01/england/league-two/sutton-united-fc/exeter-city-fc/3522827/ |publisher=Soccerway |date=1 January 2022 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> He went on to feature heavily in the second half of Exeter's season as they secured promotion to [[EFL League One|League One]]. Diabate was rewarded with a new two-year contract in June 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2022/june/diabate-new-contract/|title=✍️ Cheick Diabate seals new City contract|website=www.exetercityfc.co.uk|date=28 June 2022}}</ref>

On 30 August 2024, Diabate joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityafc.com/news/2024/august/30/diabate-arrives-on-deadline-day-/|title=DIABATE ARRIVES ON DEADLINE DAY|website=www.bradfordcityafc.com|date=30 August 2024|accessdate=30 August 2024}}</ref> He was recalled in January 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityafc.com/news/2025/january/06/diabat--returns-to-exeter/|title=DIABATÉ RETURNS TO EXETER|website=www.bradfordcityafc.com|date=6 January 2025|accessdate=7 January 2025}}</ref>

On 5 May 2025, Exeter announced the player would leave the club in June when his contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Exeter City Retained List 2025 {{!}} Exeter City F.C. |url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/retained25 |access-date=2025-05-13 |website=www.exetercityfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
On 7 July 2025, Diabate joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/cheick-diabate-signs-for-saints|title=Cheick Diabate signs for Saints!|website=www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk|date=7 July 2025|accessdate=7 July 2025}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Diabate's cousin [[Mory Koné]] is a former professional footballer, having played for [[ES Troyes AC|Troyes]], [[Le Mans FC|Le Mans]], and [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pilnick |first1=Brent |title=Cheick Diabate: Exeter City defender relishing first-team chances |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59994223 |access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref>

Diabate is a Muslim.<ref>{{cite news |last1=James |first1=Stuart |title=Cheick Diabate confident he can step into the Exeter City team |work=Devon Live|url=https://www.devonlive.com/sport/football/football-news/cheick-diabate-confident-can-step-6387204.amp |access-date=28 March 2023}}</ref>

In July 2019, Fink joined [[Borussia Dortmund]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bvb.de/News/Uebersicht/BVB-Nachwuchs-verpflichtet-Reyna-und-Fink|title=BVB-Nachwuchs verpflichtet Reyna und Fink|publisher=[[Borussia Dortmund]]|date=1 July 2019|accessdate=18 January 2022|language=German}} On 17 January 2022, Fink made his professional debut in a [[3. Liga]] match for [[Borussia Dortmund II]] against [[SV Waldhof Mannheim|Waldhof Mannheim]].{{cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2022/01/17/germany/3-liga/sv-waldhof-mannheim-07/borussia-dortmund-ii/3532824/|title=WALDHOF MANNHEIM VS. BORUSSIA DORTMUND II 1 - 3|website=Soccerway|date=17 January 2022|accessdate=18 January 2022}} ===FC Basel=== In August 2022, Fink signed a four-year contract with [[FC Basel]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcb.ch/aktuell/news/1-mannschaft/transfer-fink/|title= Bradley Fink Unterschreibt Bis 2026 Beim FCB|date=17 August 2022|website= FC Basel|language=de}} He joined Basel's first team for their [[2022–23 FC Basel season|2022–23 season]] under head coach [[Alexander Frei]] and made his debut in the [[Swiss Cup]] match on 21 August 2022. He scored his first goal for the club in the same game, as Basel won 5–0 against local amateur club FC Allschwil.{{cite web | first = | last = FC Basel 1893 | author-link = | date = 21 August 2022 | url = https://www.fcb.ch/matchcenter/startcenter/62c44a5afa02a201d68b51ff/2022-FC_Allschwil__FCB | title = 5:0 gegen den FC Allschwil – der FCB steht im Cup-1/16-Final | format = | work = 5:0 against FC Allschwil – FCB is in the Cup 1/16 finals | publisher = FC Basel 1893 AG | access-date = 2022-08-21}} Fink played his domestic league debut for the club in the away game in the [[Letzigrund]] on 28 August as Basel won 4–2 against [[FC Zürich|Zürich]].{{cite web | first = | last = FC Basel 1893 | author-link = | date = 28 August 2022 | url = https://www.fcb.ch/matchcenter/startcenter/62b02666e3be78190d362fd6/2022-FC_Zrich_-_FC_Basel_1893 | title = Der FCB bezwingt den FCZ auswärts mit 4:2 | format = | work = The FCB beats the FCZ 4-2 away from home | publisher = FC Basel 1893 AG | access-date = 2022-08-28}} He scored his first league goal for his new club in the home game in the [[St. Jakob-Park]] on 1 October. He was substituted in for [[Wouter Burger]] in the 83rd minute and scored the winning goal within one minute as Basel won 3–2 against [[FC St. Gallen|St. Gallen]], heading home a cross from [[Michael Lang (footballer, born 1991)|Michael Lang]].{{cite web | first = | last = FC Basel 1893 | author-link = | date = 1 October 2022| url = https://www.fcb.ch/matchcenter/startcenter/62b02666e3be78190d363002/2022-FC_Basel_1893_-_FC_StGallen_1879 | title = Fink köpft den FCB zum 3:2-Sieg über den FC St. Gallen | format = | work = Fink heads FCB to a 3-2 win over FC St. Gallen | publisher = FC Basel 1893 AG | access-date = 2021-11-16}} ====Loan to Grasshopper Club Zürich==== On 20 July 2023, he joined [[Swiss Super League]] rivals [[Grasshopper Club Zürich]] for a season long loan.{{cite web|publisher=[[Grasshopper Club Zürich]]|url=https://www.gcz.ch/en/news/article/1/bradley-fink-joins-gc-zurich-and-dominik-schmid-signs-for-fc-basel-1893/|title=Bradley Fink joins GC Zurich and Dominik Schmid signs for FC Basel 1893|date=20 July 2023|access-date=20 July 2023}} He made his debut in the first game of the season on 22 July 2023, coming on in the final minutes in the 1–3 home defeat to [[Servette FC]].{{cite web|publisher=Swiss Football League|url=https://sfl.ch/de/match-center/74ubxslty7u4t7z207mll1dzo|title=Grasshoppers – Servette|accessdate=26 July 2023}} On 12 August 2023, he received his first starting lineup nomination and scored his first goal for Grasshoppers just seven minutes into the game.{{cite web|title=Niederlage auf der Schützenwiese|url=https://www.gcz.ch/news/artikel/17/niederlage-auf-der-schuetzenwiese/|access-date=2023-08-20|website=gcz.ch|date=2023-08-12}} In their [[2023–24 Swiss Cup|Swiss Cup]] opening round match against [[SV Schaffhausen]] of the [[2. '''Jacob Murrell''' (born March 28, 2004) is an American professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].

Murrell previously played [[college soccer in the United States|college soccer]] for [[Georgetown Hoyas men's soccer|Georgetown University]], and high school soccer for the [[McDonogh School]], the latter of which he was named [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] for Boys' Soccer, a national recognition for the top boys high school soccer player in the United States.

== Career ==
=== Early career ===
Murrell was born and raised in [[Forest Hill, Maryland]] which is the northeastern part of the [[Baltimore metropolitan area]]. He played high school soccer for all four of his seasons at the [[McDonogh School]], a private school near [[Owings Mills, Maryland]]. Throughout his high school years, Murrell was used a versatile, utility player, playing multiple positions, before transitioning to forward his junior and senior years. Murrell played as a midfielder his freshman season and as a defender his sophomore year.<ref name="pressbox">{{cite web |last1=DuBose |first1=Brooks |title=After Historic McDonogh Soccer Season, Jacob Murrell Ready For Next Level At Georgetown |url=https://pressboxonline.com/2021/12/02/after-historic-mcdonogh-soccer-season-jacob-murrell-ready-for-next-level-at-georgetown/ |website=Pressbox Online |access-date=September 10, 2022 |date=December 2, 2021}}</ref> Murrell had a breakout season his senior year, scoring 41 goals and providing 20 assists in 24 games, helping McDonogh finish the season with a 21–3–0 record. There, he helped McDonogh reach the A Conference championship, where they lost to [[Calvert Hall College High School|Calvert Hall]] in the [[Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association|MIAA Conference A Championship]]. Unfortunately, Murrell's McDonogh side lost to Loyola Blakefield mid-season due to the heroic efforts of future veteran Jackson Graham.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Graham |first1=Glenn |title=No. 2 Calvert Hall boys soccer edges No. 1 McDonogh on Rich Monath's double-overtime goal to capture MIAA A title |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/11/07/no-2-calvert-hall-boys-soccer-edges-no-1-mcdonogh-on-rich-monaths-double-overtime-goal-to-capture-miaa-a-title/ |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |access-date=September 10, 2022 |date=November 7, 2021}}</ref>

In June 2022, Murrell was selected as the boys' soccer winner for the Gatorade National Player of the Year Award.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hindle |first1=Tom |title=Jacob Murrell Named Gatorade National POY |url=https://www.topdrawersoccer.com/club-soccer-articles/jacob-murrell-named-gatorade-national-poy_aid50927 |website=[[TopDrawerSoccer.com|TopDrawer Soccer]] |access-date=September 9, 2022 |date=June 21, 2022}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's soccer season]], Murrell committed to playing college soccer for Georgetown, turning down offers from [[Maryland Terrapins men's soccer|Maryland]], [[Penn Quakers men's soccer|Penn]], and [[American Eagles men's soccer|American]].<ref name="pressbox"/>

Murrell scored 10 goals in 10 matches for the Annapolis Blues in 2023, leading them to 2023 NPSL Mid-Atlantic Regular Season Champions. Murrell scored a 97th-minute equalizer vs the Alexandria Reds to send the  match to penalty kicks, where the Blues would win 4–2 in front of over 8,800 fans at Naval-Marine Corps Stadium in Annapolis.

=== Professional career ===
===D.C. United===
On December 19, 2023, Murrell was selected seventh overall in the [[2024 MLS SuperDraft]] by local MLS side, [[D.C. United]]. On January 5, 2024, he signed a contract with the club forgoing his final two years of collegiate eligibility.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Goff |first1=Steven |title=Jacob Murrell to sign with D.C. United, departing Georgetown early |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2024/01/05/jacob-murrell-dc-united-georgetown/ |newspaper=Washington Post |access-date=6 January 2024 |date=5 January 2024}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on May 4, 2024, in a 2–2 draw with the [[Philadelphia Union]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kallassy|first1=Sarah|title=Recap: D.C. United and Philadelphia Union play to a frustrating 2-2 draw|url=https://thedistrictpress.com/2024/05/04/recap-d-c-united-and-philadelphia-union-play-to-a-frustrating-2-2-draw/|work=The District Press|access-date=May 30, 2024|date=May 4, 2024|quote=Homegrown player Jacob Murrell netted his first goal in Black-and-Red to double D.C. United’s lead in the 33'...}}</ref>

People can sometimes knock the academy game and say it's not real football but definitely down south the standard is a different level." ===Falkirk=== On 11 August 2022, Hogarth returned to Scotland, joining [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on loan until 3 January 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2022/august/11/hogarth-joins-falkirk-on-loan/|title=HOGARTH JOINS FALKIRK ON LOAN |website=Nottingham Forest F.C.|date=11 August 2022|access-date=23 April 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812013056/https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2022/august/11/hogarth-joins-falkirk-on-loan/|archive-date=12 August 2022|url-status=live}} He made his debut for the club, starting the game, in a 3–1 win against [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] in the opening game of the season.{{cite news|title=Falkirk 3-1 Peterhead: Hosts dominate to pick up first win of the league campaign|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-3-1-peterhead-hosts-dominate-to-pick-up-first-win-of-the-league-campaign-3804871|website=The Falkirk Herald|date=13 August 2022|access-date=23 April 2024}} Since joining Falkirk, Hogarth became a first choice goalkeeper throughout his loan spell at the club.{{cite news|title=Mentality shift has impressed me most, says McGlynn|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/mentality-shift-has-impressed-me-most-says-mcglynn-3822114|website=The Falkirk Herald|date=28 August 2022|access-date=23 April 2024}}

'''Charlie Reilly''' (born 5 December 2001) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|winger]] or [[midfielder]] for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{soccerbase|116022|accessdate=24 April 2023}}</ref> He has previously played for [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]], as well as having been on loan with [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] and [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

== Youth career ==
Reilly joined the [[Hamilton Academical F.C. Reserves and Academy|Hamilton Academical Youth Academy]] at the age of 9 and would play at every age group in his nine years there.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2018-06-08 |title=Contract News {{!}} Charlie Reilly |url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/contract-news-charlie-reilly/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Hamilton Academical Website |language=en-GB}}</ref> He was a member of ''Accies''<nowiki/>' unbeaten Under-17 team which won their Elite Youth League during the [[2017–18 in Scottish football|2017–18 season]] and qualified them to the [[2018–19 UEFA Youth League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-05-13 |title=u17s win Elite Youth League |url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/u17s-win-elite-youth-league/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Hamilton Academical Website |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=McGilvray |first1=Andy |date=2018-06-09 |title=Hamilton Accies coach George Cairns says under-17s feat won't be repeated |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hamilton-accies-coach-george-cairns-12661104 |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

Reilly would play both games in their two-legged affair against Swiss side [[FC Basel]] which ended with a last-minute equaliser assisted by Reilly, followed by a famous win via [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Basel-Hamilton |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/match/2025586--basel-vs-hamilton/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Hamilton-Basel |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/match/2025602--hamilton-vs-basel/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-10-25 |title=Accies Win UEFA Youth League Thriller |url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/accies-win-uefa-youth-league-thriller/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Hamilton Academical Website |language=en-GB}}</ref> Reilly would also play both games in the following round, in which ''Accies'' lost to Danish side [[FC Midtjylland]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Midtjylland-Hamilton |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/match/2025617--midtjylland-vs-hamilton/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Hamilton-Midtjylland |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/match/2025625--hamilton-vs-midtjylland/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Senior career ==

=== Hamilton Academical ===
Shortly after winning the Elite Youth League, Reilly signed his first professional contract with [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] at the age of 16, penning a two-year deal.<ref name=":0" /> Reilly made three appearances in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] with their U20 team over the following two seasons, but never made an appearance for the senior team.

==== Airdrieonians (loan) ====
On 17 August 2019, Reilly joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] on loan until January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hamilton starlets join on loan |url=https://www.airdriefc.com/1920news/170819/Hamilton-starlets-join-on-loan |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=airdrie |language=en}}</ref> Reilly would make seven appearances while with the ''Diamonds'' before returning to his parent club in January 2020. Reilly left Hamilton Accies at the end of his contract in the summer of 2020.

=== Partick Thistle ===
On 1 October 2020, following a successful trial period, Reilly signed a one-year deal with [[Scottish League One]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Signing News: Charlie Reilly is a Jag |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-charlie-reilly-is-a-jag/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref> Reilly would make three appearances in total for the ''Jags'' that season, and was a part of the squad which won the Scottish League One in the [[2020–21 Scottish League One|2020–21 season]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Thistle clinch League 1 title {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/thistle-clinch-league-1-title |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Reilly left the club upon the expiry of his contract in the summer of 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Charlie Reilly leaves the Club |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/charlie-reilly-leaves-the-club/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

=== Albion Rovers ===
In the summer of 2021, Reilly joined [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kearney |first=Ben |date=2021-06-30 |title=Charlie Reilly and Max Wright join Albion Rovers! |url=https://albionroversfc.com/charlie-reilly-and-max-wright-join-albion-rovers/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Albion Rovers}}</ref> After making his debut for the ''Wee Rovers'' in a [[Scottish League Cup]] draw at home to [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], Reilly scored his first goal for the club and his first senior goal in the same competition away to his former club, [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Accies]]. He would tally 36 appearances and 7 goals in his first season at [[Cliftonhill]], following a shift from his [[Box-to-box|box-to-box midfielder]] role to further out wide as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Kearney |first=Ben |date=2022-07-08 |title=Charlie Reilly signs on for Season 22/23! |url=https://albionroversfc.com/charlie-reilly-signs-on-for-season-22-23/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Albion Rovers}}</ref> At the end of the season, Reilly signed another one-year deal with Rovers to stay the following season.<ref name=":1" />

Reilly would have a stand-out [[2022–23 Scottish League Two|2022–23 season]], scoring 24 goals and providing 19 assists over 39 games for Albion Rovers, and was awarded League Two's [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners#2022–23 season|player of the month]] both in November 2022<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=November award for Reilly {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/november-award-for-reilly |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> and in January 2023.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Reilly voted Player of Month {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/reilly-voted-player-of-month |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Despite immense speculation over his future in January<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |title=Dundee chase highly-rated goalscoring midfielder Charlie Reilly |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4101961/dundee-chase-highly-rated-goalscoring-midfielder-charlie-reilly/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> including having supposedly signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nicolson |first=Eric |title=EXCLUSIVE: Dundee agree deal to sign Albion Rovers goal-scoring sensation Charlie Reilly |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4330807/exclusive-charlie-reilly-dundee-sign-albion-rovers/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> Reilly remained with Rovers, with manager [[Brian Reid (footballer)|Brian Reid]] saying it would take "something exceptional" to encourage the relegation-threatened side to sell.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomson |first=Paul |date=2023-01-19 |title=Rovers star attracting interest from "plenty of clubs", says boss |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/albion-rovers-star-attracting-interest-28979654 |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> The success of Reilly's season was such that he was nominated for the [[PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year]] award, alongside [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] players [[Liel Abada]] and [[Matt O'Riley]], and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] player [[Malik Tillman]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |date=2023-05-10 |title=The 4 Young Player of the Year nominees from Celtic, Rangers and Albion Rovers |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/the-4-young-player-of-the-year-nominees-from-celtic-rangers-and-albion-rovers-4137020 |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=The Scotsman |language=en}}</ref> Reilly would also be nominated for and win [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year (lower leagues)|PFA Scotland's League Two Player of the Year award]].<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Thomson |first=Paul |date=2023-05-15 |title=Airdrie and Albion Rovers stars take top PFA Scotland prizes |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/airdrie-albion-rovers-stars-take-29982546 |access-date=2023-06-10 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 8 June 2023, after having trained full-time with the club during his prior season with Albion Rovers, Reilly officially signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-08 |title=Charlie Reilly signs |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/charlie-reilly-signs/ |access-date=2023-06-08 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Forward Reilly joins Dundee on two-year contract |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65846711 |access-date=2023-06-10}}</ref> After spending time out with injury, Reilly made his debut off the bench on 2 September in a league game away to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kucheriavyi nets late double in Dundee draw |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66625125 |access-date=2023-09-02}}</ref>

==== Arbroath (loan) ====
On 23 February 2024, After impressing in short stints for Dundee and fighting intermittent injury issues, Reilly joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on loan until the end of the season to get regular playing time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-23 |title=Dundee confirm Reilly loan |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cg3w4q4v5z3o |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-23 |title=Reilly joins Arbroath on loan |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/reilly-arbroath/ |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> He made his debut for the ''Red Lichties'' the following day off the bench in a league draw against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Arbroath v Inverness Caledonian Thistle |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68324493 |access-date=2024-02-24 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== Inverness Caledonian Thistle (loan) ====
On 1 October, after recovering from injuries through the summer and early in the season, Reilly joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on loan until January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-01 |title=Dundee midfielder Charlie Reilly joins ICT on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cvgxrqp2y09o |access-date=2024-10-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Media |first=ICTFC |date=2024-10-01 |title=Charlie Reilly joins ICTFC on loan |url=https://ictfc.com/charlie-reilly-joins-ictfc-on-loan/ |access-date=2024-10-02 |website=ICTFC |language=en-GB}}</ref> Reilly made his debut on 5 October in a league game away to his former loan club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arbroath vs Inverness CT: League One |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clyl6p7z7j3t |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Shortly after, Reilly picked up another hamstring injury which kept him out for the rest of 2024, and in January 2025 he returned to Dundee after recovering.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2024-10-16 |title=Dundee 'gutted' as injury woe strikes again for Charlie Reilly on loan at Inverness |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5103949/dundee-gutted-injury-woe-strikes-charlie-reilly-inverness/ |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2025-01-28 |title=Dundee get massive fitness boost with SEVEN new selection options as Joe Shaughnessy declared ready to return |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5171164/dundee-fitness-boost-seven-available-joe-shaughnessy/ |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== Return to Dundee ====
Reilly returned to the pitch for Dundee on 26 February 2025, notching an assist in an away league defeat to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Motherwell vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4gpzwy43p8t |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 12 June 2025, Reilly agreed a new one-year deal with Dundee for the [[2025–26 Dundee F.C. season|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-12 |title=New deal for Reilly |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/new-deal-reilly/ |access-date=2025-06-12 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Any hopes of avoiding more injury woes were dashed 15 minutes into the first friendly of the season, when a foul and awkward fall led to Reilly breaking his [[collarbone]], which required an operation that would keep him out for 6 to 12 weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2025-06-30 |title=Dundee hit by injury blow as length of Charlie Reilly's recovery period revealed |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5279913/dundee-injury-blow-charlie-reilly-recovery-period-revealed/ |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> He again returned to the pitch on 20 September as a substitute in a home league win over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], winning the game-sealing penalty.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee 3-2 Livingston: 97th-minute penalty earns Pressley's side first league win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cq5j48e2x58t |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 30 December, Reilly finally made his first start for Dundee and scored his first goal for the club in a home win over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee 2-1 Kilmarnock: Dundee take a significant step towards Scottish Premiership safety |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g51rq5lmjt |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 25 May 2026, Dundee announced that Reilly had signed a new deal for the [[2026–27 Dundee F.C. season|2026–27 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-25 |title=CHARLIE REILLY: BACK FOR 26/27! |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/reilly_2627/ |access-date=2026-05-25 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Reilly began his fourth season at Dens well, scoring 3 goals in their first 2 games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-14 |title=Why Charlie Reilly impact at Dundee is 'no surprise' as stunning brace kicks off five-star show in Annan rout |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5537986/charlie-reilly-impact-dundee-no-surprise-brace-five-annan/ |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Ethan James Laidlaw''' (born 2 January 2005) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].

Laidlaw is a product of the [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] [[Hibernian F.C. Reserves and Academy|academy]] and began his professional career with the club. He transferred to [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] in 2023, for whom he exclusively played [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#Relaunch (2016–present)|B team]] football until beginning his senior career with Falkirk in 2026. Laidlaw was capped by [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at youth level.

== Club career ==

=== Hibernian ===
A [[Forward (association football)|forward]], Laidlaw began his youth career at Longniddry Villa, under the coaching of his father.<ref name="Ritchie">{{Cite web |last=Ritchie |first=Cameron |date=1 August 2023 |title=Teenager Ethan Laidlaw signs for Brentford from Hibs |url=https://www.eastlothiancourier.com/sport/23694789.football-ethan-laidlaw-signs-brentford-hibs/ |access-date=11 August 2023 |website=East Lothian Courier }}</ref> He entered the [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] [[Hibernian F.C. Reserves and Academy|academy]] at age 8.<ref name="LeavesHibernian">{{Cite web |title=Ethan Laidlaw Joins Brentford |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2023/july/28/Ethan-Laidlaw-Joins-Brentford/ |date=28 July 2023 |website=Hibernian FC }}</ref> Laidlaw was a part of the U14 squad which won the 2018 [[Foyle Cup]] and progressed through the academy to sign his first professional contract in February 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ethan Laidlaw: Who is the young Hibs striker in the squad to face Rangers? |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/ethan-laidlaw-who-is-the-young-hibs-striker-in-the-squad-to-face-rangers-3196376 |date=11 April 2021 |website=Edinburgh News}}</ref><ref name="ProContract">{{Cite web |title=Ethan Laidlaw signs first professional contract |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2021/february/07/Ethan-Laidlaw-signs-first-professional-contract/ |access-date=28 July 2023 |website=Hibernian FC |date=8 February 2021}}</ref> He was an unused substitute during seven first team matches between April 2021 and January 2023.<ref name="Soccerway" /> Laidlaw made two [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] appearances for the B team and was a part of the 2021–22 [[SPFL Development League]]-winning squad,<ref name="Soccerway">{{Soccerway|id=697673|access-date=28 July 2023}}</ref> which subsequently entered the [[2022–23 UEFA Youth League]].<ref name="LeavesHibernian" /> He turned down a new contract and departed [[Easter Road]] when his existing contract expired at the end of the [[2022–23 Hibernian F.C. season|2022–23]] season.<ref name="Ritchie" />

=== Brentford ===
On 28 July 2023, Laidlaw transferred to the [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#Relaunch (2016–present)|B team]] at [[Premier League]] club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] and signed a two-year contract, with the option of a further year,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ethan Laidlaw departs for Brentford |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c1vk0w040kko| access-date=28 July 2023 |website=www.bbc.co.uk |date= 28 July 2023|language=en-gb}}</ref> for an undisclosed "six-figure" fee.<ref name="LeavesHibernian" /> Though he was not part of the [[2024–25 Professional U21 Development League#Professional Development League|2024–25]] [[Professional Development League|Professional U21 Development League]] Final-winning matchday squad,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bournemouth U21s 2 Brentford U21s 3: Yogane scores the winner to secure PDL title for young Bees |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-bournemouth-u21s-2-brentford-u21s-3-tony-yogane-scores-winner-to-secure-pdl-title |access-date=21 May 2025 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> Laidlaw received a winner's medal in recognition of his contribution earlier in the competition.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1925902504841109841 |user=BrentfordFCPDP |title=Ending season 2024/25 with a smile 😀 #BrentfordFC}}</ref> Often injured with "little niggles and bits that just take him out of his stride" during his first two seasons with the club,<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 April 2026 |title=Brentford’s next star? Laidlaw shines for U21s in front of Andrews |url=https://hounslowherald.com/brentfords-next-star-laidlaw-shines-for-us-in-front-of-andrews-p31487-381.htm |access-date=1 April 2026 |website=hounslowherald.com}}</ref> the option on Laidlaw's contract was taken up for the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brentford B and Academy squads, coaching staff and pre-season updates |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/academy-squads-brentford-b-coaching-staff-pre-season-updates-2025-26 |access-date=15 July 2025 |website=Brentford FC |language=en-gb}}</ref> He was an unused substitute during a first team [[pre-season friendly]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=QPR 0 Brentford 1: Captain Nathan Collins nets early goal in west London derby win |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/match-reports-qpr-0-brentford-1-pre-season-02-08-2025 |access-date=30 August 2025 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> Deployed centrally and [[Winger (association football)|out wide]],<ref name="Elder">{{Cite web |last=Elder |first=Matthew |date=9 June 2026 |title=Ex-Hibs ace who left for EPL returns to Scottish Premiership rival |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/ex-hibs-ace-who-left-for-epl-returns-to-scottish-premiership-rival-as-marvin-bartley-lands-new-head-coach-role-8665817 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ethan Laidlaw makes permanent switch to Falkirk |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ethan-laidlaw-falkirk-scottish-premiership |access-date=9 June 2026 |website=Brentford FC |language=en-gb}}</ref>

=== Falkirk ===
On 9 June 2026, Laidlaw transferred to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and signed a two-year contract, with the option of a further year,<ref name="Elder" /> for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 June 2026 |title=Ethan Laidlaw Is A Bairn! |url=https://falkirkfc.co.uk/ethan-laidlaw-is-a-bairn/ |access-date=9 June 2026 |website=Falkirk FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made five appearances early in the [[2026-27 Falkirk F.C. season|2026–27]] season,<ref name="Soccerbase2627" /> prior to suffering a [[rolled ankle]] in training on 5 August,<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 August 2026 |title=Falkirk eye advantage against Motherwell's busy schedule |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/falkirk-advantage-over-motherwell-8846323 |access-date=15 August 2026 |website=Falkirk Herald |language=en}}</ref> which required surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 August 2026 |title=Motherwell 0–0 Falkirk: What John McGlynn said |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c07rjjez5xxo |access-date=15 August 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== International career ==
Laidlaw was capped by Scotland at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|U17]], [[Scotland national under-18 football team|U18]] and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|U19]] levels.<ref name="Soccerway" /><ref>{{SFA player|id=293117}}</ref> He scored a [[Hat-trick (association football)|hat-trick]] on his international debut and was a part of the Scotland's [[2022 UEFA European Under-17 Championship|2022 UEFA European U17 Championship]] squad.<ref name="Soccerway" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=McPartlin |first=Patrick |date=5 September 2021 |title=Hibs forward Ethan Laidlaw scores hat-trick as Scotland under-17s edged out by Wales |work=Edinburgh News |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-kid-laidlaw-hits-debut-hat-trick-as-scotland-u17s-narrowly-lose-to-wales-3371589 |access-date=13 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=A Dream For Ethan Laidlaw |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/a-dream-for-ethan-laidlaw |access-date=28 July 2023 |website=Hibernian FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Scotland Under-17 squad named for Euros |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-17-squad-named-for-euros/ |access-date=28 July 2023 |website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Laidlaw is the son of former [[Scottish Football League|Scottish League]] footballer Steven Laidlaw and his brothers Keir and Josh also became footballers.<ref name="Ritchie" /><ref>{{Soccerbase|id=11657|name=Stevie Laidlaw}}</ref> He grew up in [[Port Seton]] and attended [[Preston Lodge High School]].<ref name="Ritchie" /> Laidlaw is a Hibernian supporter and served the club as a [[ball boy]].<ref name="ProContract" />

'''Ross Sinclair''' (born 7 May 2001) is a Scottish footballer who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[St. Mirren F.C.|St. Mirren]], on loan from {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/ross-sinclair/451669/|website=Soccerway|accessdate=9 August 2023|title=Ross Sinclair}}</ref>

==Early life==
Sinclair is from [[Scone, Scotland|Scone]] and attended [[Perth Academy]]. He joined the football academy at [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] when he was 12 years-old.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/dream-come-true-ross-sinclair-30074198.amp|website=Daily Record|accessdate=9 August 2023|title= "Dream come true": Ross Sinclair ready for more after making St Johnstone debut|date=25 May 2023}}</ref>

==Club career==
Sinclair played on loan at [[Brechin City F.C.]] and [[Cowdenbeath F.C.]] in the [[Scottish League Two]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cedl1n85wdjo.amp|title= Time for Goalkeeper Ross Sinclair to step up at St Johnstone?|website=BBC Sport|date=22 July 2022|accessdate=9 August 2023}}</ref> He signed a three-year professional contract with St Johnstone in May 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/ross-sinclair-signs-new-3-year-contract#:~:text=The%20Football%20Club%20is%20proud,until%20the%20summer%20of%202024.|accessdate=9 August 2023|website=perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk|title=Ross Sinclair Signs New 3 Year Contract|date=25 May 2021}}</ref> Sinclair joined [[Montrose F.C.]] in [[Scottish League One]] on loan in July 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/3538522/st-johnstone-and-scotland-under-21-keeper-ross-sinclair-joins-montrose-on-loan/|website=The Courier|accessdate=9 August 2023|title= St Johnstone and Scotland under-21 keeper Ross Sinclair joins Montrose on loan|first=Scott|last=Lorimer|date=July 28, 2022}}</ref>

Sinclair made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut for St Johnstone in May 2023 against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]]. He then played the next game against [[Livingston F.C.]] and kept a clean sheet. He received praise from on-loan goalkeeper [[Remi Matthews]] for his performances.<ref>{{cite web|title=yRemi Matthews believes Ross Sinclair is ready to be St Johnstone No.1|first=Eric|last=Nicolson|date=27 June 2023|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/4510843/remi-matthews-ross-sinclair-ready-st-johnstone-no-1/|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Sinclair started two matches for St Johnstone in the [[Scottish League Cup]] at the start of the 2023–24 season, but suffered a double break of his arm and an elbow dislocation in a behind closed doors friendly in August 2023, which had to be operated on.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/4621336/ross-sinclair-st-johnstone-arm-break/|website=The Courier|accessdate=9 August 2023|title= Ross Sinclair breaks arm in closed-doors match as St Johnstone search for Dimitar Mitov back-up|first=Eric|last=Nicolson|date=9 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23710192.st-johnstone-hunt-new-goalkeeper-shock-ross-sinclair-injury/|website=Herald Scotland|accessdate=9 August 2023|title=St Johnstone hunt for new goalkeeper after shock Ross Sinclair injury|first=Aidan|last=Smith|date=8 August 2023}}</ref> He returned at the start of the 2024–25 season, competing for the starting position with new signing [[Josh Rae]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/ckgwrnx0rr4o|website=BBC Sport |access-date=3 November 2024 |title=Sinclair makes long-awaited St Johnstone return|date=31 August 2024}}</ref>

Sinclair joined [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on an emergency loan in April 2026, making his debut for the club on 25 April 2026 against Livingston in the Premiership.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/6368-ross-sinclair-joins-on-seven-day-emergency-loan |title=ROSS SINCLAIR JOINS ON SEVEN-DAY EMERGENCY LOAN|website=st.mirren.com|accessdate=26 April 2026|date=23 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishnews.com/sport/soccer/livingston-battle-to-rare-victory-over-st-mirren-to-earn-lifeline-26VV6XI7DJNGVDEZM7AHKV5QSE/ |website=Irishnews.com|title=
Livingston battle to rare victory over St Mirren to earn lifeline|accessdate=26 April 2026|date=25 April 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Former St Johnstone goalkeeper [[Alan Mannus]] has praised Sinclair for his ability to play out from the back with his feet.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/3381105/alan-mannus-st-johnstone-scotland-ross-sinclair/|website=The Courier|title= Alan Mannus: St Johnstone and Scotland under-21 star Ross Sinclair 'has all the qualities' a top goalie needs|accessdate=9 August 2023|first=Eric|last=Nicolson|date=June 12, 2022}}</ref>

==International career==
Sinclair was called up to represent Scotland at under-21 level in September 2021.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=9 August 2023|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/ross-sinclairs-rise-scotland-u21-24917470.amp|website=Daily Record|title= Ross Sinclair's rise to Scotland U21 stage has been great watch for former coach|date=6 September 2021}}</ref> That month, he made his debut for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U-21]] team against [[Turkey national under-21 football team|Turkey U-21]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2021/09/07/europe/uefa-u21-championship-qualification/turkey-under-21/scotland-under-21/3455515/|title=SCOTLAND U21 VS. TURKEY U21 1-1|accessdate=9 August 2023|website=Soccerway|date=7 September 2021}}</ref>

'''Joseph Brooks Bevan''' (born 15 July 2004) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{soccerbase|167746}}</ref><ref>{{soccerway|joe-bevan/878386}}</ref>

==Career==
After playing for [[Kilsyth Athletic F.C.|Kilsyth Athletic]] and [[Camelon Juniors F.C.|Camelon Juniors]],<ref>{{cite tweet|user=KilsythAth
|number=1610378530071941120|title=Buzzing to see another former Kilsyth Athletic player make the step up to the SPFL as Joe Bevan gets his move to League 2 side Albion Rovers}} {{better source|date=January 2025}}</ref> Bevan signed for [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://albionroversfc.com/joe-bevan-joins-albion-rovers/|title=Joe Bevan joins Albion Rovers! – Albion Rovers|date=3 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.camelonjuniors.co.uk/joe-bevan-departs/|title=Joe Bevan Departs|date=3 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/albion-rovers-land-striker-camelon-28867392|title=Albion Rovers land Camelon Juniors striker after fending off other clubs|first=Paul|last=Thomson|date=3 January 2023|website=Daily Record}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/albion-rovers-new-boy-joe-29046804|title=Rovers new boy Joe Bevan: I'll bring energy and goals to help keep side in SPFL|first=Paul|last=Thomson|date=26 January 2023|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

After a trial with [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] in December 2023, he signed for the club in January 2024 on an 18-month contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://albionroversfc.com/joe-bevan-departs-albion-rovers-for-the-premier-league/|title=Joe Bevan departs Albion Rovers for the Premier League! – Albion Rovers|date=1 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68169100|title=Joe Bevan: Burnley take forward from Lowland League Albion Rovers for undisclosed fee|date=1 February 2024|work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/24090349.albion-rovers-striker-joe-bevan-earns-burnley-transfer/|title=Albion Rovers striker Joe Bevan earns Burnley transfer|date=1 February 2024|website=The National}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/former-camelon-juniors-star-joe-bevan-earns-premier-league-move-to-vincent-kompanys-burnley-4501194|title=Former Camelon Juniors star Joe Bevan earns Premier League move to Vincent Kompany's Burnley|date=1 February 2024|website=Falkirk Herald}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/24090349.albion-rovers-striker-joe-bevan-earns-burnley-transfer/|title=Albion Rovers striker Joe Bevan earns Burnley transfer|date=1 February 2024|website=Glasgow Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24090349.albion-rovers-striker-joe-bevan-earns-burnley-transfer/|title=Albion Rovers striker Joe Bevan earns Burnley transfer|date=1 February 2024|website=The Herald}}</ref>{{overcite|date=August 2026}}

In January 2025 he moved on loan to [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c07k5jp5mzno|title=Carlisle: Burnley striker Joseph Bevan joins on loan in club's 11th January signing|date=31 January 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsandstar.co.uk/sport/24900528.carlisle-united-sign-burnley-forward-joseph-bevan/|title=Carlisle United announce loan signing of Burnley forward Joseph Bevan|date=31 January 2025|website=News and Star}}</ref>

On 2 January 2026, Bevan joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-and-a-half year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-02 |title=Bevan joins the Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/bevanjoinsdee/ |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> On 25 January, Bevan made his debut for Dundee off the bench in a league game away to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership radio commentary & text updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cgqezldx58wt |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 11 July 2026, Bevan scored his first and Dundee's first goal of the season against [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], and scored his second goal three days later against [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Dundee come from behind to defeat Airdrie in League Cup opener |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c8x22xyy7qzt |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Charlie Reilly scores double as Dundee hit five at Annan Athletic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwydz2776zyt |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>
