'''Danny Schmidt''' (born 30 January 2003) is a German professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Wiesbaden]], Schmidt began his career at [[SV Neuhof]] in his home state of [[Hesse]]. In 2012, he moved to [[1. FSV Mainz 05]]. In April 2022, when he was the top scorer with 12 goals in 16 games for the under-19 team, he was promoted to the under-23 team in the [[Regionalliga]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Sextett rückt auf |url=https://www.sportausmainz.de/sport/artikel/Sextett_rueckt_auf-41818297476 |access-date=2 November 2024 |publisher=Sport aus Mainz |date=20 April 2022 |language=German}}</ref>

On 29 February 2024, Schmidt signed a deal to move to [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] of the [[2. Bundesliga]] for free once his contract expired on 1 July.<ref name=express>{{cite news |last1=Silz |first1=Viktoria |title=Fortuna holt Mainz-Talent – schon der zweite Sommer-Deal |url=https://www.express.de/sport/fussball/fortuna-duesseldorf/fortuna-duesseldorf-macht-transfer-offiziell-mainz-talent-kommt-748906 |access-date=2 November 2024 |work=Express |date=29 February 2024 |language=German}}</ref> He made his debut on 4 August as the season began with a 2–0 win away to [[SV Darmstadt 98]]; the ''[[Rheinische Post]]'' wrote that he had been signed as a prospect, but had earned his starting place by scoring in friendly matches over the summer. Manager [[Daniel Thioune]] played him as a [[Forward (association football)|centre forward]] and praised his performance, but doubted whether he would have started in his natural position due to the club's strength there already.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Oldenburg |first1=Leah |last2=Dinkelborg |first2=Tobias |title=So lobt Fortuna-Trainer Thioune Schmidt trotz schwierigen Debüts |url=https://rp-online.de/sport/fussball/fortuna/fortuna-duesseldorf-trainer-daniel-thioune-lobt-danny-schmidt-nach-seinem-profi-debuet_aid-117408359 |access-date=2 November 2024 |work=[[Rheinische Post]] |date=4 August 2024 |language=German}}</ref> In his third game on 25 August, he came on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] and scored a late winner in a 2–1 victory at [[SSV Ulm 1846]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Später Doppelschlag: Düsseldorfs Joker schocken Ulm |url=https://www.kicker.de/ulm-gegen-duesseldorf-2024-bundesliga-4937107/analyse |access-date=2 November 2024 |work=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |date=25 August 2024 |language=German}}</ref>

On 4 January 2026, Schmidt joined [[Rot-Weiss Essen]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 January 2026 |title="Heiß auf Rot-Weiss": Essen verstärkt sich vorn mit Fortune Schmidt |url=https://www.kicker.de/heiss-auf-rot-weiss-essen-verstaerkt-sich-vorn-mit-fortune-schmidt-1180621/artikel |access-date=5 January 2026|website=kicker |language=de}}</ref>

On 18 August 2026, Schmidt joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/clyj77xer8po|title=Saints sign German striker Schmidt on two-year deal|publisher=BBC|date=18 August 2026|accessdate=18 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Schmidt represented Germany at [[Germany national youth football team|under-17 level]].<ref name=express/>

'''Joseph Charles Gardner''' (born 6 June 2005) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Joe Gardner |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/joe-gardner/761617/ |accessdate=23 January 2025 |website=Soccerway}}</ref> Born in England, he has represented [[Football Association of Iceland|Ireland]] at a youth level.

==Club career==
While part of the [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] youth academy, which he joined in 2016,<ref name="auto">https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2026/july/28/gardner-completes-permanent-move-to-falkirk/</ref> he featured for the club's U21 side in the [[EFL Trophy]] in the 2023–24 and 2024–25 seasons, and scored against [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] in a 2–1 victory in September 2024.<ref>{{cite web|website=Football League World|date=22 January 2025|url=https://footballleagueworld.co.uk/walsall-lead-lincoln-city-in-race-for-nottingham-forest-joe-gardner/|title= Walsall in pole position over Lincoln City to seal Nottingham Forest transfer|first=Adam|last=Le Roux|accessdate=23 January 2025}}</ref>

He made his first-team debut for Nottingham Forest against [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] in the [[FA Cup]] on 7 February 2024.<ref> {{cite web|website=Soccerway|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2024/02/07/england/fa-cup/nottingham-forest-fc/bristol-city-fc/4312833/|date=7 February 2024|accessdate=23 January 2025|title=Nottingham Forest vs. Bristol City 1–1}}</ref> He later featured on the bench for [[Premier League]] matches without making his debut.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.footballinsider247.com/exclusive-walsall-lead-race-to-sign-nottingham-forest-star-joe-gardner/|title= Exclusive: Walsall lead race to sign Nottingham Forest star Joe Gardner|website=Football Insider|first=Pete|last=O'Rourke|date=22 January 2025|accessdate=23 January 2025}}</ref> He scored six goals in [[Premier League 2]] for Forest in the first half of the 2024–25 season.<ref name="contract"/>

On 31 January 2025, he signed a new contract with Nottingham Forest and joined [[EFL League One]] side [[Lincoln City F.C.|Lincoln City]] on a six-month loan.<ref name="contract">{{cite web|website=BBC Sport|title=Forest forward Gardner joins Lincoln on loan|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cgmyn4mwxmvo|date=31 January 2025}}</ref> Gardner made his debut coming off the bench against [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]] on 8 February 2025, where he received a straight red card 4 minutes into his debut.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lincoln City 1–1 Cambridge United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crlk41n7l6kt|access-date=8 February 2025|work=BBC Sport|date=8 February 2025}}</ref> He scored his first league goal for Lincoln against [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] on 4 March 2025, scoring the fourth goal to round off a 4–1 win.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lincoln City 4–1 Crawley Town|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4geev9yze5t|access-date=4 March 2025|work=BBC Sport|date=4 March 2025}}</ref> 

Gardner joined divisional rivals [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]] on 14 July 2025.<ref>{{cite web|website=mansfieldtown.net|title=Stags sign young Forest forward on loan|url =https://www.mansfieldtown.net/news/2025/july/14/stags-sign-young-forest-forward-on-loan/|date=14 July 2025}}</ref> He was one of three Nottingham Forest youth players to sign for Mansfield, alongside [[Kyle McAdam]] and [[Jamie McDonnell (footballer)|Jamie McDonnell]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c5y0880549go|title=Mansfield Town: Why Nottingham Forest's academy offers rich pickings for Stags|date=31 July 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his debut in the league game against [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe]] on 6 September 2025.<ref>{{cite web|website=nottinghamforest.co.uk|title=Nottingham Forest FC – Loan Watch|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2025/september/08/loan-watch---young-reds-in-action/|date=8 September 2025}}</ref> He scored his first goal in a 1–1 league draw against [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]] on 13 September 2025.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mansfield Town 1–1 Stevenage|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn76rzy3zkxt|access-date=13 September 2025|work=BBC Sport|date=13 September 2025}}</ref>

On 28 July 2026, Gardner signed with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on a three-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://falkirkfc.co.uk/joe-gardner-is-a-bairn/|title=JOE GARDNER IS A BAIRN|first=Paddy|last=Hainey|date=28 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="auto"/>

==International career==
In January 2023, he was called up by the [[Republic of Ireland national under-19 football team]] for a UK-based training camp ahead of their  UEFA European U19 Championship qualifiers the following month.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.fai.ie/latest/mu19-25-invited-to-uk-training-camp/|website=fai.ie|accessdate=21 April 2025|title= 25 invited to UK training camp|date=29 January 2023}}</ref> On 13 March 2025, Gardner received his first [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Republic of Ireland U21]] call up for their friendlies against [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] & [[Hungary national under-21 football team|Hungary U21]] in Spain.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fai.ie/latest/u21-squad-named-scotland-and-hungary-friendlies/|title=Ireland Under-21 squad named for Scotland and Hungary friendlies|website=fai.ie}}</ref> He made his debut for the side against [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] on 21 March, missing an 88th minute penalty in a 2–0 loss.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2025/0321/1503376-ireland-u21s-slump-to-defeat-against-scots-in-spain/|title=Ireland U21s slump to defeat against Scots in Spain|date=21 March 2025|publisher=Raidió Teilifís Éireann}}</ref>

'''Joseph Anthony Westley''' (born 18 October 2004) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]].

==Career==
Westley started his career in the youth team at [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], but following his release in the summer, he signed for [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] in August 2021 on a two-year scholarship.<ref name="Scholar">{{Cite web|url=https://www.burnleyfootballclub.com/content/westley-pens-first-professional-contract|title=WESTLEY PENS FIRST PROFESSIONAL CONTRACT|date=26 January 2023|website=Burley FC}}</ref> He initially struggled with injury problems but became a key part of [[Tony Philliskirk]]'s youth team towards the end of the 2021–22 season.<ref name="Scholar"/> In the 2022–23 season he was elected as youth team captain and after scoring 20 goals in 21 matches he was rewarded with his first professional contract in January 2023, signing a two-and-a-half year deal.<ref name="Scholar"/>

In January 2024 he went on his first loan to [[National League (division)|National League]] side [[AFC Fylde]] for the remainder of the season, with the ''Coasters'' in the relegation places.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://afcfylde.co.uk/fylde-welcome-westley/|title=Fylde Welcome Westley|date=23 January 2024|website=AFC Fylde}}</ref> He moved on loan to [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] in September 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rochdaleafc.co.uk/joe-westley-signs-on-loan/|title=Joe Westley Signs On Loan – Rochdale AFC|website=rochdaleafc.co.uk}}</ref> Westley signed on loan for [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] in January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c79dqn5d9vro|title=Joe Westley: Swindon Town sign Burnley striker on loan|date=23 January 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.swindonadvertiser.co.uk/sport/24880836.swindon-town-football-club-sign-joe-westley-burnley/|title=Forward joins Town on loan from Championship side Burnley|date=23 January 2025|website=Swindon Advertiser}}</ref> He scored on his debut for the club on 24 January 2025, coming off the bench to score the winning goal in a 2–1 away win at Newport County.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11750/13295136/newport-1-2-swindon-joe-westley-comes-off-bench-to-score-the-winner-on-robins-debut|title=Newport 1–2 Swindon: Joe Westley comes off bench to score the winner on Robins' debut|website=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bordercountiesadvertizer.co.uk/sport/national/24884275.on-loan-joe-westley-nets-debut-winner-swindon-fight-back-beat-newport/|title=On-loan Joe Westley nets debut winner as Swindon fight back to beat Newport|date=24 January 2025|website=Border Counties Advertizer}}</ref> Westley said he wanted to score more goals for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wiltshiretimes.co.uk/sport/24884430.joe-westley-ready-keep-decisive-swindon-town/|title=Joe Westley ready to keep being decisive for Swindon Town|date=25 January 2025|website=Wiltshire Times}}</ref>

On 5 August 2025, Westley signed a 3-year deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 August 2025 |title=Westley is a Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/westley-is-a-dee/ |access-date=5 August 2025 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> On 20 September, Westley scored his first goal for the club in a home league win over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee 3-2 Livingston: 97th-minute penalty earns Pressley's side first league win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cq5j48e2x58t |access-date=20 September 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His father is former player turned manager [[Graham Westley]].<ref name="auto"/>

Krauhaus is a product of the [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] and [[Bromley F.C.|Bromley]] [[Football academy|academies]] and made his senior breakthrough with the latter club. He transferred to Brentford in 2024. == Career == === Bromley === A [[midfielder]], Krauhaus began his youth career in the [[Charlton Athletic F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Charlton Athletic Academy]].{{Cite tweet |number=1749562114597863587 |user=TheSecretScout_ |title=TSS spoke with Ben Krauhaus who has signed for Brentford from Non-League Bromley. On being released at 16 by Charlton 🗣️ “After getting released from Charlton I went on trial at 5–6 different pro clubs and I didn’t get signed to any of them, looking back on it now it was probably the wrong decision to go on trial at all them clubs because I wasn’t in the right head space after just being released from the club I had spent 7 years at. After getting rejected by all them clubs I ended up at Bromley because it was local and I had a few friends who played for them.”}} Following his release, he joined the [[Bromley F.C.|Bromley]] [[Football academy|academy]].{{Cite web |date=24 November 2023 |title=Ben Krauhaus pens new deal |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/ben-krauhaus-pens-new-deal/ |access-date=13 April 2024 |website=Bromley Football Club |language=en}} He progressed through the academy to made his first team debut in an [[FA Trophy]] match in December 2021. Krauhaus spent much of 2022 on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] lower down the [[Non-League football|non-League]] [[English football league system|pyramid]] and signed his first professional contract during the 2022 off-season.{{Cite web |date=28 June 2022 |title=Under 23's sign First Year Contracts |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/first-team/under-23s-sign-first-year-contracts/ |access-date=13 April 2024 |website=Bromley Football Club |language=en}} He established himself as a regular member of the Bromley matchday squad during the second half of the [[2022–23 National League|2022–23]] [[National League (division)|National League]] season, with 11 appearances and one goal, predominantly as a substitute.{{Soccerway|id=686594|access-date=13 August 2024}} After signing a new one-year contract,{{Cite web |date=24 May 2023 |title=New deal for Ben Krauhaus! |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/new-deal-for-ben-krauhaus/ |access-date=13 April 2024 |website=Bromley Football Club |language=en}} Krauhaus established himself as a virtual ever-present starter during the [[2023–24 National League|2023–24]] season.{{Cite web |date=22 January 2024 |title=Ben Krauhaus signs for Premier League side Brentford |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/ben-krauhaus-signs-for-premier-league-side-brentford/ |access-date=13 April 2024 |website=Bromley Football Club |language=en}} He signed a new contract in November 2023 and was voted the club's December 2023 Player of the Month. Krauhaus transferred out of Bromley for a club-record undisclosed fee in January 2024, but he immediately returned to the club on loan until the end of the 2023–24 season. A [[metatarsal]] injury suffered during Bromley's National League play-off semi-final ruled Krauhaus out of the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|shoot-out]] victory over [[Solihull Moors F.C.|Solihull Moors]] in the final, which saw the club promoted to the [[English Football League|EFL]] for the first time in its history,{{Cite web |title=Ben Krauhaus: Ready for a New Chapter |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ben-krauhaus-interview-bromley |access-date=4 July 2024 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}} though he still received a promotion medal.{{Cite tweet |number=1787513520575111515 |user=KrauhausBen |title=HISTORY MAKERS🏆🏆 @bromleyfc}} In recognition of his performances during the 2023–24 season, Krauhaus received the club's Young Player of the Year award.{{Cite web |date=10 May 2024 |title=2023/24 Award Winners Confirmed at Broomfields Ceremony |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/2023-24-award-winners-confirmed-at-broomfields-ceremony/ |access-date=12 May 2024 |website=Bromley Football Club |language=en}} Krauhaus ended his spell at [[Hayes Lane]] with 64 appearances and 9 goals, with 51 appearances and 8 of those goals coming during the 2023–24 season. === Brentford === On 22 January 2024, Krauhaus transferred to the [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#Relaunch (2016%E2%80%93present)|B team]] at [[Premier League]] club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] and signed a {{frac|3|1|2}}-year contract, with the option of a further year, for an undisclosed fee.{{Cite web |title=Brentford B sign Ben Krauhaus |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ben-krauhaus-bromley-brentford-transfer |access-date=13 April 2024 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}} Following a loan away during the second half of the [[2023–24 Brentford F.C. season|2023–24]] season and recovering from a metatarsal injury, he returned to match play on 10 August 2024.{{Cite web |title=Brentford B 1 Chelsea U21s 5 |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-brentford-b-1-chelsea-u21s-5 |access-date=22 August |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ben-krauhaus-joins-bromley-on-loan-transfer |access-date=16 July 2025 |website=Brentford FC |language=en-gb}}{{Cite web '''Deniss Meļņiks''' (born 7 September 2002) is a Latvian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] or [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and the [[Latvia national football team|Latvia national team]].

==Club career==
As a youth player, Meļņiks joined the [[youth academy]] of Latvian side [[Riga FC|Riga]]. Following his stint there, he joined the youth academy of Italian [[Serie A]] side [[Torino FC|Torino]] in 2019. 

Ahead of the [[2021 Latvian Higher League|2021 season]], he signed for Latvian side [[FK Spartaks Jūrmala|Spartaks]], where he made thirty-eight league appearances and scored zero goals. Subsequently, he signed for Latvian side [[FK Auda|Auda]] in 2023, helping the club win the [[2025 Latvian Football Cup]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|deniss-melniks}}</ref>

==International career==
Meļņiks is a Latvia international. During September and October 2023 and March 2024 he played for the [[Latvia national under-21 football team]] for [[2025 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportacentrs.com/futbols/latvijas_izlase/09092023-melniks_un_basovs_priecigi_par_italijas_n|title=Prieks par Itālijas noturēšanu, Meļņiks pāreju uz "Torino" atzīst par pāragru|trans-title=Happy to have retained Italy, Melniks considers the move to Torino too early|language=lv|publisher=Sportacentrs.com|date=9 September 2023|access-date=26 November 2025}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Meļņiks plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] or [[midfielder]]. Latvian news website ''Baltic Football News'' wrote in 2024 that he "has showcased his versatility and defensive prowess".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://balticfootballnews.com/deniss-melniks-extends-contract-with-fk-auda/|title=Deniss Meļņiks extends contract with FK Auda|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=Baltic Football News|date=16 December 2024|access-date=26 November 2025}}</ref>

'''Josh Fowler''' (born 14 November 2001) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a striker [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

==Career==
During his time at [[Beith Juniors F.C.|Beith Juniors]], Fowler had trials with [[Scottish Premiership]] clubs [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] but wasn't signed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ardrossanherald.com/sport/23615930.beith-juniors-striker-josh-fowler-spotted-training-motherwell/|title=Beith Juniors: Striker Josh Fowler spotted training with Motherwell |website=ardrossanherald.com |date=27 June 2023 |access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23660346.derek-mcinnes-opens-josh-fowler-kilmarnock-trial/|title=Derek McInnes opens up on Josh Fowler Kilmarnock trial |website=heraldscotland.com |date=18 July 2023 |access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref> 

After playing in both Australia and Dubai, Fowler signed with [[Scotland|Scottish ]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] in June 2025.<ref name="dailyrecord">{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/josh-fowler-reveals-swapped-dubai-35897133.amp|title=Why swapping Dubai for Queen's Park can help goal machine Josh Fowler realise a dream|website=Daily Record|access-date=22 December 2025}}</ref><ref name="queensparkfc">{{cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/josh-fowler-joins-queens-park-dubai-city-beith-juniors/|title=Josh Fowler joins Queen's Park from Dubai City {{pipe}} Queen's Park Football Club|website=queensparkfc.co.uk|access-date=22 December 2025}}</ref><ref name="ardrossanherald">{{cite web|url=https://www.ardrossanherald.com/sport/25244002.former-beith-juniors-striker-josh-fowler-joins-queens-park/|title=Former Beith Juniors striker Josh Fowler joins Queen's Park {{pipe}} Ardrossan and Saltcoats Herald|website=ardrossanherald.com|access-date=22 December 2025}}</ref>

Fowler scored on his Queen's Park debut in a 2–1 away loss to The Spartans in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stages.<ref name="co.uk">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c9qxeex9dwzt|title=Spartans vs Queen's Park: Scottish League Cup stats & head-to-head, BBC Sport - BBC Sport|website=bbc.co.uk|access-date=22 December 2025}}</ref> Fowler scored his first league goal for Queen's Park in a 3–1 away defeat to Arbroath.<ref name="co.uk2">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ckgy8k8p6xzt|title=Queen's Park 1-3 Arbroath: Visitors secure first win since Scottish Championship return - BBC Sport|website=bbc.co.uk|access-date=22 December 2025}}</ref>

On 29 January 2026, Fowler signed with fellow [[Scottish Championship]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a two and a half year deal, for an undisclosed fee.<ref> https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/josh-fowler-signs-for-saints/</ref>

'''Liam Henderson''' (born 23 August 1996) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].

Starting in the [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] Academy in 2014, Henderson was released in 2016<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 1, 2016 |title=Hearts announce release of six out of contract players |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/14528619.hearts-announce-release-six-contract-players/ |first=Alasdair |last=Mackenzie |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=The Herald |language=en}}</ref> and subsequently played for Falkirk, [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]], [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]], [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] and [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] before returning to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in 2022.

==Club career==

===Heart of Midlothian===
Henderson started his career at Heart of Midlothian, making his one and only first team appearance for the club in a 4-1 defeat to Livingston in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup|Challenge Cup]] in August 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Livingston 4-1 Heart of Midlothian - London Hearts |url=https://londonhearts.com/scores//games/201408201.html |access-date=2026-02-21 |website=londonhearts.com}}</ref> 

===Falkirk===
Henderson signed for Falkirk following his release from Hearts in 2016,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falkirk add Kidd to squad {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/falkirk-snap-up-defender-kidd |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> failing to make an appearance in two seasons at the club.

===Edinburgh City===
Following a loan to Cowdenbeath, Henderson joined Edinburgh City on loan in the 2017–18 season, but soon moved to Australia to join Stirling Macedonia. However, his spell in Australia was brief and he returned to Edinburgh City on a permanent basis in August 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2018 |title=Liam Henderson rejoins City after returning from Australia |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/liam-henderson-rejoins-city-after-returning-from-australia-269085 |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=Edinburgh News |language=en}}</ref> Playing for three seasons in [[Scottish League Two]] and being on the losing side in two sets of [[Scottish League One]] play-off games, Henderson left the club at the end of the 2020–21 season.

===Arbroath===
[[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] won the race for Henderson's signature for the 2021-22 Season,<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 30, 2021 |title=Liam Henderson |url=https://arbroathfc.co.uk/liam-henderson/ |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=Arbroath FC |language=en}}</ref> with Henderson playing 25 times, the team finishing second and participating in the [[Scottish Premiership]] play-offs. Ultimately, the team were beaten and Henderson left the club at the end of the season.

===Return to Falkirk===
Henderson returned to Falkirk as [[John McGlynn (Scottish footballer)|John McGlynn]]'s first signing at the club for the [[2022–23 Scottish League One]] season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ouakli |first=Adam |date=May 25, 2022 |title=LIAM HENDERSON IS A BAIRN! - Falkirk Football Club |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2022/05/25/liam-henderson-is-a-bairn/ |access-date=2025-12-31 |language=en-US}}</ref> In [[2023–24 Falkirk F.C. season|2023–24]], Henderson was part of the "invincible" squad that went a whole [[Scottish League One]] season unbeaten, playing himself into the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#2023–24|PFA Scotland League One Team of the Year]] alongside nine of his Falkirk team-mates. Henderson then went on to achieve promotion from the [[Scottish Championship]] the following season, as Falkirk became Back-to-Back Champions. While also earning another [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#2024–25|PFA Scotland Team of the Year]] nomination, the player celebrated by signing a two-year contract extension, keeping him at the club until 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacLeod |first=Andrew |date=June 20, 2025 |title=LIAM HENDERSON EXTENDS CONTRACT WITH FALKIRK - Falkirk Football Club |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2025/06/20/liam-henderson-extends-contract-with-falkirk/ |access-date=2025-12-31 |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Leon McCann''' (born 16 March 2000) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender_(association_football)#Full-back|full back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].

Having come through the [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] youth system, McCann joined [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in 2019 before moving to Falkirk in 2021. He was part of both their [[Scottish League One|League One]]-winning "Invincibles" team in [[2023–24 Falkirk F.C. season|2023–24]] and their [[Scottish Championship]]-winning team in [[2024–25 Falkirk F.C. season|2024–25]]. 

==Club career==
===Hamilton Academical===
McCann started off in the pro-youth system with [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]]  aged 13, whilst attending [[Braidhurst High School]] in neighbouring [[Motherwell]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 September 2020 |title=Hot Prospect #6: Leon McCann – Youth Football Scotland |url=https://www.youthfootballscotland.co.uk/hot-prospect-6-leon-mccann/ |access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref> He was captain when the ''Accies'' under-19s played in the [[2018–19 UEFA Youth League]] and made four appearances across three seasons in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] for the under-20 side, but did not make a senior appearance for their first team.

===Airdrieonians===
Originally signing on a 5-month loan deal from Hamilton in August 2019, McCann signed an 18-month deal with [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in early January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leon is a Diamond |url=https://www.airdriefc.com/1920news/080120/leon-is-a-diamond |date=8 January 2020 |access-date=2 January 2026 |website=Airdrieonians FC}}</ref> He departed Airdrie in 2021 following the expiration of his contract at the club.<ref name="Leon-signs-Falkirk">{{Cite web |last=Robertson |first=Euan |date=19 June 2021 |title=Falkirk blew me away so I rejected other clubs, admits ex-Airdrie star McCann |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/falkirk-blew-away-rejected-clubs-24334941 |access-date= 2 January 2026 |website=Daily Record}}</ref> 

===Falkirk===
[[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] won the race for McCann's signature in August 2021, offering the full-back a 3-year deal.<ref name="Leon-signs-Falkirk" /> He was part of Falkirk's [[2023–24 Falkirk F.C. season|2023–24]] "Invincible" League One-winning side, earning a two-year contract extension in February 2023, keeping him at the club until 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ouakli |first=Adam |date=23 February 2024 |title=LEON MCCANN SIGNS TWO YEAR CONTRACT EXTENSION | website=Falkirk FC |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/02/23/leon-mccann-signs-two-year-contract-extension/ |access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref> McCann then went on to be part of Falkirk's "Back to Back" [[2024–25 Scottish Championship]]+winning side.

'''Finn Yeats''' (born 19 April 2004) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Falkirk}} club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].

Having come through the [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] youth system, Yeats was released in May 2022.<ref name="Left-AFC">{{Cite web |title=Aberdeen FC - Development Squad Player Departures |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2022/05/20/development-squad-player-departures/ |access-date=5 January 2026 |website=Aberdeen FC |language=en}}</ref> After impressing on trial at [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], he was brought in to trial at Falkirk, impressing manager [[John_McGlynn_(Scottish_footballer)|John McGlynn]] enough to earn a two-year deal.<ref name="joins-FFC">{{Cite web |last=Ouakli |first=Adam |date=4 July 2022 |title=FINN YEATS SIGNS FOR FALKIRK - Falkirk Football Club |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2022/07/04/finn-yeats-signs-for-falkirk/ |access-date=5 January 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Aberdeen===
Yeats came through Aberdeen's youth system and spent a season on loan at [[Highland_Football_League|Highland League]] club [[Keith F.C.|Keith]] before being released in May 2022.<ref name="Left-AFC" /><ref name="joins-FFC" />

===Falkirk===
[[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] snapped up Yeats after he impressed on trial in July 2022 earning a two-year contract with the then League One club.<ref name="joins-FFC"></ref> Despite being a midfielder, Yeats was deployed as an emergency [[Defender_(association_football)#Full-back|Right-Back]] during Falkirk's [[2022-23 Falkirk F.C. season|2022-23]] & [[2023-24 Falkirk F.C. season|2023-24]] [[Scottish League One]] campaigns, earning a place in the 2023-24 [[PFA_Scotland_Team_of_the_Year#League_One_9|PFA Scotland Team of the Year]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=x.com |url=https://x.com/PFAScotland/status/1781360026512204019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203045319/https://x.com/PFAScotland/status/1781360026512204019 |archive-date=3 December 2024 |access-date=5 January 2026 |website=X (formerly Twitter)}}</ref><ref name="contract-extension">{{Cite web |last=MacLeod |first=Andrew |date=3 May 2024 |title=FINN YEATS SIGNS CONTRACT EXTENSION - Falkirk Football Club |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/05/03/finn-yeats-signs-contract-extension/ |access-date=5 January 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref> Yeats was rewarded with a two-year deal in May 2024, keeping him at the club until 2026.<ref name="contract-extension" /> In January 2026, Yeats scored his first [[Scottish Premiership]] goal for the club in a match against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirrren]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 January 2026 |title=Contender for Premiership goal of the season scored by former Highland League star |url=https://www.northern-scot.co.uk/sport/contender-for-premiership-goal-of-the-season-scored-by-forme-424333/ |access-date=16 January 2026 |website=Northern Scot |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal==
Yeats is the son of former [[Keith F.C.|Keith]], [[Huntly F.C.|Huntly]], [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] and [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] player, Craig Yeats.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 January 2026 |title=Contender for Premiership goal of the season scored by former Highland League star |url=https://www.northern-scot.co.uk/sport/contender-for-premiership-goal-of-the-season-scored-by-forme-424333/ |access-date=25 January 2026 |website=Northern Scot |language=en}}</ref> His uncle is former Scottish international [[Warren Cummings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aberdeen FC - AFC YOUTH ACADEMY {{!}} THE CLASS OF 2020 |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2020/09/02/afc-youth-academy-the-class-of-2020/ |access-date=25 January 2026 |website=Aberdeen FC |language=en}}</ref>

'''Žan Bešir''' (born 17 October 2000) is a Slovenian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref name=":0">{{Soccerway|new_id=besir-zan/CUVgQJ7m}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Koper and loans ===
Bešir made his senior debut for [[FC Koper]] on 18 September 2019 in a [[Slovenian Cup]] match away to [[NK Maribor]], where he scored both a goal and an [[own goal]] as he helped seal an upset victory for the then [[Slovenian Second League]] side.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-09-18 |title=KOP 3-2 MAR |url=https://www.soccerway.com/match/koper-vP5HUcK5/maribor-6ycYQFJU/?mid=6HPbG5dN |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=soccerway.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-09-18 |title=Koper v pokalu izločil Maribor |url=https://maribor24.si/sport/koper-v-pokalu-izlocil-maribor/?pv=7c9e035c-e2e6-41f7-9eb1-d87620d9ab0d |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=maribor24.si |language=sl}}</ref> While with Koper, Bešir became a regular substitute player during their [[2021–22 Slovenian PrvaLiga|2021–22 title race]] which they narrowly lost to Maribor while later lifting [[Slovenian Cup]] that season against [[NK Bravo]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Izjemne poteze Kotnika in Colleyja in Koper dviga pokal |url=https://siol.net/sportal/prva-liga/pokal-slovenije-finale-koper-slavil-bravo-znk-olimpija-mandaric-579161 |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=siol.net |language=sl}}</ref> Bešir also went on several loans while at Koper, playing for [[NK Jadran Dekani]] in the Second League and for [[ND Gorica]] and [[NK Tabor Sežana]] in the [[Slovenian PrvaLiga]].<ref name=":0" />

=== Primorje and Nafta ===
In July 2023, Bešir signed for [[Slovenian Second League]] club [[ND Primorje]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-16 |title=Žan Bešir bo v sezoni 2023/24 igral v 2. SNL: Nekdanji mladi reprezentant Slovenije se dokazuje v dresu ajdovskega Primorja - Planet Nogomet |url=https://planetnogomet.si/novice/primorje-okrepitev-koper-zan-besir/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |language=sl-SI}}</ref> In January 2024, despite having started well for his new team, he was sent on loan to Primorje's promotion rivals [[NK Nafta 1903]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-11 |title=Žan Bešir bo zamenjal barve v bitki za napredovanje v Prvo ligo Telemach: Primorje ostalo brez pomembnega aduta, ki odhaja v Lendavo - Planet Nogomet |url=https://planetnogomet.si/novice/zan-besir-prestop-primorje-nafta/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |language=sl-SI}}</ref> After PrvaLiga club [[NK Rogaška]] failed to obtain a license, Bešir enjoyed two promotions in one season with Nafta getting automatically promoted alongside his parent club, Primorje.<ref>{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2024-05-23 |title=Nafta 1903 se resno spogleduje s prvo državno nogometno ligo, Rogaška ostala brez licence, kvalifikacij ne bo |url=https://lendavainfo.com/nafta-1903-se-resno-spogleduje-s-prvo-drzavno-nogometno-ligo-rogaska-ostala-brez-licence-kvalifikacij-ne-bo/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=Lendavainfo.com |language=sl-SI}}</ref>

Returning to Primorje in the top flight, Bešir made headlines for scoring against his previous loan team, Nafta, in October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-27 |title=Član Primorja Žan Bešir svojemu bivšemu klubu preprečil krvavo potrebno zmago: "K sreči izkoristili priložnost, na katero smo čakali" - Planet Nogomet |url=https://planetnogomet.si/novice/zan-besir-gol-primorje-nafta-izjave/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |language=sl-SI}}</ref> Bešir followed this up with a great November, culminating in being named as the PrvaLiga Player of the Month.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Žan Bešir je v Primorju razvil svoj potencial: Novembra je bil igralec meseca v Prvi Ligi Telemach - Novica - Nogomania |url=https://www.nogomania.com/Novica/Zan-Besir-je-v-Primorju-razvil-svoj-potencial-Novembra-je-bil-igralec-meseca-v-Prvi-Ligi-Telemach |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=www.nogomania.com}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 8 July 2026, after attending a pre-season trip to [[Hungary]] with the club, Bešir signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] with an option of another year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-07 |title=Zan Besir becomes third summer signing |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/zan-besir-becomes-third-summer-signing/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-07 |title=Dundee snap up Zan Besir as third summer signing - were Dundee United in for the Slovenian star? |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5531631/dundee-snap-up-zan-besir-dundee-united/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> Bešir made his debut for the ''Dark Blues'' on 14 July in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage win away to [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Charlie Reilly scores double as Dundee hit five at Annan Athletic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwydz2776zyt |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== International ===
On 12 November 2021, Bešir made his debut for the [[Slovenia national under-21 football team]], coming on as a substitute in a [[2023 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification|2023 UEFA Euro qualifier]] victory over [[Albania national under-21 football team|Albania U21]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 November 2021 |title=SLO 3-0 ALB |url=https://www.soccerway.com/match/albania-rgyIK1Vt/slovenia-r9183Ek1/?mid=CUICnVlQ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=soccerway.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Connor John Allan''' (born 10 January 2004) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a defender for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].

==Club career==
===Rangers===
Allan signed his first professional contract with Rangers in June 2020, after impressing in the [[Alkass International Cup|Alkass Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/9-rangers-academy-stars-sign-18363597 |title=9 Rangers academy stars sign first professional deals|website=glasgowlive.co.uk}}</ref>

On 9 October 2022, after impressing for the B team as well as playing every minute in the [[2022–23 UEFA Youth League group stage|UEFA Youth League]]; Allan signed a new contract at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]] that committed his future at the club until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/connor-allan-signs-new-contract-until-2025/3FeF9wWRr8tDlpBqo3cgcK |title=Connor Allan Signs New Contract Until 2025|website=rangers.co.uk}}</ref>

A few days after signing his new deal with Rangers, Allan was named on the first team bench for two UEFA Champions League [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] matches against [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]],<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2035705--napoli-vs-rangers/ |title=Napoli 3–0 Rangers|website=uefa.com}}</ref> and [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] respectively.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2035722--rangers-vs-ajax/ |title=Rangers 1–3 Ajax|website=uefa.com}}</ref>

====Kelty Hearts (loan)====
On 20 September 2024, Allan joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/connor-allan-joins-kelty-hearts-on-loan/7ApoQr72UNcrs59f5EJ01c |title=Connor Allan Joins Kelty Hearts On Loan|website=rangers.co.uk}}</ref>

Allan scored his first senior goal in a 2–0 home win against Annan Athletic.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Match Report {{!}} Annan Athletic 0-2 Kelty Hearts | url=https://keltyhearts.co.uk/mr-annan-0-2-kelty-18-11-24/ | access-date=2026-08-30 | website=www.keltyhearts.co.uk}}</ref> He featured 16 times in the league, scoring once before returning to Rangers.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c04n3114dlwo |title=Lovelace and Allan leave Rangers
|website=bbc.co.uk}}</ref>

===Falkirk===
On 3 February 2025, Allan signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] for an undisclosed fee — signing a two-and-a-half-year deal and was immediately loaned back to Kelty Hearts until the [[2024–25 Scottish League One|end of the season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://falkirkfc.co.uk/bairns-sign-connor-allan/ |title=BAIRNS SIGN CONNOR ALLAN|website=falkirkfc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.centralfifetimes.com/sport/24908200.connor-allan-joins-falkirk-rangers-returns-kelty-loan/ |title=Connor Allan joins Falkirk from Rangers but returns to Kelty on loan|website=centralfifetimes.com}}</ref> He returned to Falkirk on 9 May 2025, following the conclusion of the loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://keltyhearts.co.uk/loanees-move-on-9-5-25/|title=2024/25 Loanees Move On|website=keltyhearts.co.uk.co.uk}}</ref>

On 12 July, Allan made his debut for ''The Bairns'' during a 7–0 win against [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] in the [[2025–26 Scottish League Cup group stage|Scottish League Cup group stage]] coming on as a 67th minute substitute for [[Scott Arfield]] at [[Glebe Park, Brechin|Glebe Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cly8dd8x2rlt |title=Brechin City 0–7 Falkirk
|website=bbc.co.uk}}</ref> During the [[2025–26 Falkirk F.C. season|2025–26 season]], Allan went onto make 32 appearances across all competitions, scoring once.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=141563&season_id=158 |title=Connor Allan|website=soccerbase.com}}</ref>

==International career==

Allan has been capped at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scotland U16]], [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19]], [[Scotland national under-20 football team|Scotland U20]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] level.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/falkirk-new-boy-connor-allan-included-in-scotland-u20-squad-5122810 |title=Falkirk new boy and former loanees help make up Scotland under-20s squad for Slovakia friendly|website=falkirkherald.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/connor-allan-rewarded-for-falkirk-form-with-scotland-under-21-selection-5388583 |title=Connor Allan rewarded for Falkirk form in Scottish Premiership with Scotland Under-21 selection|website=falkirkherald.co.uk}}</ref>
